title: GP
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking an enthusiastic Salaried GP to join our friendly, community-focused practice. The role involves delivering high-quality, patient-centred care, including routine consultations, management of acute and chronic conditions, and preventative healthcare.

You will work as part of a supportive multidisciplinary team and contribute to the continued development of practice services. Opportunities to develop clinical interests, participate in teaching, and engage in quality improvement are encouraged.

We offer a positive working environment with a strong emphasis on teamwork, professional development, and work-life balance, with flexibility considered..

  • Provide General Medical Services in accordance with the GMS contract

  • Undertake surgery consultations, telephone and online consultations

  • Diagnose and manage patients presenting with acute and chronic conditions

  • Prescribe safely and appropriately in line with practice and national guidelines

  • Process and action laboratory results, clinical correspondence, and referrals

  • Maintain accurate, contemporaneous clinical records

  • Participate in practice meetings, clinical governance, audit, and quality improvement activities

  • Work collaboratively as part of the multidisciplinary team

  • Contribute to the training and supervision of medical and allied health professionals where appropriate

Borth Surgery is a purpose-built Health Centre, established in 1995, located on the main street of Borth, a charming coastal village nestled in the heart of Cardigan Bay. We are a highly community-focused practice, committed to delivering compassionate, patient-centred care while fostering strong relationships with our local population.

Our modern premises offer excellent facilities, including two large rear car parks with designated disabled spaces, ensuring easy access for patients and staff. The practice serves a wide and diverse area, from Penparcau in the south to Furnace in the north, and across to Ponterwyd in the east.

We have a friendly and experienced multidisciplinary team comprising a GP Partner, a Salaried GP, two Practice Nurses, a Healthcare Assistant, and a District Nursing team, supported by a proactive Practice Manager and skilled administrative staff. We pride ourselves on a supportive and collaborative working environment.

In addition to providing a full range of general practice services, we run specialist clinics in Respiratory Care, Diabetes, and Cardiovascular Disease. We are also an established training practice, supporting a range of learners, and host a Coding Hub delivering services to practices across Wales.

title: Consultant Psychiatrist General Adult (ADHD) - Substantive
descriptionHtml:
Atrom Mindcare RTC is seeking an experienced Consultant Psychiatrist in General Adult Psychiatry to join our expanding Adult ADHD Service.

The post-holder will play a key role in delivering high-quality diagnostic assessments, formulation, and management plans for adults presenting with ADHD and related comorbidities. This is a flexible, hybrid role suited to a motivated clinician with a strong interest in neurodevelopmental disorders and modern, patient-centred models of care.

About Atrom Mindcare RTC Adult ADHD Service

Atrom Mindcare is a Private Holistic Psychiatric Clinic located in Epping on the border of North East London and Essex. Atrom Mindcare deliver a range of Adult Psychiatric treatments including Deep TMS and Psychological therapies and Psychiatric Assessments. This post is to recruit for the growing demand for its Adult ADHD pathway under NHS Right to Choose to deliver evidence-based care to adults with ADHD. Our vision is to ensure timely, high-quality assessments and person-centred treatment pathways for all service users.

title: Consultant Psychiatrist Inpatient & Community Forensics
descriptionHtml:
Your expertise can change lives.At Nottinghamshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust, we believe in care that goes beyond treatment--it's about compassion, respect, and trust. If you're ready to make a real difference, we'd love you to join us as a Consultant Forensic Psychiatrist in ourLow Secure and Community Forensic Directorate.

This is an opportunity to work at the heart of our community, supporting people through their recovery journey and helping them build brighter futures. You'll be part of a team that values collaboration, innovation, and inclusion, delivering care across a range of specialist services:

  • Community Forensic Service
  • Inpatient services at Wells Road Centre

Why You'll Love Working With Us

  • Our Values in Action: We put people first--patients and colleagues alike. Compassion and respect aren't just words; they're how we work every day.
  • Support That Matters: From structured mentoring for new consultants to a strong peer network, you'll never feel alone in your role.
  • Flexibility: Full-time is ideal, but we're open to conversations about flexible working.
  • Growth Opportunities: Access our academic programme, CPD sessions, and annual appraisals to keep your skills sharp and your career moving forward.

For an informal chat or visit, contact:

Dr Abdul Shaikh, Clinical Director? abdul.shaikh@nottshc.nhs.uk | ? 0115 969 1300

Apply now and help us shape the future of forensic mental health care in Nottinghamshire.

What Your Role Looks Like

The post-holder will have consultant responsibilities for a caseload of up to 14 in inpatient and 8 community-based patients. Some of these patients will be subject to Mental Health Act (MHA) provisions (conditionally discharged, guardianship or CTO). Care co-ordination is provided by community psychiatric nurses, occupational therapists or mental health practitioners. You will have specific consultant responsibility predominantly for patients across Nottinghamshire.

Day-to-day, you'll:

  • Provide high-quality, evidence-based care to patients in the community and in an inpatient setting.
  • Work closely with multidisciplinary teams to ensure safe, effective treatment.
  • Take part in service development and academic programmes.
  • Uphold professional standards and contribute to the efficient running of services.

#TeamNottsHC comprises over 11,000 dedicated colleagues who #MakeADifference every day. We deliver intellectual disability, mental health, community health, forensic, and offender healthcare services across Nottinghamshire, Leicestershire, Lincolnshire, and South Yorkshire. Our care is provided from over 200 sites, spanning community locations, acute settings, and secure environments, including prisons.

We are one of the largest mental health and community Trusts in the East Midlands and one of Nottinghamshire's biggest employers. We also host national and regional services, such as the National High Secure Deaf Service and the Nottingham Centre for Transgender Health.

We offer a variety of employee-led staff networks, including Equality, Diversity, and Inclusion (EDI) groups, the Green Champions network, the Freedom to Speak Up network, the Health and Wellbeing Champions network, and the Menopause Champions network.

The health and wellbeing of our colleagues is a top priority. We invest significantly in this through our in-house occupational health and staff counselling services, supported by a dedicated Health and Wellbeing team.

The Trust is committed to reducing its carbon emissions, with a specialised Energy and Environmental team working to ensure compliance with environmental legislation, enhance our environmental performance, and achieve our net-zero commitment.

title: General Practitioner (GP)
descriptionHtml:
The primary focus for this role is to help deliver safe and effective patient care to registered patients across DMC Primary care. You will be responsible for the provision of medical services to the practice population, delivering an excellent standard of clinical care whilst complying with the [GMS/PMS] contract. Furthermore, the post-holder will adhere to the GMC standards for good medical practice, contributing to the effective management of the practice, leading by example, maintaining a positive, collaborative working relationship with the multidisciplinary team.

The delivery of effective medical care to the entitled population. Provision of services in line with the GMS contract. Generic prescribing in accordance with local and national guidance. Effective management of long-term conditions using CESEL guidelines. Timely processing of administration, including referrals, repeat prescriptions and related tasks. On a rotational basis, undertake telephone triage and duty doctor responsibilities. Maintain accurate clinical records in line with best practice, policy and guidance. Work collaboratively, sharing an equal proportion of the practice workload. Adhere to clinical guidelines and participate in audit processes. Contribute to continuous improvement and quality initiatives within the practice. Accept delegated responsibility for specific areas, including QOF. Attend and contribute effectively to practice meetings. Support the development and maintenance of the practice, including clinical governance, training, financial management and HR. Ensure compliance with appraisal and revalidation. Commit to ongoing professional development and promote learning across the practice team. Support the training of medical students. Assist partners in achieving strategic objectives, making recommendations to improve income and reduce costs. Adhere to practice protocols and policies. Promote collaborative working and a culture of continuous improvement. Participate in practice audits, local initiatives to enhance service delivery.

title: Clinical Pharmacist
descriptionHtml:

title: Consultant Psychiatrist, Crisis Intervention (attracts £25K RRP)
descriptionHtml:
Surrey and Borders Partnership NHS Foundation Trust is a General Medical Council (GMC) Sponsor Employer.

This job attracts a Recruitment and Retention payment of £25,000 in addition to £8000 relocation allowance. The RRP is pro rata for part time employees.

We are looking for an enthusiastic and compassionate Consultant Psychiatrist to join our Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services (CAMHS) Crisis and Liaison team, working across Frimley and Redhill. You will play a key role in supporting children and young people under 18 who are experiencing a mental health crisis, providing expert clinical input, assessment, and treatment within a well-established multi-disciplinary team.

The Crisis Intervention Service (CIS) provides timely mental health support to children and young people seen in hospital emergency departments, community settings, or referred through our 24/7 CYPS Crisis Line. You'll work closely with colleagues from mental health, education, paediatrics, and social care to deliver effective, evidence-based care and to help prevent hospital admissions where possible.

This role offers the opportunity to contribute to service development, clinical leadership, and the ongoing improvement of crisis pathways across Surrey. You will also be encouraged to take part in teaching, training, and quality improvement initiatives within a supportive and forward-thinking Trust.

Work Base to be negotiated between: Leatherhead, Chertsey or Guildford.

The Consultant's duties will be predominantly devoted to the care and treatment of children and young people (under 18 years old) in our crisis pathway.

This is somewhat a unique role, as having elements of interface with social care, paediatric acute colleagues and our Hope Service counter parts with support from the Crisis Intervention Service. We are committed to staff development and training opportunities.

This role will require you to travel between multiple sites within your working day.

Our Offer:

  • NHS Consultant grade £113,565 - £150,569 per annum + £149 fringe + on- call requirement
  • GMC Sponsorship
  • Recruitment premia £25,000 *subject to policy requirements
  • Relocation allowance: up to £8000 *subject to policy requirement
  • Sponsorship for International candidates
  • Up to £2000/year CPD allowance *subject to policy requirements
  • NHS pension employers contribution 23.7% from day one
  • Company Car Lease Scheme
  • Discounted Nuffield Gym Membership and many mor

Please check our benefits here:Medical : Surrey and Borders Partnership NHS Foundation Trust for other benefits.

Surrey and Borders Partnership NHS Foundation Trust is the leading provider of health and social care services for people of all ages with mental ill-health and learning disabilities in Surrey and North East Hampshire. We also provide social care services for people with a learning disability in Croydon and ASD and ADHD assessment services in Hampshire.

We actively seek to engage people who use our services and our communities in improving the mental wellbeing of the local population. We work closely with other NHS and voluntary sector organisations who provide services and support people who use services and carers.

Surrey is a beautiful county lying just 30 minutes away from Central London and from the South Coast.

Our historic market towns and bustling districts are enveloped in wonderful countryside, and our excellent road and rail networks bring the rest of the country within easy reach.

For international travel, both Gatwick and Heathrow airports are nearby.

Please note that we reserve the right to close posts as soon as sufficient applications are received.

We look forward to receiving your application!

title: Consultant Psychiatrist, CYPS, Aldershot (attracts £25K RRP)
descriptionHtml:
Surrey and Borders Partnership NHS Foundation Trust is a General Medical Council (GMC) Sponsor Employer.

This job attracts a Recruitment and Retention payment of £25,000 in addition to £8000 relocation allowance. The RRP is pro rata for part time employees.

We are looking for a Consultant Psychiatrist to join our Community Children and Young People's (CYPS) Mental Health Team in North East Hampshire, based at the Aldershot Centre for Health.

This is a fantastic opportunity to join a well-established, welcoming, and multi-skilled team that supports the mental health and wellbeing of children and young people aged 5 to 18. Our service provides specialist assessments, evidence-based treatments and ongoing support for young people with a range of emotional, behavioural, and complex mental health needs.

You'll provide clinical leadership and direct psychiatric input as part of a multidisciplinary team that includes psychologists, nurses, therapists, and support workers. You'll work with schools, GPs, local authorities and other partners to ensure coordinated and person-centred care. The team also has strong links to our Eating Disorder Service, Crisis Intervention and Early Intervention in Psychosis teams.

You'll be joining a Trust committed to early intervention, prevention, and supporting young people to thrive. If you're passionate about improving outcomes for children and families, we'd love to hear from you!

You'll have the opportunity of working within a well-established and friendly team of highly skilled professionals who are passionate and committed to the care needs of our children and young people.

You would be responsible for providing a diagnostic, assessment and treatment service for children and adolescents with mental health problems within a multi-disciplinary approach to care, promoting high-quality multidisciplinary working and relationships. On average, a full-time consultant would complete 2-3 monthly assessments. Patients have a consultant review after 6 weeks of treatment in the team and then every 2-3 months.

You will participate in an emergency out-of-hours rota, providing back-up for junior doctors and professionals in assessing young people seen in A&E.

You'll have opportunities to support, supervise and train our Junior Medical Staff within the team.

title: Volunteer Car Driver - Sheffield
descriptionHtml:
We have a fantastic opportunity for a Volunteer Car Drivers to join our team based in Sheffield.

Are you ready to make a meaningful impact in your community?Join us as a Patient Transport Volunteer Driver and become a vital part of our Patient Transport Service in your local area. Your commitment will ensure that vulnerable patients can access essential medical appointments on time with ease and comfort.

Our volunteer team is a diverse blend of individuals united by a shared desire to make a positive difference in their communities.

As a volunteer, you'll be the friendly face that patients rely on during their journey to appointments. Your role is simple yet profoundly impactful: providing safe and reliable transportation, while offering reassurance and support during a challenging time in their lives.

No prior experience is necessary- just bring your caring attitude, a 4-5 door car, and some spare time. Whether you're available from the crack of dawn or prefer flexible hours that fit around your schedule, every contribution counts.

By volunteering, you will experience the fulfilment of giving back to your community and supporting the NHS. Join our growing team of compassionate volunteers who are dedicated to enhancing patient care and making a real difference in people's lives.

title: Salaried GP - LLR
descriptionHtml:
At DHU Healthcare, every role matters. Were a not-for-profit team driven by compassion and respect, where your voice is heard and your growth truly matters. Join us and be part of something bigger. For you, for them, with us.

Shaping the future of care.

At DHU Healthcare, our Urgent and Emergency Care teams work on the frontline of the NHS, delivering expert, compassionate care 24/7, 365 days a year. From Emergency Departments and Urgent Treatment Centres to GP surgeries and communities across the East Midlands and beyond, were there when people need us most.

Our teams of skilled medical, nursing, allied health, and support professionals all work together to respond quickly and effectively to every patient. We deliver a wide range of services including community nursing, urgent treatment, primary care streaming, urgent on-day primary care, GP home visiting, phlebotomy, community hospital medical cover, telephone consultation support, and palliative care home visiting. With us, youll be supported to succeed - in your role, your development, and your career.

Every patient journey relies on skilled clinicians delivering safe, high quality care. Your expertise helps us meet urgent needs and improve outcomes.

As a Salaried GP you will:

  • Assess, diagnose and manage patients presenting with urgent undifferentiated illness and minor injury presentations in line with UTC scope, competence and local pathways.
  • Undertake clinical history taking, physical examination and clinical decision making using evidence based practice.
  • Request, interpret and act on appropriate investigations available within the UTC setting, including point of care tests, ECGs and imaging where available and authorised.
  • Maintain full GMC registration, licence to practise and inclusion on the Performers List.
  • Maintain appraisal, revalidation, mandatory training and professional development requirements.

We offer a benefits package with your health, happiness and future in mind. You'll have access to the NHS pension scheme (and well honour your existing NHS pension pot and holiday entitlement if transferring), free parking at most sites, birthday leave, and our Health Cash Plan for you and your family covering dental, optical, therapy costs, and 24/7 GP access after six months.

Plus, wellbeing perks, flexible working, a salary sacrifice Car Lease Scheme with low-emission options, enhanced maternity and paternity leave, and a rewarding referral programme. It's our way of saying thank you.

Learning, leading, shaping healthcare

At DHU Healthcare, we support your growth at every stage of your career. With career paths, tailored training, and the DHU Academy, you'll have the tools and encouragement to explore skills and opportunities, take the next step, and make an impact. From leadership programmes and apprenticeships to essential role-specific training, development is part of how we work and shape healthcare together.

A culture where differences matter.

We believe that when everyone feels valued respected and supported, they can do their best work. We're proud to reflect the rich diversity of the communities we serve, welcoming colleagues from all backgrounds. We are committed to supporting the Armed Forces community and, as a Disability Confident Employer, we welcome candidates to share any support or reasonable adjustments they may need during the recruitment process.

title: Consultant Psychiatrist in Older Adults
descriptionHtml:
Priory Hospital Dewsbury is looking for a Consultant Psychiatrist in Older Adults (or General Adult Psychiatrist with experience in managing Older Adults).

Flexible hours up to 37.5 hours per week.

Competitive Salary and package.

Service rated Good CQC.

Based in the residential area of Earlsheaton, Dewsbury, West Yorkshire, Priory Hospital Dewsbury provides 32 beds, divided into two 16-bed wards for males who have mental health disorders. Hartley Ward is a level 2 Rehabilitation and Recovery Ward (Higher Support Needs). Jubilee Ward is an Older Adult service. Each service has a dedicated Consultant Psychiatrist who performs the duties of Responsible Clinician.

The available post is for Jubilee Ward (10 bedded Specialist Dementia Service, and 6 bedded Functional Disorders).

An excellent opportunity for somebody looking to join an established team caring for individuals with Dementia. Jubilee Ward is a 16 bedded male unit which provides a therapeutic environment for men with dementia (10 beds) and Functional Disorders (6 beds). Most patients are under MHA. The Consultant will work closely with other experienced members of the MDT. The post would be suitable for an Older Adult Consultant Psychiatrist or a General Adult Psychiatrist, with experience of older adults.

descriptionHtml:

The main focus of this post will be provision of mental health services to the county region of Nottingham, specifically the Broxtowe and Hucknall Locality Mental Health Team, which covers the relevant practices within the catchment area and includes the associated university populations.

An Advisory Appointment Committee (AAC) will be required for this post.

A Golden Hello of 20% of the minimum point of the National Consultant (2003) contract will be paid for this post.

We are one of the largest mental health and community Trusts in the East Midlands and one of Nottinghamshire's biggest employers. We also host national and regional services, such as the National High Secure Deaf Service and the Nottingham Centre for Transgender Health.

We offer a variety of employee-led staff networks, including Equality, Diversity, and Inclusion (EDI) groups, the Green Champions network, the Freedom to Speak Up network, the Health and Wellbeing Champions network, and the Menopause Champions network. These networks play a vital role in supporting our diverse workforce and promoting a culture of inclusivity.

The health and wellbeing of our colleagues is a top priority. We invest in this through our in-house occupational health and staff counselling services, supported by a dedicated Health and Wellbeing team.

The Trust is committed to reducing carbon emissions, with a specialised Energy and Environmental team working to ensure compliance with environmental legislation, enhance our environmental performance, and achieve our net-zero commitment.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
We are delighted to offer a unique opportunity for a Salaried General Practitioner to join our friendly team at Yorkleigh Surgery which is part of the Inspire Healthcare group. Interested? Informal chats are very welcome

The salaried GP will provide high-quality, patient-centred primary care as part of the practices clinical team. Responsibilities include consulting with patients for acute, chronic and preventive healthcare needs, managing undifferentiated presentations and ensuring safe follow-up and continuity of care. The role involves face-to-face and remote consultations, requesting and interpreting investigations, completing medication reviews, prescribing within governance policies and undertaking home visits when required. The GP will maintain accurate clinical records and contribute to safeguarding by adhering to local and statutory policies.

The postholder will work closely with the multidisciplinary team, including nursing, pharmacy, ANP and social prescribing staff, to deliver coordinated care. They will support the practice in meeting QOF, Enhanced Services and contractual requirements, and take part in clinical meetings, audits, significant event reviews and quality improvement work. Administrative tasks such as reviewing results, processing prescriptions, actioning correspondence and managing clinical queries are part of the role. Participation in the practice rota, including duty doctor sessions where needed, is expected, alongside maintaining professional development in line with GMC revalidation.

Yorkleigh Surgery prides itself on creating a warm, welcoming environment for staff and patients. We provide quality clinical care to approximately 8050 patients and have worked to establish close connections within the local community, including nursing and residential homes, pharmacies, the District Nursing Team, and other healthcare professionals.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
Purbeck Health Centre is looking to appoint a Salaried General Practitioner to join our established and supportive practice in Milton Keynes.

This is a 6-session post, worked on an agreed basis, with a 1-hour unpaid break. A clear job plan will be agreed, and the role is well supported by experienced partners, clinicians and the wider practice team.

We are looking for a General Practitioner who delivers safe, practical clinical care, communicates clearly with patients and colleagues, and works well as part of a team while remaining confident in autonomous practice. Continuity, sound clinical judgement and respectful working relationships are important to how we work.

Salary is competitive and will be discussed with suitable candidates. The post is offered on BMA model salaried General Practitioner terms, with annual leave, study leave and NHS Pension eligibility.

The post holder will provide high-quality general practice care to the registered patient population, working independently while being part of a supportive multidisciplinary team.

The role involves assessing, diagnosing and managing acute and long-term conditions through face to face, telephone and online consultations, in line with local and national guidance. This includes safe prescribing, appropriate referrals, reviewing results and completing associated clinical administration in a timely manner.

The post holder will contribute to the ongoing management of patients with long-term conditions, support health promotion and preventative care, and maintain clear, accurate clinical records.

The role includes participation in practice meetings, clinical governance activity, audit, significant event reviews and quality improvement work. The post holder will engage fully with appraisal and revalidation requirements and contribute to a professional, respectful working environment.

A clear job plan will be agreed and reviewed regularly to support safe and sustainable working.

Purbeck Health Centre is a GP-led general practice providing care to a diverse local population in Milton Keynes. Clinical leadership sits with the General Practitioners, supported by a skilled and well-established multidisciplinary team.

Our clinical team includes Advanced Nurse Practitioners and Advanced Clinical Practitioners, Practice Nurses, Healthcare Assistants, Clinical Pharmacists, Pharmacy Technicians and First Contact Physiotherapists. This structure allows patients to be seen by the most appropriate clinician and supports safe, efficient care delivery.

The practice is supported by a Practice Manager and a trainee Deputy Practice Manager, alongside a strong administrative function. We actively support training and development, including structured programmes for management roles.

We are forward thinking in our approach and make practical use of digital tools, including artificial intelligence, to support clinical and administrative work, improve efficiency and reduce unnecessary workload, while maintaining patient safety and professional standards.

Our administrative and reception teams are central to patient access, care navigation and the smooth day-to-day running of the practice. We place strong emphasis on clear communication, professional standards and effective teamwork.

We aim to deliver reliable, well-organised general practice care, supported by strong leadership, good systems and a respectful working culture.

title: Salaried General Practitioner
descriptionHtml:
All Saints Surgery is a friendly, single site practice in Burton On Trent, caring for around 11,000 patients as part of East Staffordshire Primary Care. We are looking for an enthusiastic salaried GP to join our team and help us strengthen capacity for patients, with a particular focus on supporting timely same-day urgent care alongside good continuity for those who need it most.

You will work alongside 2 GP partners, 1 salaried GPs, our nursing team and a wider multidisciplinary team that includes clinical pharmacists, first contact physiotherapists, social prescribers and care coordinators. We use EMIS Web and offer a supportive environment with protected time, regular clinical meetings and a real commitment to a manageable, sustainable workload.

We would be happy to talk to GPs at any stage of their career, including those recently qualified, those returning to practice, and experienced GPs looking for a settled salaried role. We can be flexible on sessions and working pattern for the right person, and we welcome an informal chat or visit before you apply.

Provide consultations to patients attending the surgery, by telephone and online clinically appropriate.

Take a share of duty doctor and same-day urgent access sessions, triaging and managing acute presentations safely.

Assess, diagnose and treat patients across the full range of general practice, making appropriate referrals to secondary care and other services.

Prescribe safely and cost effectively in line with practice and ICB formulary guidance, and contribute to medicines optimisation and repeat prescribing.

Review and action investigation results, clinical correspondence and documents in a timely way.

Contribute to the ongoing management of patients with long term conditions and to delivery of the Quality and Outcomes Framework and local and enhanced services.

Maintain accurate, contemporaneous and coded records using EMIS Web

Recognise and act on safeguarding concerns for children and adults at risk in line with practice policy and statutory duties.

At All Saints Surgery you will join a close, supportive team where people genuinely look out for one another. Our GPs, nurses, pharmacists and wider clinical and administrative colleagues work side by side, share knowledge openly and help each other through the busy days. New starters tell us they feel welcome from day one.

The atmosphere is calm, friendly and grounded. We protect time for a proper coffee and a chat as well as for clinical meetings, and we take workload and wellbeing seriously, so you can do good work without feeling stretched too thin. Decisions are made together and your ideas will be heard, whatever your stage of career.

You will have a manageable, well-organised list, protected administrative time and generous study leave to support your development, appraisal and revalidation, plus the NHS Pension Scheme and the day-to-day backing of experienced colleagues and a strong multidisciplinary team. We are happy to be flexible on sessions and working patterns to fit life outside work. WE offer free parking.

Above all, this is a place that values kindness, continuity and good medicine. If you want to work somewhere you are trusted, supported and able to build real relationships with patients and colleagues, we would love to hear from you.

title: First Responder PTS and Events (FREC 3 / 4) Bank Worker
descriptionHtml:
At YorMed, were proud to be a CQC registered 'Good' independent ambulance service supporting patients, NHS partners, and private clients across the UK and beyond. We are based in beautiful countryside near Malton, just outside York.

Due to continued growth, we are looking for enthusiastic individuals with a passion for excellence in patient care to join our Patient Transport and Event Medical teams. Ideally to commit to providing 1 shift a week.

We are looking for FREC 3 and FREC 4 qualified First Responders based across North Yorkshire and York to join our expanding team.

We have regular weekend and weekday work available throughout the year including patient transport missions and a variety of exciting events across the region. We offer flexibility that fits around your existing commitments, choosing work that suits your availability.

Responsibilities include:

  • Respond promptly to calls, operating effectively both independently and as part of a clinical team
  • Accurately record, process, and share patient information, including observations and treatment, with relevant healthcare partners (within GDPR Guidelines)
  • Maintain clear and consistent communication with the Control Room and colleagues in line with operational and clinical protocols
  • Provide an appropriate initial assessment and immediate care within the FREC 3/4 scope and organisational policies.
  • Recognise illness, injury and patient deterioration and request appropriate clinical support.
  • Record observations, care provided and escalation decisions accurately.
  • Support safe, dignified and person-centred patient transport where assigned.
  • Assist patients with mobility, wheelchairs and transfers.
  • Provide first-response medical cover at events as part of an agreed clinical structure.
  • Work effectively with clinicians, control teams, event staff and emergency services.
  • Maintain patient privacy, dignity, consent and confidentiality.
  • Follow safeguarding, infection prevention, information governance and incident-reporting procedures.
  • Check and maintain equipment, consumables and vehicles.
  • Safely assist with the movement and handling of patients using appropriate techniques and equipment following risk assessment
  • Work only within your verified scope of practice and seek support whenever a patients needs exceed it.

YorMed Ltd is an independent CQC registered provider with a Good rating based in the beautiful rural countryside at Eddlethorpe - just outside of Malton, and close to the city of York.

title: Ambulance Care Assistant (bank)
descriptionHtml:
Join our dedicated emergency CQC registered response team as an Ambulance Care Assistant/Driver, where you'll play a vital role in delivering compassionate patient care and ensuring safe transportation to healthcare facilities. This dynamic position combines the responsibilities of providing essential support to paramedics, first responders and patients with the crucial task of driving ambulance vehicles efficiently and safely. Your energetic approach and commitment to safety will help us deliver timely, professional medical assistance in diverse situations, making a real difference in people's lives every day.

We are looking for people to join our bank and are ideally able to commit to one shift per week (min 4 hours). You must be able to start work from the Ambulance Station at Malton, and be prepared to travel anywhere in the UK.

Duties

  • Safely operate ambulance vehicles, adhering to all traffic laws and safety protocols, while maintaining a high standard of driving professionalism.
  • Assist paramedics with patient handling, including lifting, transferring, and securing patients on stretchers or wheelchairs.
  • Provide compassionate support to patients during transit, ensuring their comfort and dignity are maintained at all times.
  • Conduct routine vehicle maintenance checks, including fluid levels, tire pressure, and safety equipment, reporting any issues promptly.
  • Communicate clearly and effectively with team members, emergency services, and patients to coordinate smooth operations.
  • Support the loading and unloading of medical equipment and supplies necessary for patient care.
  • Maintain accurate records of journeys, patient details, and vehicle inspections in compliance with organisational policies.

YorMed Limited is an independent ambulance, patient transport and event medical services provider based in North Yorkshire, delivering professional, reliable and patient-focused services across the UK.

Why Work With YorMed?

At YorMed, we believe that the quality of our service starts with the people who deliver it. We are committed to building a professional, supportive and dependable team of ambulance and event medical personnel who share our focus on excellent patient care.

Varied opportunities including patient transport, ambulance work and medical cover at a wide range of events.

Flexible working our bank and casual opportunities can work well alongside other employment and existing commitments.

Professional standards our patient transport services operate within a CQC-regulated environment, with a strong emphasis on governance, safeguarding, infection prevention, patient dignity and safety.

A supportive team environment as an independent provider, we value good communication and develop positive working relationships with our crews.

Opportunities to use your skills whether you are working in patient transport or providing medical support at an event, you will have the opportunity to put your training and experience into practice.

Clear compliance standards we take recruitment and compliance seriously and require appropriate qualifications, competencies, DBS checks and supporting documentation before personnel are approved for deployment.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:

title: Salaried GP - 6 sessions
descriptionHtml:

The Oaks is a forward thinking and progressive organisation with two main objectives, firstly to become an employer of choice that secondly, delivers first class care to its patients.

The Practice is now actively encouraging its salaried GP team to not just to get involved, but to assist and lead on projects that achieve our two main business aims highlighted above. Of course, time is given and protected to do this.

The Practice, whilst having a family feel to it, also understands the importance of structure, recognition and development for its staff. This is an excellent opportunity for anyone looking to work in a supporting environment with a built in culture of development and progression.

We have sessions available at multiple sites and throughout the week so please don't hesitate to get in touch if you would like to talk about this or anything else.

descriptionHtml:

title: Speciality Doctor in Eating Disorders
descriptionHtml:
This post forms part of the new Community Eating Disorders Service. The role will involve direct clinical care and supporting a multi-disciplinary team which includes specialist nurses, nurse therapists, clinical psychologists, dietitians, occupational therapists, social workers, and peer support workers. The work is outpatient based and will include assessment and follow-up work and management of psychiatric and physical co-morbidity.

The ratio of new patients to follow-up is expected to be 1:5.

Protected time will be allocated within the job plan for CPD and audit. Training will be available and there will be opportunities to be involved in research.

It is envisaged that the post holder will work 10 programmed activities over 5 days. Following appointment, a meeting will take place no later than three months from appointment with the Lead Consultant and Medical Lead to review and revise the job plan and objectives of the post holder.

The main responsibilities of this post will be to support the consultants in providing high quality services to patients with eating disorders. The post-holder will assist the consultants in all aspects of the service, including the provision of emergency care.

The post-holder will be expected to assess and manage patients suffering from a range of eating disorders; this will include both psychiatric and general medical care. Management will include both pharmacological and psychological treatments. The post-holder will be expected to carry out a full medical assessment, perform a mental state examination and perform a physical examination when appropriate.

The post-holder will assess patients referred for both outpatient and inpatient treatment and liaise with referrers.

The post-holder will support non-medical members of the multidisciplinary team and review patients as required at their request.

The post-holder will be expected to attend team meetings and clinical reviews, leading such events if required.The post-holder will conduct, and regularly review, assessments of risk with patients and determine/agree management strategies to reduce risks.

The post-holder will communicate and liaise with relatives and carers and other disciplines and agencies, including general practitioners, as appropriate. The post may also include liaison with other trusts regarding individual patient care.

At Coventry and Warwickshire Partnership NHS Trust (CWPT), we deliver a wide range of physical, mental health, learning disability and autism services, and are proud to serve communities across Coventry, Warwickshire and beyond.

We put 'people at our heart'; this ethos is at the centre of everything we do and how we do it. We care for our staff and colleagues as much as they care for others and offer a wide range of benefits and development opportunities.

  • generous annual leave entitlement which increases during your time with us
  • excellent learning and development opportunities, including apprenticeship frameworks, distance learning, internal training, coaching and mentoring, and much more
  • salary sacrifice schemes for lease car/ vehicle, Cycle to Work, home and electronics, gym membership and more
  • discounts with a range of retailers, restaurants and entertainment venues through our Employee Assistance Programme and NHS discount schemes
  • wellbeing support, including an in-house counselling service, external helpline and more
  • staff networks and support group

We're always on the lookout for people who share our passion for improving the lives and wellbeing of people in our community, as well as our values of compassion, collaboration, excellence, integrity and respect.

title: Consultant Medical Virologist
descriptionHtml:
This is a full-time post for virology services at UKHSA Clinical Network Laboratory, Birmingham, providing Consultant level input into the laboratory, clinical virology and public health service. The post is based at the Lead Public Health Laboratory for the Midlands which is situated at the Birmingham Heartlands Hospital in the University Hospital Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust (Teaching). However, it is a requirement of employment that the post holder be prepared to work at any additional or different location owned or served by the trust, either on an on-going or temporary basis according to the demands of the service. The provision of clinical virology services at Good Hope, Solihull, Birmingham Heartlands Hospitals and Queen Elizabeth Hospital will be by rotation and in partnership with other infection service consultants. In addition to the clinical virology service, the post holder will be providing public health functions for the Midlands Region.

The University Hospital Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust is one of 96 Foundation Trusts in England. The Trust was established in the first of April 2018 by the merger of Heart of England and Queen Elizabeth Hospital Foundation Trusts. The new organisation includes Birmingham Heartlands Hospital, Good Hope Hospital, Solihull District General Hospital, Queen Elizabeth Hospital and Birmingham Chest Clinic. It is a dynamic organisation that represents one of the largest trusts in the UK.

See attached Job Description.

1. Work with colleagues for the provision of a comprehensive clinical medical virology service including: advice regarding appropriate specimens, involvement in specimen analysis, validation and interpretation of results for transmission to service users. Appropriate involvement in policies guidelines and standard operating procedures preparation, relevant to consultant virologist duties. On-call duty will be shared equitably with the other consultants in virology and will involve supervision and support of the on-call Specialist Trainees on front-line duty and provision for cover for consultant colleagues' periods of leave. The on-call support is generally through telephone consultation and only on rare occasions is attendance necessary.

2. In conjunction with the other infection (microbiology, virology, infectious diseases, and immunology) consultants, provide ward-based and telephone advice on the prevention, diagnosis and management of infection in individual patients and outbreaks of infection. This will involve ad hoc clinical consults arising from referrals or significant laboratory results, attending multi-disciplinary clinical meetings and regular ward rounds.

3. Collaborate with colleagues in UKHSABPHL and Infectious Disease Unit in delivering a joint infection service for the host Trust and other users of the service

For further details, please refer to the attached Job Description & Person Specification.

We pride ourselves as being an employer of choice, where Everyone Matters promoting equality of opportunity to actively encourage applications from everyone, including groups currently underrepresented in our workforce.

UKHSA ethos is to be an inclusive organisation for all our staff and stakeholders. To create, nurture and sustain an inclusive culture, where differences drive innovative solutions to meet the needs of our workforce and wider communities. We do this through celebrating and protecting differences by removing barriers and promoting equity and equality of opportunity for all.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:

title: Consultant in Stroke Medicine
descriptionHtml:
The Trust's Stroke Department in the Directorate of Elderly Care, Stroke and Rehabilitation falls under the remit of the Speciality Medicine Collaborative.

Our CEO, Trudie Davies, and Executive Medical Director, Adrian Clements, would love to hear from you to discuss your future career in North Cumbria. To arrange an informal chat, please contact Sally Rushton on Sally.Rushton1@ncic.nhs.uk for Trudie and Julia McClune on Julia.mcclune@ncic.nhs.uk for Adrian.

descriptionHtml:

The post-holder will be expected to contribute to the smooth running, governance, and further development of the IBD service including:

  • Independent care of patients with complex IBD
  • Actively lead and contribute to IBD MDTs
  • Support and training of the IBD nurses
  • Foster close teamworking within the IBD team
  • Developing IBD care pathways
  • Support networking with internal and external providers
  • Support IBD data collection/ audit and database
  • Implement national policies and guidance and local GIRFT recommendations relating to IBD care
  • Develop departmental IBD research portfolio
  • Maintain appropriate CPD
  • Endoscopy (Elective, training, and inpatient emergency)
  • Outpatient work (clinics, referral vetting, GP advice and guidance)
  • Inpatient work (Consultant of the week to cover GI ward, Ward referrals)
  • Weekend work (6 hours on site and emergency endoscopy) 1 week in 14

You will be expected to be able to travel to all three Trust hospital Sites (Watford General Hospital, Hemel Hempstead Hospital and St Albans Hospital).

You will take part in clinical governance and clinical risk management, and in their implementation, including audit.

A new hospital has been planned for Watford. A new four roomed Endoscopy Unit at St Albans has been planned with a completion date of 2026.

We are building on the success of our award-winning virtual hospital and re-imaging models of care, working ever more closely with partners and making the most of advances in digital healthcare.

Staff wellbeing and development are a priority at West Herts Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust, as is the role of innovation in improving clinical care, outcomes and patient experience.

We are a flexible working employer

At West Herts we recognise the importance of a good work life balance and the ability to work flexibly. We are delighted to offer a variety of flexible working options for all staff. Please check out our web page for more information.

https://www.westhertshospitals.nhs.uk/flexibleworking/

We encourage and welcome people with disabilities. If you need help, please ask.

We reserve the right to close this advert early due to the volume of applicants. Please apply as soon as possible to avoid disappointment.

If you do not hear back within 3 weeks of your application, please assume you have been unsuccessful on this occasion.

title: Consultant Dermatologist
descriptionHtml:
Join 18 Week Support as a Consultant Dermatologist and make a direct contribution to improving patient access to NHS care. We are seeking experienced Dermatologists to deliver both Two-Week Wait (2WW) and General Dermatology clinics across our NHS services.

You will work alongside experienced clinical teams, helping to reduce waiting times while delivering high-quality, patient-centred care. This is an opportunity to use your expertise in a supportive environment, with flexible opportunities available across a range of NHS sites.

If you are an experienced Consultant Dermatologist looking for additional clinical work alongside your existing commitments, we would be pleased to hear from you.

  • As a Consultant Dermatologist, you will be responsible for delivering high-quality dermatology clinics, including:

    • Assessing, diagnosing and managing patients across 2WW and General Dermatology pathways.
    • Undertaking comprehensive dermatological examinations and clinical assessments.
    • Assessing and managing patients with suspected skin cancer where appropriate.
    • Developing and communicating appropriate treatment and management plans.
    • Providing specialist clinical advice and guidance to patients and colleagues.
    • Maintaining accurate and timely clinical documentation and communicating outcomes appropriately.
    • Working collaboratively with the wider clinical team to ensure safe and effective patient care.
About 18 Week Support

18 Week Support is a leading NHS insourcing provider, working in partnership with NHS Trusts across the UK to increase clinical capacity, reduce waiting times and improve patient access to care.

Our clinical teams work alongside NHS services to deliver additional outpatient and surgical capacity, supported by experienced Clinical Leads and Nurse Leads. Patient safety, clinical governance and quality of care are central to everything we do.
