title: Locum Consultant in Obstetrics and Gynaecology
descriptionHtml:
Join a dynamic and forward-thinking Obstetrics and Gynaecology team committed to delivering high-quality patient care, service development, innovation and collaborative working. Applications are welcomed from candidates who have a range of skills committed to a flexible job plan to support service needs.

Based within the Croft Wing at Warrington Hospital, the department forms part of a maternity service rated Good by the CQC (January 2024) and provides care for approximately 2,600 births annually.

The department offers a comprehensive range of benign and complex gynaecological surgery. Most hysterectomies are performed laparoscopically, supported by advanced laparoscopic services across Warrington and Halton Hospitals. Additional procedures include outpatient hysteroscopy, NovaSure endometrial ablation and MyoSure tissue removal.

Gynaecological cancer services are delivered in collaboration with Liverpool Women's Hospital, supported by weekly multidisciplinary meetings and specialist nursing teams. Complex endometriosis cases are referred to regional tertiary centres.

The successful candidate will join a motivated consultant team, sharing responsibility for obstetric and gynaecology services while contributing to clinical governance, audit, teaching, training, supervision of junior doctors and ongoing service improvement.

The department welcomes applications from candidates who would be interested in a Locum Consultant Obstetrician & Gynaecologist to provide maternity cover until 31st March 2027, while supporting the Trust's elective recovery programme and continued delivery of high quality gynaecology services.

This is an excellent opportunity to join a dynamic and supportive consultant team committed to delivering high-quality patient care, service development, and collaborative working. The successful candidate will provide comprehensive obstetric and gynaecological care, contribute to service improvement, supervise junior medical staff, and participate in audit, quality improvement, clinical governance, and departmental leadership activities.

The role comprises 10 Programmed Activities (PAs), and in addition there may be an opportunity to do out of hours on-call 1:11 frequency with prospective cover.

Shared office accommodation, dedicated secretarial support, and operational support from the Clinical Business Unit (CBU) Manager are provided

Our mission, vision and values are at the heart of North Cheshire and Mersey NHS Foundation Trust (NCM). They underpin everything we do and everything we aspire to be as an organisation

Our mission is to be exceptional for our patients, our communities and each other

Our vision is to be a great organisation providing excellent healthcare and opportunities to work and learn

Our approach to healthcare is founded on our four core values:

Kind - we are caring, supporting and respectful to everyone

Open - we are honest, transparent and open to new ways of working

Fair - we listen, value our differences and are inclusive to all

One team - we work well together and with our communities

We employ almost 6,500 people from more than 80 nationalities and are fully committed to being an equal, diverse and inclusive employer. Our culture and values ensure that everyone is treated with dignity and respect, and that no job applicant or employee is disadvantaged at any stage of their journey.

We are also proud to be an Armed Forces Friendly organisation and welcome applications from members of the Armed Forces community, including veterans, reservists and families.

Working at NCM means becoming part of a dedicated team of clinical and support staff who are passionate about keeping people well and supporting wellbeing. If you share our values and are motivated by making a difference for our patients, we'd be delighted to receive your application

title: Human Anatomy Unit Deputy Manager
descriptionHtml:
This is an exciting opportunity to play a key role in the leadership and day-to-day operation of Imperial's Human Anatomy Unit. Working closely with the Human Anatomy Unit Manager, you will help ensure the delivery of high-quality anatomical, clinical skills and pathology teaching facilities that support undergraduate, postgraduate, external education and research activities.Support the leadership and operational management of a multidisciplinary anatomical services facility. Supervise and support a dedicated technical team, ensuring the effective planning and delivery of teaching and operational activities. Coordinate the preparation and delivery of anatomy, clinical skills and pathology teaching sessions. Ensure compliance with the Human Tissue Act 2004, Human Tissue Authority (HTA) standards, health and safety legislation, and institutional policies. Oversee the maintenance, development and efficient use of teaching facilities, equipment and resources. Work collaboratively with academic, professional services and external partners to support a high-quality learning experience. Contribute to service development, continuous improvement initiatives and operational planning across the Unit.Imperial's Human Anatomy Unit at our Charing Cross campus.
  • The opportunity to continue your career at a world-leading institution and be part of our mission to use science for humanity.
  • Benefit from a sector-leading salary and remuneration package (including 43 days' annual leave and generous pension schemes).
  • Be part of a diverse, inclusive and collaborative work culture with various staff networks and resources to support your personal and professional wellbeing.

employer: Royal Papworth Hospital NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Thoracic Surgeon
locations: Cambridge Bio Medical Campus, United Kingdom
descriptionHtml:
This is a Substantive Consultant Surgeon post at Papworth Hospital. The post-holder will be expected to be proficient in adult general thoracic surgery as practiced in the UK.

The post-holder will work with the existing team of NHS Consultant Surgeons.

This job is currently based around fixed operating sessions and flexible cover for the other thoracic surgery sessions (currently 6 operating days Mon-Fri with ad-hoc Saturday lists).

Have responsibility for patients admitted under the care of the thoracic surgical service, and provide assessment, treatment and follow up for patients requiring thoracic surgery. Provide a cohesive service with the other Consultants and contribute to the smooth running of Thoracic Services.

Maximise thoracic surgery operating session use through developing and providing cover for both external and internal MDTs.

Contribute to the training of junior doctors in accordance with standards required by college, Postgraduate Dean and hospital. Demonstrate a commitment to continuing professional development and work with the team to build the academic activities of the thoracic surgery group.

Work with the team to support thoracic surgical / oncological related research, as part of an agreed research programme, and to contribute to audit activities.

The on-call Consultant Surgeon at Papworth Hospital also provides cover for thoracic trauma at Addenbrooke's Hospital and occasional, emergency cases from the rest of the Eastern Region.

The post holder will participate in an on-call consultant rota for thoracic surgery which is on a 1 in 4 basis. Currently there are separate on-call rotas for thoracic surgery, cardiac surgery and cardiothoracic transplant surgery, and the surgical group works effectively together.

Clinical support is provided by the resident surgical team, advanced nurse practitioners who are ward based and surgical care practitioners (SCP) on a firm and rota system.

Royal Papworth Hospital NHS Foundation Trust is the UK's leading heart and lung hospital, delivering care to more than 50,000 patients a year in its new state-of-the-art hospital in Cambridge. We perform the most heart and/or lung transplants in the UK and carried out the UK's first successful heart transplant in 1979. It also offers emergency heart attack treatment, sleep centre care and is one of just five centres nationally for those in severe respiratory failure.

Based on the Cambridge Biomedical Campus the largest centre of medical research and health science in Europe the Trust is at the heart of treatments of the future. Royal Papworth became the first hospital trust in the country to be rated outstanding in all five areas assessed by the Care Quality Commission - a rating it still holds today. The Trust holds its values of compassion, excellence & collaboration at its core, and all colleagues joining the team are expected to uphold these in their day-to-day roles & interactions. Royal Papworth is proud of its diverse workforce and encourages people to embrace their individuality.

The Trust values difference and welcomes all applications irrespective of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy & maternity, race, religion & belief, sex and sexual orientation. Providing they meet the minimum post criteria, applicants with disabilities will be offered an interview.

For a street view tour: https://royalpapworth.nhs.uk/virtual-tour

title: Salaried GP with a view to partnership
descriptionHtml:
We are a forward-thinking and dynamic GP practice, committed to providing high-quality care to our patients. We are looking for a dedicated and enthusiastic Salaried GP to join our team for 5/6 sessions per week. We offer a supportive and collaborative working environment, and we're excited to provide an opportunity to be considered for partnership in the future.

The surgery has comprehensive administrative support enabling our clinicians to focus on patient care during their 15 minute consultations. We are a Total Triage surgery using SystmOne and in addition use a variety of innovative online consultation tools like Accurx, SystmConnect.

The surgery is part of the NIHR East Midlands Research Delivery Network and a Training Practice with North Oxfordshire GP Trainee Scheme.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Patient Consultations: Manage both routine and urgent appointments via face-to-face and telephone consultations, ensuring safe, evidence-based, and individualised care.
  • Clinical Examinations & Care Plans: Perform comprehensive clinical assessments, addressing both physiological and psychological needs. Develop personalised care plans with timely referrals in line with practice, PCN, and local guidelines.
  • Independent Prescribing: Prescribe independently within your scope of practice, adhering to local or national prescribing guidelines, and promote health strategies that encourage patients to adopt healthier lifestyles.
  • Home Visits: Manage routine and emergency home visits as required.
  • Administrative Responsibilities: Handle routine administrative tasks such as responding to queries, managing repeat prescriptions, reviewing patient test results, and preparing referral letters or correspondence in a timely manner.
  • Clinical Management: Oversee patient care, initiate investigations, review results, and make appropriate referrals to secondary care or other providers, developing treatment plans that align with disease management protocols and NICE guidelines.
  • Collaboration: Work alongside other health and social care providers to ensure integrated care and maintain accurate, up-to-date patient records.
  • Team Support: Support both clinical and administrative staff in maintaining high standards and meeting practice targets.

Brackley Medical Centre is an innovative and supportive training practice which aims to provide high quality, safe and personalised patient care to over 16,000 patients. We are based in a purpose built health care facility which opened in 2020; the building is shared with both Northamptonshire Health Foundation Trust and Oxford University Hospital Trust who both operate a variety of secondary care services and satellite clinics; which provide our patients with unique local services for our semi-rural practice.

Focussed on high quality patient care and employee development we have a wide multi-disciplinary team; including experienced GPs, compassionate nurses and HCAs and Advanced Clinical Practitioners who respond to patient on the day demand. As part of Brackley & Towcester PCN we have First Contact Physios, Clinical Pharmacists, Mental Health workers, Social Prescribers and Health Coaches. Together, we collaborate to ensure the best possible health outcomes for our patients through a holistic and integrated approach to care.

We are looking to recruit an Salaried GP for 5/6 sessions per week to join our friendly team; salary will be dependent on experience. We will review applications as they come in to facilitate prompt recruitment.

employer: Hull University Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust
title: Consultant Respiratory Medicine
descriptionHtml:
The respiratory department operates a phased working job pattern. The appointee will be on ward duty (Respiratory Ward) for 1 week (7 days) at a time on a 1:5 rota. The respiratory consultants contribute equally to a 1:11 rota for respiratory in-reach to the AAU at HRI. 1 PA is allocated for respiratory inreach duties for week days. The workload for this will be variable as per respiratory admissions to the AAU; winter months see a higher number. Respiratory Consultants are helped by a SpR as well and work can be distributed as per requirements. There will be consideration of time off in lieu (such as for weekend working). Six new patients per clinic will be booked as standard. At the start of the post we do not anticipate follow up patients to be booked in to clinic. In due course when follow-up slots are required 1 new patient slot will equate to 2 follow up patients.

The new appointee will be allocated a consultant colleague to mentor and support them when they start.

The candidate will be supporting both the Asthma and Sleep/ NIV service. The successful candidate will also be expected to develop the CPET/Breathlessness Service

The Humber Health Partnership is one of the largest acute and community Partnership arrangements in the NHS, seeing well over one million patients every year and managing a budget of over £1.3 billion.

Made up of two Trusts - Northern Lincolnshire and Goole NHS Foundation Trust (NLAG) and Hull University Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust (HUTH) - our Partnership has significant ambitions and is committed to delivering world-class hospital and community services for the 1.65 million people we serve.

Together we employ nearly 20,000 staff. Our five main hospital sites are Diana, Princess of Wales Hospital, Scunthorpe General Hospital and Goole and District Hospital, for NLAG and Hull Royal Infirmary and Castle Hill Hospital for HUTH.

As Teaching Hospitals working with the Hull York Medical School, we both lead and contribute to research in many areas - biomedical research, primary care, palliative medicine, cardiovascular and respiratory medicine, vascular surgery, cancer surgery and oncology.

We believe that by developing a diverse, inclusive, innovative, skilled and caring workforce, we can deliver excellent care to our patients and a great future for our employees, our Partnership and our community.

employer: Mid and South Essex NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant -  Diabetes and Endocrinology
descriptionHtml:
An exciting opportunity has arisen for a passionate and dedicated prt time Consultant to join our dynamic Diabetes and Endocrine team at Basildon Hospital!

We're seeking an enthusiastic clinician with a strong interest in specialist diabetic foot care, antenatal diabetes, and a commitment to delivering high-quality, patient-centred care across both inpatient and outpatient settings.

You'll be joining a collaborative and forward-thinking department that values innovation, shared learning, and teamwork. Our service works closely with multidisciplinary colleagues to ensure holistic, effective, and compassionate care for all patients.

At Basildon Hospital, we pride ourselves on fostering a supportive and inclusive environment where your ideas and expertise will help shape the future of our services. Whether you're looking to develop a sub-specialty interest, lead service improvements, or contribute to teaching and research, this is an excellent opportunity to make a meaningful impact while advancing your career.

If you're a motivated Consultant seeking a fulfilling role within a progressive Trust committed to excellence in patient care -- we'd love to hear from you.

You will play an active role in delivering and developing a broad range of sub-specialty outpatient diabetes clinics, including:

  • Diabetic foot
  • Insulin Pump / Hybrid Closed-Loop Clinics
  • Antenatal Diabetes Clinics

You will also be involved in rotational ward cover and will help manage inpatient care on our 27-bed Diabetes, Endocrinology and General Medicine ward, as well as supporting diabetes outliers and our inpatient diabetes team. Additional responsibilities include:

  • Providing electronic triage, Advice & Guidance, and support across specialties
  • Active participation in our established multidisciplinary meetings and collaborative working across departments

Our ambition is to deliver excellent local and specialist services, to improve the health and well being of our patients, and provide a vibrant place for staff to develop, innovate and build careers.

We aim to make the most of our skills and experiences so we can become the best we can be. As one organisation we will recruit the finest and retain more specialist staff due to more employment opportunities across our Trust

employer: The Shrewsbury and Telford Hospital NHS Trust
title: Locum Consultant Radiologist with Specialist Interest in Chest Imaging
descriptionHtml:
The Shrewsbury and Telford Hospital NHS Trust is looking for a Locum Consultant Radiologist with specialist interest in Chest Imaging to support Lung Cancer Screening in a busy and expanding department, predominantly based at he Princess Royal Hospital (PRH), with responsibilities across both hospitals' sites.

Due to a rapidly expanding workload most interests can be accommodated. One cancer MDT is an expectation; a second interest can likely be accommodated. Lung biopsy skills are expected. The posts will include sessions at the two main hospital sites within an overall flexible group job planning format, with an agreed overall sessional make up as described below.

Apart from lung biopsy work, there is currently no dedicated respiratory imaging component such as a formal MDT. There may, however, be scope to develop a non-cancer MDT in the future, as much of this discussion is presently carried out informally through individual meetings or email correspondence with the chest physicians. The ability to cover the screening MDT would be highly valuable, and there may also be future opportunities to take on the Responsible Radiologist role.

Applications are welcome from candidates who wish to be considered for a part-time or flexible working arrangement. Contribution to an out of hours on call rota is core to this role.

  • Share in the general imaging workload and collaborate with colleagues to support tumour-specific and other sub-specialty reporting, using PACS.
  • Contribute to the general work of the department would be expected from the successful applicant, including reporting of the general radiographic examinations carried out within the main sites, as well as in the various community hospital locations in Shropshire and the CDC.
  • Maintain a general Radiology practice while contributing to sub-specialty areas, as per departmental needs.
  • To work flexibly according to changes in work patterns and requirements. Requirement to participate in the non-resident on call and resident evening and weekend working. On call overnight is outsourced from 8.30pm to 8.30am and weekdays and weekends after 5.30pm to provide a more palatable and sustainable work pattern. On site attendance will occasionally be necessary during on call periods.
  • General radiological sessions will include in and outpatient cross section as well as plain films and body ultrasound. General skills must be maintained to support the acute hospitals' needs in evening and weekend working.
  • Addressing GP and clinician queries and vetting are core to the role.
  • To be involved in the organisation and administration of the Radiology Department and teaching of other clinical staff including participation in regular clinico-radiological meetings with other Consultants.
  • To be involved in the training of junior Radiology staff.

The Shrewsbury and Telford Hospital NHS Trust (SaTH) is the main provider of acute hospital services for around half a million people in Shropshire, Telford & Wrekin and mid Wales.

Our main service locations are the Princess Royal Hospital (PRH) in Telford and the Royal Shrewsbury Hospital (RSH) in Shrewsbury which are located 20 minutes' drive apart. Both hospitals provide a wide range of acute hospital services including accident & emergency, outpatients, diagnostics, inpatient medical care and critical care.

Our Poppy's Promise Commitment

We believe that compassionate care sits at the heart of everything we do. Every member of our team -- clinical or non-clinical -- plays a vital role in ensuring that patients, families, and colleagues are treated with dignity, empathy, and respect at all times.

We expect all staff to demonstrate compassion not only through their words, but through their actions: by listening attentively, communicating clearly and kindly, and recognising individual needs, feelings, and circumstances of those in our care.

Effective communication is central to safe and high-quality healthcare. We value colleagues who take the time to understand others, explain information in a meaningful way, and respond to concerns with patience and understanding.

By joining our team, you are committing to uphold these values -- ensuring that every patient feels heard, respected, and valued, and that compassion is embedded in every interaction, every day.

employer: The Shrewsbury and Telford Hospital NHS Trust
title: Consultant Radiologist with interest in Uroradiology
descriptionHtml:

employer: NELFT North East London Foundation Trust
title: Community Adult Consultant Psychiatrist MHWT East
descriptionHtml:
Community Adult Consultant Psychiatrist

This post is for an Adult Consultant Psychiatrist position in the East Mental Health & Wellness Team (MHWT-E), based at Beam Park Health Centre, 2 Halewood Way, Rainham, RM13 8QZ.

This is a replacement, substantive, full-time post - 10 Programmed Activities (PAs) post with 7.5 Direct Clinical Contact activities (DCC) and 2.5 Supporting Professional Activities (SPAs).

On-call responsibility: The postholder will be part of the Senior Psychiatrist on-call rota covering out of hours and weekends for Mental Health Services in NELFT. The on call will cover service delivery for Adults and Older Adults presenting with mental health problems. This is currently a 1:50 rota with a 3% Category A salary supplement. The trust has also a daytime (9am - 5pm) Section 136 rota, with an approximate frequency of one day every three months.

The successful candidate will work as part of a multidisciplinary team providing care to adults with mental health needs who are registered with a GP Practice located in the eastern part of the London Borough of Barking & Dagenham (plus a small number of patients who reside in that part of the Borough but whose GP is elsewhere). This roughly equates to residents of the Electoral Wards named East Brook, Alibon, Goresbrook, River and Village on the borough map in Section 3.1 below.

The successful candidate will provide senior medical support to the team, and direct input on clinical cases. The consultant will be expected to provide guidance and supervision to the team, work directly with adult patients (and their families), and liaise as appropriate with other external mental health providers, and acute hospitals.

NELFT NHS Foundation Trust provides mental health and community services for over 4.9 million people living in the London Boroughs of Waltham Forest, Redbridge, Barking and Dagenham, Havering, and across Essex. We work to ensure our patients, their friends and family, feel confident that their health needs are well met. With an excellent reputation for research and development, our skilled health professionals are at the cutting edge of evidence-based innovation, opening up the possibilities for better ways of working and delivery of care.

employer: Royal United Hospitals Bath NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant in Radiology - Chest Radiology
descriptionHtml:
Applications are invited for a Consultant Radiologist to join a friendly, forward-thinking team of 30 Consultant Radiologists at the Royal United Hospital Bath;

Consultant Radiologist with specialist interest in Chest Radiology (10 PAs).

The post is full time but anyone wishing to work part time is also encouraged to apply. The post includes participation in the evening and weekend and on call rota.

If you want to balance these professional opportunities with quality of life then Bath has it all. Bath is a beautiful Georgian city in the South West of England, and is England's only city with UNESCO World Heritage Site status. There is a wealth of cultural and leisure opportunities, some of the best state and independent schools in the UK, whilst only 90 minutes from London and on the doorstep of the beautiful diverse South West countryside.

This is a replacement post following retirement for a substantive Consultant Thoracic Radiologist.

The RUH will work alongside the existing thoracic radiologists to help deliver the expanding lung cancer service including reporting chest radiographs and CT, performing lung biopsy, and preparing and presenting at the weekly lung cancer MDT meeting. The RUH has a tertiary satellite specialist pulmonary hypertension service, affiliated with The Royal Free London NHS Foundation Trust. Circa 250 referrals per annum are received from around the South West and Wales. The appointee will be involved in reporting CT and MRI for patients with suspected pulmonary hypertension and participating in the weekly PH MDT. There will be an additional requirement to report for and participate in the ILD MDT

An ability to contribute to the cardiac CT +/- MRI service is desirable although not essential. With a specialist cardiac CT list on average at least once a day, the department performs approximately 1200-1400 CTCAs per annum, including CT coronary angiography, aortic valve calcium scoring and TAVI planning scans. The RUH utilises FFRct post-processing analysis as part of the NHSE MedTech mandate.

Working for your organisation

At the RUH we're proud to put people at the heart of what we do, working together as one team to make a difference for our patients, each other, and our community. No matter what your role is, we value everyone's contribution in supporting the exceptional, person-centred care we pride ourselves on.

We are committed to creating a compassionate and inclusive environment. This can be seen in our growing community of staff networks - celebrating successes and creating opportunities to listen and learn. We value our differences, champion kindness and civility, and truly believe that diversity makes us stronger.

A culture of learning, developing and innovating is the thread that runs throughout our whole organisation. We want to support you to thrive, taking your career to its full potential.

We value staff wellbeing, with a well-established programme of support. We believe in a holistic approach spanning all aspects of living a healthy life, including physical, emotional, spiritual and financial wellbeing. We've even got a pool!

We are committed to supporting you and hope you want to join our team. In the meantime, find out more about living and working the beautiful historic city of Bath, learn about our extensive package of staff benefits, and read about how we're providing healthcare fit for the future with the landmark Dyson Cancer Centre and our passion for research.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
Salaried GP | Full-time or Part-time Available | Up to £110,000 per annum FTE (40 hours) dependent on experienceSystem: EMIS Location: Rosedean House Surgery, Liskeard, Cornwall

title: Prescribing Clinical Pharmacist
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for somebody who shares our idea of what a PCN should be - supportive of its member Practices, effective and innovative. You'll be prepared to work hard to look after your patients and work with the lead clinical pharmacist and pharmacy team, wider multidisciplinary team colleagues and PCN leadership team to maintain a resilient and sustainable PCN.

We would like someone to join our team who has at least 1 year experience working as a Clinical Pharmacist in General Practice.

Hours of work per week = 27 to 37 hours

The employer is Network North PCN Ltd

For an informal chat / visit please contact Marie Wragg, PCN Manager marie.wragg2@nhs.net or David Russell, Lead Clinical Pharmacist david.russell8@nhs.net

To apply, please send your CV and covering letter to Marie.wragg2@nhs.net or apply via NHS jobs.

The post holder is a prescribing clinical pharmacist who acts within their professional boundaries, working alongside a team of pharmacists across the PCN which is made up of 5 Practices.

They will improve patients health outcomes and the efficiency of the primary care team by providing direct, accessible and timely medicines and expertise including face to face contact with patients.

The post holder will be an integral part of the PCN, as well as part of a wider general practice and multi-disciplinary team. This includes being a conduit of patient medicines information into and out of hospitals. They will work to optimise medication issues to improve patient care and safety, and augment clinical staff in the management of patients, with minimal support needed from the Lead Pharmacist.

As part of their employment, the post holder will ideally have completed the CPPE pathway and must be an Independent Prescriber, equipping the prescribing clinical pharmacist to be able to practice and prescribe safely and effectively in a primary care setting.

The supervision and mentorship network will be provided to support the prescribing clinical pharmacist.

Network North PCN is a well-established Primary Care Network in North Sheffield, with a stable patient population. We have a compassionate and supportive team. We are committed, friendly and flexible. Key info:

- 5 Practices within the PCN

- On site duty GPs, available for questions/queries/support

- System One and EMIS practices

- Approx. 45,000 patients

- Commitment to CPD

- Emphasis on teaching within Practices

- Forward thinking, innovative and keen to embrace new ways of working

- Multi-disciplinary team - including an Advanced Care Practitioner, Care Coordinators, Clinical Pharmacists, GPs, Mental Health Workers, Pharmacy Technician, Physician Associates, Physiotherapists and Social Prescribing Link Worker

title: GP Educator - Medical Student Education
descriptionHtml:
Put medical education at the heart of your working week

Are you a GP with a passion for teaching who would like education to be the main focus of your role?

This is an exciting opportunity to join WellBN in an education-led post, with the substantial majority of your working week dedicated to supervising, teaching and supporting medical students rather than routine clinical sessions.

The role is particularly suited to a GP with an interest or background in medical education who enjoys helping students develop their clinical reasoning, consultation skills and understanding of patient-centred care.

Join us

If you would like to make teaching and student development the main focus of your working week, while retaining a smaller clinical commitment, we would love to hear from you.

There is an option to convert to a substantive post. Job-share applications are welcome.

We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are happy to discuss reasonable adjustments during recruitment.

For an informal conversation or to express your interest, please contact Susan King at susan.king72@nhs.net.

You will oversee Year 4 and Year 6 medical students during their placements, helping them connect their learning with the realities of modern general practice. Through supervision, case discussion, feedback and teaching, you will support their development as confident, thoughtful and compassionate future doctors.

The post comprises seven sessions dedicated to educational supervision, alongside one or two clinical sessions per week. We welcome job-share applications from GPs interested in sharing the educational and clinical responsibilities.

During student placements, the emphasis will be on education: overseeing the students learning, reviewing clinical cases with them, discussing their assessments and management plans, and providing constructive feedback.

Between student placements, clinical cross-cover is expected to support the wider practice team.

An exciting new chapter for WellBN

WellBN is preparing to launch a new organisation in January 2027, alongside an upcoming rebrand and under new management.

Were developing a progressive, modern approach to general practice, with compassionate patient care, collaborative working and staff wellbeing at its heart. Joining at this stage offers the opportunity to contribute to the educational environment as the organisation develops.

descriptionHtml:
Specialty Doctor - Ellis Ward

Full Time - 10PAs

The Trust is seeking an energetic and motivated specialty doctor, ideally with Section 12 Approval, to work on male only acute inpatient ward to support the consultant psychiatrist in providing high quality clinical care to our patients

This post is based at Tolworth Hospital, Red Lion Rd, Tolworth, Surbiton KT6 7QU. Ellis Ward forms part of the inpatient provision of the Trust's Acute and Urgent Care Service Line, which includes 8 acute adult wards and a PICU, based on 2 sites, Springfield Hospital in Tooting, and Tolworth Hospital in Surbiton.

There are 10 Programmed Activities. These clinical sessions will be on Ellis Ward, within the Inpatient Services of South West London & St George's Mental Health NHS Trust ("the Trust").

The appointed Specialty Doctor will be clinically supervised by the Ellis Ward Consultant Psychiatrist (Dr Jose Felix Mendez Jimenez).

The job plan will be reviewed regularly and may be modified reflecting changing needs within the service.

Ellis ward is a mixed 20 bedded ward. Over the last 12months, on average, there were 12 admissions/transfers in, and 10 discharges/transfers out per month.

South West London and St George's Mental Health Trust was formed in 1998. Springfield University Hospital in Tooting is the largest site from which the Trust operates and has provided mental health services since 1841. It provides a range of mental health, learning disability and substance misuse services.

The Trust was originally known as the Pathfinder NHS Trust in 1994 and provided services for Wandsworth and Merton. In subsequent years its strategy was to grow and to become the main statutory provider of mental health services for South West London. The Trust took on Putney and Roehampton services in 1998, Sutton Mental Health Services in 1999, and Kingston and Richmond services in 2001 as the former health authorities were disbanded and primary care trusts were established. The different histories of services in different boroughs are still reflected in service models, cultures and partnership arrangements but a recent move to Service Lines has enabled more homogeneity across the five London Boroughs the Trust now covers.

The Trust now provides mental health services to five London Boroughs: Wandsworth, Merton, Sutton, Kingston and Richmond.

employer: The Shrewsbury and Telford Hospital NHS Trust
title: Consultant Urological Surgeon with interest in Paediatric Urology
descriptionHtml:
The Shrewsbury and Telford Hospital NHS Trust is seeking to appoint a substantive Consultant Urological Surgeon with a specialist interest in Paediatric Urology. The post will be predominantly based at The Royal Shrewsbury Hospital, with responsibilities extending across both hospital sites.

This is an excellent opportunity to join a supportive and collaborative multidisciplinary team delivering high-quality urology services to a wide and diverse catchment population. The post has been designed to strengthen and further develop urological care across Shropshire, Telford & Wrekin, and Mid-Wales.

The successful candidate will bring expertise in General Urology alongside a subspecialist interest in Paediatric Urology.

Contribution to an out of hours on call rota is core to this role.

  • Provide independent consultant level care for patients, working alongside the wider consultant body to ensure high-quality continuous management.
  • Manage patients with a full range of urological conditions, delivering both elective and emergency care autonomously. This will include providing out-patient and day case activity to support care of children and young people.
  • Contribute actively to clinical governance, audit, and quality improvement activities, and support the education and supervision of junior medical staff and other staffing groups that are involved in patient care.
  • Undertake administrative responsibilities required to support safe and effective clinical practice.
  • To develop enhanced clinical skills, especially in the assessment and management of acutely ill patients.
  • To have excellent team-working skills with the abilities and professional attitude to work well in a multi-professional team.
  • To deliver clinical and quality targets agreed both nationally and locally with clinical teams and commissioners.
  • To follow patients throughout their clinical pathways.

The Shrewsbury and Telford Hospital NHS Trust (SaTH) is the main provider of acute hospital services for around half a million people in Shropshire, Telford & Wrekin and mid Wales.

Our main service locations are the Princess Royal Hospital (PRH) in Telford and the Royal Shrewsbury Hospital (RSH) in Shrewsbury which are located 20 minutes' drive apart. Both hospitals provide a wide range of acute hospital services including accident & emergency, outpatients, diagnostics, inpatient medical care and critical care.

Our Poppy's Promise Commitment

We believe that compassionate care sits at the heart of everything we do. Every member of our team -- clinical or non-clinical -- plays a vital role in ensuring that patients, families, and colleagues are treated with dignity, empathy, and respect at all times.

We expect all staff to demonstrate compassion not only through their words, but through their actions: by listening attentively, communicating clearly and kindly, and recognising individual needs, feelings, and circumstances of those in our care.

Effective communication is central to safe and high-quality healthcare. We value colleagues who take the time to understand others, explain information in a meaningful way, and respond to concerns with patience and understanding.

By joining our team, you are committing to uphold these values -- ensuring that every patient feels heard, respected, and valued, and that compassion is embedded in every interaction, every day.

title: Senior GP Administrator
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking a highly organised, proactive, and experienced Senior Administrator to join our busy and friendly primary care team at Honeypot Medical Centre.

The successful candidate will play a key role in ensuring the smooth day-to-day operation of administrative services across the practice. They will lead and support a team of administrators while delivering efficient, patient-focused services that contribute to high standards of care, regulatory compliance, and practice performance.

The role involves overseeing patient registration processes, clinical recall programmes, document management, workflow allocation, appointment administration, referral processing, prescription support, and the maintenance of accurate patient records using EMIS and Docman systems. The post holder will also support the achievement of Quality and Outcomes Framework (QOF) targets and other contractual requirements through effective patient recall and engagement processes.

As a Senior Administrator, you will act as a point of escalation for administrative queries, contribute to service improvement initiatives, support staff development, and work collaboratively with clinicians, management, and external agencies to ensure safe, efficient, and high-quality patient care.

  • Provide day-to-day supervision and support to the administration team.

  • Coordinate and monitor recall programmes including:
    • QOF recalls
    • Cytology recalls
    • Immunisation recalls
    • NHS Health Check recalls
    • Learning Disability recalls
    • Diabetes recalls
  • Support the management of appointment scheduling and patient communications.
  • Process referrals, prescriptions, and clinical administration tasks.
  • Maintain accurate and up-to-date patient records in accordance with information governance requirements.
  • Liaise with external organisations regarding the archiving and retrieval of patient medical records.
  • Monitor administrative performance and identify opportunities to improve efficiency and patient experience.

    • With over 80 years of service to the local community, Honeypot Medical Centre is a well-established and forward-thinking GP practice committed to delivering high-quality, patient-centred care. With your expertise in Adult Psychiatry, you'll join our multi-disciplinary team (MDT) to deliver patient care through home treatment enabling early discharge from inpatient care. You'll work closely with inpatient wards and community teams, including the Inpatient Social Work service and the Patient Flow Transformation lead.

We offer rewarding career development with protected SPA time as part of your job plan, encouraging you to take leadership courses to enhance your skills. We also offer a relocation allowance of up to £8,000 for external applicants (subject to eligibility criteria).

Applicants must be fully registered with the General Medical Council (GMC) and on the Specialist Register or be within six months attaining their Certificate of Completion of Training (CCT) or an equivalent approved indicator of training.

Could this be the next step in your career? Come and join one of the UK's leading mental health Trusts at the forefront of research infrastructure and make a real difference to people's lives.

This role provides senior medical input and clinical leadership to the Buckinghamshire Crisis Resolution and Home Treatment Team (CRHTT). You will have responsibility for your own patients as well as those patients seen by medical staff under your supervision.

The key components of the CRHTT service are:

1. Crisis response (emergency assessments and reviews)

2. Intensive home treatment characterized by the availability of multiple visits each day which are of a length and content to allow for specialist psycho-social intervention to be delivered

3. Gate-keeping admissions to psychiatric beds

4. Enabling early discharge from psychiatric admission

The CRHTT provide crisis response and inpatient gate-keeping and a home treatment service to service users leaving inpatient care and living within South Bucks. There will be a phased approach to future expansion which will be dependent on further new investment. The nature and speed of phasing will also take account of CRHTT model fidelity and assessment of safety and quality in relation to existing service provision (i.e. whatever is developed will have good fit and add value to user / care experience).

We'd welcome clinicians who want to help shape how general practice develops.

title: Advanced Heart Failure Clinical Fellow
locations: Cambridge Bio Medical Campus, United Kingdom
descriptionHtml:
This is a Clinical Fellowship in Advanced Heart Failure, Mechanical Circulatory Support (MCS) and Heart Transplantation. The post is available for one year, with a possibility of extension by mutual agreement.

This Fellowship post in the Transplant Unit at Royal Papworth Hospital provides an opportunity for a Cardiologist to receive sub-specialty training in the management of advanced heart failure, mechanical circulatory support and heart transplantation.

The post-holder will work with the six existing Transplant Cardiologists and one Health Education East of England rotating cardiology registrar as part of the wider Transplant Team. The post will provide experience and training in all aspects of inpatients and outpatient care of advanced heart failure and heart transplant patients.

Successful candidates in the role will receiving training opportunities on par with a UK trainee and the post-holder will have a trained and named educational supervisor, be mentored by the existing team with regular meetings and oversight by the whole team.

Informal visits can be arranged through Dr Pettit or Dr Bhagra.

The post-holder will be responsible to the Clinical Lead of the Transplant Unit and accountable to the Medical Director when undertaking the following duties:

1.Delivery of patient care under Consultant supervision, seeking advice or assistance as required according to level of experience.

2.To read and abide by the standard operating procedures of the Transplant unit.

3.Completion of accurate records, such as patient notes and discharge summaries.

4.Attendance at clinics, catheter labs, ward rounds and clinical meetings.

5.Undertaking procedures which will be directly or indirectly supervised as appropriate for level of experience.

6.Participation in clinical audit and research

7.Participation in regular timetabled teaching of other junior medical staff, students and non-medical staff.

8.Participation in training activities, maintaining portfolio and personal development plan.

9.Attendance at mandatory training.

10.Compliance with the policies and procedures of the Trust.

11.Adherence to the working pattern of the specialty and participating in the monitoring of hours as required by the Trust.

12.Notify the appropriate consultant if unavailable to attend work

13.Booking annual leave in accordance with the departmental arrangements and policies of Trust

Royal Papworth Hospital NHS Foundation Trust is the UK's leading heart and lung hospital, delivering care to more than 50,000 patients a year in its new state-of-the-art hospital in Cambridge. We perform the most heart and/or lung transplants in the UK and carried out the UK's first successful heart transplant in 1979. It also offers emergency heart attack treatment, sleep centre care and is one of just five centres nationally for those in severe respiratory failure.

Based on the Cambridge Biomedical Campus the largest centre of medical research and health science in Europe the Trust is at the heart of treatments of the future. Royal Papworth became the first hospital trust in the country to be rated outstanding in all five areas assessed by the Care Quality Commission - a rating it still holds today. The Trust holds its values of compassion, excellence & collaboration at its core, and all colleagues joining the team are expected to uphold these in their day-to-day roles & interactions. Royal Papworth is proud of its diverse workforce and encourages people to embrace their individuality.

The Trust values difference and welcomes all applications irrespective of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy & maternity, race, religion & belief, sex and sexual orientation. Providing they meet the minimum post criteria, applicants with disabilities will be offered an interview.

For a street view tour: https://royalpapworth.nhs.uk/virtual-tour

employer: Royal United Hospitals Bath NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Radiologist - Non-Vasc Interventional Radiology
descriptionHtml:
Applications are invited for a Consultant Radiologist to join a friendly, forward-thinking team of 30 Consultant Radiologists at the Royal United Hospital Bath.

This post is for a Consultant Radiologist with specialist interest in Non-Vascular Interventional Radiology (10 PAs).

This post will help meet the increase in demand for interventional and diagnostic radiology services and to help us establish and provide an interventional oncology service.

The post is full time but anyone wishing to work part time is also encouraged to apply. The post includes participation in the IR on-call rota (participation in the diagnostic on-call rota is optional). Home PACS links are available.

Candidates are encouraged to visit the hospital and can make arrangements through contacting the Clinical Lead: Dr Gary Cross (gary.cross@nhs.net) or Dr Joseph Keighley, Consultant Interventional Radiologist (joseph.keighley@nhs.net).

This is a replacement post following retirement for a substantive Consultant Interventional Radiologist.

The candidate must be able to provide a range of non-vascular interventional radiology procedures and ideally will be competent in haemorrhage control. This role also demands a good level of diagnostic radiology competence and another specialist area of interest is encouraged but not essential. The post holder will contribute to the general radiology work of the department in conjunction with the other radiologists all of whom perform regular sessions in general radiology.

The case mix in interventional radiology at the RUH predominantly comes from our busy Urology, Gastroenterology and Surgical departments and from a wide range of oncological services. Approximately 1300 IR procedures are performed per year. Specialist nurses and radiographers undertake some vascular access in addition to 3 established IR consultants. With this new appointment we will provide a 1:5 IR on call service (weekends 0800-1800 only) and our aim is to establish an interventional oncology practice providing thermal ablation and some elective embolisation. We have links with North Bristol NHS Trust who provide tertiary level IR services.

At the RUH we're proud to put people at the heart of what we do, working together as one team to make a difference for our patients, each other, and our community. No matter what your role is, we value everyone's contribution in supporting the exceptional, person-centred care we pride ourselves on.

We are committed to creating a compassionate and inclusive environment. This can be seen in our growing community of staff networks - celebrating successes and creating opportunities to listen and learn. We value our differences, champion kindness and civility, and truly believe that diversity makes us stronger.

A culture of learning, developing and innovating is the thread that runs throughout our whole organisation. We want to support you to thrive, taking your career to its full potential.

We value staff wellbeing, with a well-established programme of support. We believe in a holistic approach spanning all aspects of living a healthy life, including physical, emotional, spiritual and financial wellbeing. We've even got a pool!

We are committed to supporting you and hope you want to join our team. In the meantime, find out more about living and working the beautiful historic city of Bath, learn about our extensive package of staff benefits, and read about how we're providing healthcare fit for the future with the landmark Dyson Cancer Centre and our passion for research.

title: Consultant Oncoplastic Breast Surgeon
descriptionHtml:
An exciting opportunity has arisen for a Consultant Oncoplastic Breast Surgeon to join Somerset NHS Foundation Trust's county-wide breast service. Based primarily at Musgrove Park Hospital in Taunton, you will join a highly experienced multidisciplinary team delivering comprehensive breast care across Somerset. Clinical sessions at Yeovil District Hospital will be undertaken as required.

Working alongside consultant breast surgeons, breast radiologists, consultant radiographers, breast clinicians, advanced practitioners and specialist nurses, you will play a key role in delivering high-quality, patient-centred breast cancer and benign breast services.

The breadth of expertise within the team supports a truly patient-centred approach to care, fostering close multidisciplinary collaboration across the entire breast care pathway and providing an excellent environment for service development, innovation, education and professional growth.

This post offers an excellent opportunity to contribute to the continued development of an innovative and expanding oncoplastic and reconstructive breast surgery service. It offers a Monday to Friday working pattern with no on call commitment and it attracts a 10 PA per week job plan.

Applications are welcomed whether you are an experienced Breast Surgeon looking to relocate to the beautiful somerset countryside or a newly qualified Consultant who has or will be completing their CCT within the coming months.

  • Deliver expert assessment, treatment and surgical care for patients with symptomatic and screening detected breast disease.
  • Undertake outpatient activity, including one-stop, new diagnosis, reconstructive, surgical planning and postoperative clinics.
  • Undertake regular operating lists, providing oncoplastic and reconstructive procedures within the post holder's scope of competence.
  • Participate fully in breast multidisciplinary team meetings and support evidence-informed treatment decisions.
  • Work collaboratively across the multidisciplinary breast team and with oncology, pathology, genetics and tertiary services.
  • Provide clear and compassionate information to patients, supporting informed and shared decision making.
  • Maintain accurate clinical records and practise in accordance with professional standards, Trust policies and clinical governance requirements.
  • Contribute to service improvement programmes that enhance clinical outcomes, patient experience and staff experience.
  • Support innovative and sustainable models of breast care, aligned with evidence-informed practice and the needs of patients across Somerset.
  • Help develop the oncoplastic and reconstructive breast surgery service, including partial breast reconstruction and perforator flap techniques where appropriate.
  • Use clinical audit, quality improvement methods, service data and patient feedback to identify and deliver improvements.
  • Contribute to the development and review of clinical pathways, guidelines and standards.

At Somerset NHS Foundation Trust, we're committed to supporting our employees with a range of benefits designed to enhance your professional and personal life. We offer:

  • Flexible working options to help you balance work and life
  • NHS pension scheme for long-term financial security
  • Generous annual leave allowance to recharge and relax
  • A strong focus on career development to help you grow and achieve your potential

Additionally, you'll gain access to our Blue Light Card, unlocking exclusive discounts on shopping, dining, and leisure activities, as well as NHS-specific perks to support you both inside and outside of work.

We are proud to foster a diverse, skilled, and inclusive workforce, and we encourage applications from all backgrounds.

Why Somerset? Somerset offers the perfect blend of idyllic countryside, outstanding areas of natural beauty, and breathtaking coastlines, with vibrant cities like Bristol, Bath, and Exeter just a short drive away - and only two hours to London.

The region is home to excellent educational facilities, and with affordable housing compared to other parts of the country, it's a great place to build both your career and your future.

Somerset truly has it all - the peaceful countryside and cosmopolitan city life, with something for everyone to enjoy.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
We're looking for a motivated and experienced GP to join our friendly, multidisciplinary primary care team across the Hammersmith & Fulham Health Centres, based at Charing Cross Hospital and Hammersmith Hospital.

This is an exciting opportunity to become an integral part of a team committed to delivering high-quality, patient-centred care and continuously improving the services we provide to our local community.

As a Salaried GP, youll have the opportunity to use and develop your clinical skills while working closely with a wide range of healthcare professionals. Youll provide the full range of General Medical Services and play an important role in shaping and maintaining excellent standards of care across our Centres.

Were seeking a committed, enthusiastic and experienced GP with a broad range of clinical experience and skills.

The role is offered for a minimum of 6 sessions per week, providing an excellent opportunity for a GP looking for a rewarding role within a well-established primary care environment.

title: Salaried GP / GP Partner
descriptionHtml:
Due to recent retirements, were looking for enthusiastic list-holding GPs to join our friendly, relaxed and supportive, high earning dispensing practice in the heart of Cornwall.

We have an opportunity for a salaried GP or a GP with a view to partnership to work from 4 to 8 sessions a week.

The 3 sites are all dispensing practices, within a close proximity and within approx. 5 mins of the A30, this provides convenient road access from many parts of Cornwall. We are proud to be active members of both the well-regarded Arbennek PCN and the Cornwall Deep End Network. Through both of these partnerships and alongside the INT we have been able to develop innovative initiatives such as Community Hubs that helps address health inequalities and improve opportunities for our patients.

being a great place to work,

employer: Lancashire & South Cumbria NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Psychiatrist and Honorary Research Fellow, South Cumbria
descriptionHtml:
Consultant Psychiatrist (General Adult) and Honorary Research Fellow

We are excited to launch the recruitment to this new post, jointly developed by Lancashire and South Cumbria NHS Foundation Trust and the University of Cumbria. The post holder will spend 6 PAs per week working with the General Adult Home Based Treatment Team (HbTT), based in Kendal and 4 PAs working as an Honorary Research Fellow at The University of Cumbria as part of the Mental Health Leaders Award. This would be based at the Lancaster Campus of the University of Cumbria.

The contract for the clinical role with LSCft would be permanent. The Honorary Research Fellow element would be fixed term until the end of February 2029, since that is dependent on funding.

As part of the clinical role, the postholder would be expected to contribute to the out of hours On Call rota, for which additional remuneration would be paid.

The clinical element of the role would be with the well-established Kendal HbTT and you would work as part of a multi-disciplinary team (MDT) to provide a service for those living in the Kendal area. The main duties would involve outpatient clinics for both new referrals and ongoing reviews. You would be expected to lead the MDT and provide supervision to the Resident Doctors working with the team.

The University of Cumbria Mental Health Leaders Award (MHLA) is a £2.5mn NIHR funded research grant, aimed at building capacity and capability around applied mental health and inequalities research at the University of Cumbria. You will be contributing to the aim of the MHLA, to increase our understanding of what the research priorities around mental health and inequalities in Cumbria are, and develop the infrastructure to deliver this research. This part of the post will be based with the MHLA operational team at University's Lancaster Campus. You will be expected to be on site 1 day per week.

Applicants should hold full GMC registration and be included on the Specialist register of the GMC or they should be eligible for entry to the Specialist Register within 6 months of the interview date.

It is a requirement that applicants are Section 12 Approved at the time of commencing employment and have or are eligible to have Approved Clinician Status. Remuneration will be as set out in the terms of the New Consultant Contract according to previous experience.

The role:

At least 2.5 SPAs as standard for a full time post (we would be flexible in looking at enhancements to support other activities that support the wider ambitions of the Trust).

Excellent peer support group

Study leave budget of £3000 over 3 years or up to £5000 over 3 years for newly qualified Consultants

Opportunities to be a clinical supervisor

Relocation package available.

At our Trust, we're really keen to develop our Consultant workforce and nurture their areas of interest in a flexible way where possible. Come and have a chat with us about what your special interest or development area and build a suitable job plan with us. There are also opportunities to have a role in Digital Leadership if this is a passion for any of our Consultants.

Working within our Care Coordinator team, you will thrive in a fast-paced environment where no two days are the same. You will play a pivotal role in supporting patients to access the right services at the right time, helping to improve outcomes and patient experience across our network.

As a key member of the team, you will also act as an ambassador for the work of the PCN, helping to showcase our services, successes and community impact through social media and digital engagement. You will be the link between our teams, patients and wider stakeholders, promoting the valuable work taking place across the network and ensuring our achievements are shared with the communities we serve.

This is an exciting opportunity for someone who is proactive, organised and passionate about making a difference, with the ability to build strong relationships, adapt to changing priorities and contribute to the continued development of innovative primary care services.

Why join us?

Be part of a progressive and supportive PCN focused on improving patient care.

Work in a varied and dynamic role with opportunities to develop new skills.

Help shape and promote innovative services that make a real difference to local communities.

Join a team that values collaboration, creativity and continuous improvement.

This role offers the opportunity to be at the heart of Primary Care Network development, supporting projects that make a real difference to patients, practices and the wider community. With a varied workload and no two days the same, it is ideal for someone who enjoys building relationships and contributing to innovative healthcare services.

As a Care Coordinator, you will work with PCN leaders, practice teams and partner organisations to improve patient care and access to services. descriptionHtml:
Consultant Child and Adolescent Psychiatrist or Consultant Paediatrician with a Special Interest in Neurodevelopmental Disorders

This newly developed post is part of a substantial investment in the services offered to children and young people with neurodevelopmental disorders by Coventry and Warwickshire Partnership Trust (CWPT). The post holder will provide consultant input and leadership in a community setting as part of an all-age neurodevelopmental service.

The post holder's main objective would be to provide medical input to the neurodevelopment team who provide assessment and treatment for children and young people of school age with autistic spectrum disorders and ADHD. This will include completing assessments, providing consultation to other professionals, overseeing multidisciplinary treatment plans and appropriately prescribing medication if required.

In particular, they would be expected to assess complex cases such as:- where there is a significant risk of self-harm, harm to others or risk of neglect- where there is diagnostic uncertainty or complexity- where the interaction of potential illness and personality factors needs to be evaluated.

The post holder would be expected to see around 12 new patients a month and 48 follow up reviews per month. It is expected that this substantial new investment will address historical waiting lists for neurodevelopmental assessment.

title: Clinical Pharmacist
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking an enthusiastic, confident, patient-focused and practice based Clinical Pharmacist to become a valued member of our friendly, supportive practice team.

Ideally, you will bring previous General Practice experience with an IP qualification and a strong passion for delivering safe, high-quality, and effective care within primary care. This is an exciting chance to make a meaningful impact on patient care.

As a Clinical Pharmacist, you will work as an integral part of the multidisciplinary team, using your clinical expertise to optimise medicines, improve patient outcomes and promote the safe and effective use of medicines.

You will undertake structured medication reviews, support patients with long-term conditions, provide clinical advice to patients and colleagues, and contribute to medicines optimisation and quality improvement initiatives.

Although full time is preferable we can be flexible for the right candidate.

Undertake structured medication reviews and medicines optimisation to improve patient outcomes safety and adherence.

Provide clinical advice to GPs, nurses and the wider multidisciplinary team on prescribing and medicines-related issues.

Support the management of patients with long-term conditions, including medication review, monitoring and follow-up.

Identify and manage medication-related risks, including interactions, adverse effects, contraindications and inappropriate prescribing.

Support medicines reconciliation following hospital discharge and changes in care.

Provide patients with clear advice and counselling on their medicines, promoting adherence and shared decision-making.

Support safe, effective and cost-effective prescribing in line with NICE guidance, local formularies and practice policies.

Contribute to repeat prescribing, medicines safety, clinical audits, quality improvement and prescribing reviews.

Work collaboratively with community and hospital pharmacy teams and other healthcare professionals to ensure continuity of care.

Maintain accurate clinical records and comply with professional, legal, confidentiality and information governance requirements.

Participate in multidisciplinary meetings, clinical governance and service development.

Maintain professional competence through continuing professional development and work within GPhC standards

We are a progressive, friendly GP practice serving a diverse patient population. Our team includes GPs, Practice nurses, Specialist nurses (Respiratory, diabetes and family planning) HCAs, pharmacists, paramedics and administrative staff who work collaboratively to provide safe, effective, and holistic care. We value innovation, teamwork, and continuous improvement.

title: Salaried GP - Long Term Conditions
descriptionHtml:

  • Be confident managing both acute and long-term health conditions.
  • Possess strong communication and multidisciplinary working skills.
  • Be committed to maintaining high standards of patient care and clinical governance.

The ideal candidate will have worked with boarding communities in the past and be aware of The Medical Officers of Schools Association. (MOSA). Professional experience providing primary healthcare to children and young adults is essential.

Please note: This vacancy is for 6 sessions per week

Working within the East Northants Neighbourhood Team, you will provide high-quality clinical care while championing personalised care planning and shared decision-making. You will work collaboratively with a range of healthcare professionals to improve patient outcomes, enhance quality of life, and support individuals to manage their health effectively.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Delivering comprehensive Long-Term Condition (LTC) reviews and supporting achievement of QOF targets.
  • Developing and maintaining high-quality, personalised care plans tailored to patients' individual needs and goals.
