On 1 October 26, Cowes Medical Centre and Newport Health Centre formally merged under a single partnership structure. Whilst both practices continue to operate under separate GMS contracts, responsibility for the overall management and delivery of services now sits with one partnership. This development presents an exciting opportunity to bring together the knowledge, skills, and experience that exist across both sites, whilst retaining the strengths and local identity of each practice.

The merger creates a platform for greater collaboration, shared learning, and more consistent ways of working across teams. By combining expertise and aligning processes, the practices can build on existing successes, improve resilience, enhance patient services, and create a more integrated approach to care.

We have a diverse, multi-disciplinary team which includes GP Partners, Advanced Nurse Practitioners, Paramedics, MSK Practitioners, Mental Health Practitioners, Practice Nurses, HCAs, Chronic Pain Coach, Care Coordinators, a Social Prescriber and many more vital roles to support our community.

We pride ourselves on a strong ethos of education, training, teamwork, and high-quality, patient-centred care and of course an enviable Island lifestyle that comes with living on the Isle of Wight (sea views optional but highly recommended)

We offer competitive pay, flexible sessions to fit around real life, protected CPD, and a genuine work-life balance.

employer: Kingston and Richmond NHS Foundation Trust
title: Specialty Doctor in ENT
descriptionHtml:
We are looking to appoint an innovative and high performing individual to join our well-established and progressive Ear, Nose and Throat Department at Kingston Hospital of Kingston and Richmond NHS Foundation Trust.

The successful candidate would complement a department of multi-disciplinary professionals, (including advanced audiologist practitioners and voice therapists), who collectively deliver acute and elective ENT services, both general and subspecialty, for all disciplines. The service is delivered as part of the Southwest London clinical network, and we have close links with St George's Hospital and Royal Marsden Hospital where patients receive cancer treatment.

We also run ENT clinics at Queen Mary's Hospital and Cobham Day Surgery Hospital. Our Audiology department is fully accredited by UKAS under the IQIPS version 2 standard.

A comprehensive clinical service is provided for the management and treatment of a wide range of diseases and disorders of hearing, balance, voice, swallowing, smell and taste. Our multidisciplinary service is delivered as part of an integrated care network covering South West London and Surrey.

Aspen Building, which is a purpose-built outpatient unit at Kingston Hospital provides six examination and interventional procedure rooms, co-located radiology and histopathology clinics for same day FNAs, voice therapy and a full paediatric and adult audiology suite together with associated office and staff facilities.

Queen Mary's Hospital offers four outpatient consultation and procedure rooms, two audiology consultation and procedure rooms, three sound proofed test booths, an Otoneurology assessment room and hearing aid store.

employer: Dorset HealthCare University NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant in Learning Disabilities for Ferndown and Purbeck
descriptionHtml:
This is an exciting opportunity to join our service as a part-time (6 PA) Consultant Psychiatrist in Learning Disability Psychiatry, as part of the reconfiguration of Psychiatry of Intellectual Disability (Learning Disability) provision within the Community Learning Disability Teams in Dorset.

As the consultant psychiatrist you'll provide a community psychiatry service for adults with learning disabilities across the Purbeck and Ferndown areas. The role does not include epilepsy management, which is provided by the specialist Dorset Epilepsy Service within the Neurology service.

You will be supported by experienced colleagues in Learning Disability Psychiatry and will work as part of a well-established, integrated Community Learning Disability Team, with additional support from the Intensive Support Team. You'll contribute to weekly IST review meetings and the wider development of community-based Learning Disability services.

This is an excellent opportunity to contribute to the ongoing development of community-based Learning Disability services, working collaboratively with a skilled multidisciplinary team to deliver high-quality, person-centred care to adults with learning disabilities across Dorset.

You'll provide psychiatric leadership, assessment, diagnosis and treatment for adults with learning disabilities, alongside psychiatric input to patients supported by the IST. Clinical work will be a combination of clinics and home visits. The role includes medical cross-cover for annual, study and emergency sick leave with Consultant colleagues across the adult Learning Disability service.

We offer a £10,000 Recruitment & Retention Payment, paid monthly during your first year in post, alongside a relocation package of up to £10,000 if you are relocating to Dorset. You'll also benefit from flexible working, excellent NHS benefits, 10 days' study leave and an annual study budget of up to £1,000 - supporting you both professionally and personally.

You'll be offered the opportunity to participate in the county-wide senior on-call rota, which attracts a 3% on call availability supplement plus 0.75 APA per week. The on-call frequency is approximately 1 in 21.

Interested in finding out more? We'd love to hear from you. Contact Dr Cressida Manning, Medical Lead for Specialist Services at cressida.manning@nhs.net for an informal conversation about the opportunity.

At Dorset HealthCare we're on a mission to empower people to make the most of their lives through our outstanding, joined-up healthcare services. We're a dynamic, forward-looking Trust, running 12 community hospitals, specialist inpatient facilities and a wide range of integrated community and mental health services for a population of almost 800,000 people.

We do things differently here - it's one of the reasons the CQC rated us 'outstanding' in 2019. It's also why 95% of patients across our services say they have a good or very good experience of our services and 89% of staff feel they can really make a difference. Whether you're looking to work with us in one of our bustling market towns, vibrant urban locations, thriving seaside spots, or among the rolling hills of Dorset, there are lots of ways you can make a difference in our communities.

Our 7,000-strong workforce is at the heart of what we do and our success is a testament to our brilliant people. We're all about building a workplace for the future, we believe in equal opportunities and we celebrate diversity. We're an inclusive workplace, where everyone is welcome, everyone can be authentic, and we are all encouraged to be the best version of ourselves.

Working with us you'll be part of a strong team, challenge yourself, build a career, and teach us what we don't know. And you'll be working towards our vision to be better every day through excellence, compassion and expertise in all we do.

title: PCN Frailty GP
descriptionHtml:
We have a fantastic opportunity for an experienced and motivated GP to join Folkestone, Hythe & Rural Primary Care Network as a Frailty GP.

We are an ambitious, innovative and forward-thinking PCN, recognised as being at the forefront of Integrated Neighbourhood Working across Kent and Medway.

Having been part of the national Neighbourhood Health Implementation Programme (NNHIP) pilot, we are helping to shape the future of neighbourhood healthcare.

This is a very exciting opportunity to join a progressive and dynamic environment, working within our established Integrated Neighbourhood Team to deliver a more proactive, responsive and joined-up approach to caring for patients living with frailty and complex needs.

We are looking for a GP who shares our ambition and enthusiasm for developing new ways of working.

Previous experience in frailty care would be highly desirable, although not essential.

Above all, we are seeking someone who is enthusiastic about integrated working and wants to play a key role in shaping the future of neighbourhood healthcare.

The post holder will act as a clinical leader for our established Integrated Neighbourhood Team, providing senior clinical leadership, oversight and guidance to a dynamic multidisciplinary team of clinicians and healthcare professionals.

The team delivers a combination of proactive and reactive care, supporting patients living with frailty, complex health needs and those at risk of deterioration or hospital admission.

The GP will play a key role in supporting clinical decision-making, managing complexity and ensuring a coordinated, patient-centred approach to care.

The role will involve working closely with a diverse range of professionals across neighbourhood services, providing clinical leadership and contributing to multidisciplinary discussions and care planning.

An important aspect of the role will be helping to lead and develop our innovative neighbourhood model, supporting new ways of working and shaping the future delivery of integrated care across our PCN.

Folkestone, Hythe & Rural Primary Care Network brings together seven GP practices serving a population of approximately 50,000 patients across a mixture of rural and urban communities.

Our member practices are Oaklands Health Centre, White House Surgery, Harbour Medical Practice, New Lyminge Surgery, Church Road Surgery, Sun Lane Surgery and Hawkinge and Elham Valley Practice.

Our population is diverse, covering communities with areas of significant deprivation alongside a high proportion of older patients and people living with frailty, multimorbidity and complex health needs.

We are an ambitious, progressive and forward-thinking organisation with a strong reputation for innovation, collaboration and developing new approaches to care.

Having participated in the national Neighbourhood Health Implementation Programme pilot, we have been at the forefront of Integrated Neighbourhood Working across Kent and Medway.

We have developed an established Integrated Neighbourhood Team, bringing together professionals from primary care, community health and wider partners to deliver more joined-up, proactive and responsive care.

We pride ourselves on creating a supportive and inclusive working environment where staff are valued, encouraged to contribute ideas and actively involved in service development.

This is an exciting time to join our PCN as we continue to build on our achievements and help shape the future of neighbourhood healthcare.

title: Rehabilitation Medicine Consultant
descriptionHtml:
This is a replacement post which provides an opportunity for a committed and flexible individual to join the current consultants in developing specialist rehabilitation services in Portsmouth and South East Hampshire and to evolve and adapt along with the service. The post is for a full time Consultant in Rehabilitation Medicine and applications for those wishing to work on a less than full time basis would also be welcome.

The Lotus Rehabilitation Centre relaunched in December 2021 after NHS England approved funding for a new modular 2-storey block to be built on the Queen Alexandra Hospital Site, Portsmouth. Located adjacent to the current Rehabilitation block (which houses therapy services and the hydrotherapy pool), the ground floor provides a modern, air-conditioned 26-bed rehabilitation environment for both the Rehabilitation Medicine and Stroke Rehabilitation services (13 beds each). The centre contains 2 rehab gyms, a meeting room, patient social space as well as private access to outdoor rehabilitation and garden space. There is a bridge link to the main hospital, with easy access to other medical specialty services and imaging services.

In addition to inpatient rehabilitation, the service also provides Rehabilitation Medicine outpatient clinics, including a specialist spasticity service. The clinics are based at St Marys health care campus, Portsea Island. The service works in partnership with Steepers to provide consultant sessions at the dedicated Murrison accredited regional prosthetic services based at Portsmouth Enablement Centre, St Marys health care campus, Portsea Island.

The appointee will work closely with the other 2 Consultants in Rehabilitation Medicine in providing comprehensive Rehabilitation Medicine services in Portsmouth serving the regional footprint as well as improving, strengthening and developing specialist services. The post offers opportunities to include elements of acute outreach, inpatient and outpatient Neurorehabilitation, paediatric to adult transition clinics and Prosthetic Rehabilitation services subject to interests and negotiation. Opportunities also exist to contribute to Rehabilitation ongoing and future service development and governance; Educational Supervision; and Departmental and Care Group leadership roles. The service is part of the Wessex Trauma Network and there are additional opportunities to be involved with this as well as opportunities for the appointee to develop a research portfolio if desired, or to collaborate academically with the University of Portsmouth and Kings College in delivering the newly established Medical Degree Programme.

Here at Portsmouth Hospitals University NHS Trust, we are proud to provide expert, compassionate care for our local population. We are ranked as the third in the country for research, embedding education and training across the organisation. Our main hub is the Queen Alexandra Hospital, which is one of the largest hospitals on the south coast employing over 8,700 staff.

Our patients come from all walks of life and so do we. We hire great people from a wide variety of backgrounds because it makes our hospital stronger. If you share our values and our enthusiasm for getting it right for patients, colleagues, and our community, you will find a home at Portsmouth Hospitals University NHS Trust.

employer: Wrightington Wigan & Leigh Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant in Elderly Care Medicine
descriptionHtml:
Now is a really exciting time to Join our Team of forward-thinking Ageing & Complex Medicine (Elderly Medicine) Consultants at Wrightington Wigan and Leigh (WWL) NHS Foundation Trust, and make a real difference to our elderly patients in the Wigan Borough.

Here at WWL we put the patient at the heart of everything we do, as we strive to deliver and develop our modern and comprehensive Elderly Care service. On-Call

employer: Countess of Chester Hospital NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant in Plastic & Reconstructive Surgery
descriptionHtml:
Working Full time: 10 sessions per week

An exciting opportunity has arisen for a full-time consultant in Plastic & Reconstructive surgery to join our expanding department in the beautiful city of Chester. This role is predominantly to aid with a surge in demand of skin cancer referrals as well as supporting general plastic services. The successful candidate will be expected to have an interest in general plastic surgery with a large proportion of skin cancer cases making up the bulk of elective work. The post also involves some orthoplastic support for lower limb cases in Oswestry as well as locally.

Permanent and locum applications will be considered.

Duties and Responsibilities

The appointee will be responsible for the care of patients referred by general practitioners, other hospital departments and will undertake clinics, ward rounds and theatre lists. 'Programmed Activities' as appropriate. The job plan will be a 10PA job plan which will be agreed in discussion between the successful candidate, the Lead Clinician in Plastic Surgery, and with Planned Care operational management team. This will be subject to Annual Review.

Total 'Programmed activities'= 10

On-Call Commitment

The appointee will be expected to participate in a 1 in 4 on call service. This is currently under review and subject to change. Consultant on call from home, generally for telephone advice for junior doctors.

The Trust's services are provided from three locations: o The Countess of Chester Hospital: providing 473 general and acute beds. o Ellesmere Port Hospital: providing 60 beds as a rehabilitation, intermediate and outpatient facility. o Tarporley War Memorial Hospital: a base for community services which serve the local rural population. The Countess of Chester Hospital NHS Foundation Trust employs 5,964 staff (headcount) to provide care and treatment to a population of over 400,000 people living in Chester and West Cheshire which includes Ellesmere Port and Neston as well as the Deeside area of Flintshire. The Trust works collaboratively within the wider Cheshire and Merseyside Integrated Care System. Due to its location on the border with North Wales, the Trust also works closely with the Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board. The Trust treats patients from England and some parts of Wales. During 2024/2025, there were approximately 643,000 patient attendances (inpatient, A&E, outpatient and diagnostic) ranging from a simple outpatient appointment to major cancer surgery

employer: University Hospitals Sussex NHS Foundation Trust (279)
title: Consultant Rheumatologist
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking to appoint a substantive Consultant Rheumatologist. The appointee will work with Consultant colleagues to provide a comprehensive service for residents across West Sussex. The Rheumatology department is part of the MSK Directorate including Trauma and Orthopaedics and Pain Management. The post will be based predominantly at Worthing and Southlands Hospitals. However there will be some sessions at other Trust locations if and when required.

The post offers an excellent opportunity for you to develop as a Consultant and also contribute to service development.

  • Outpatient clinics: assessment of all new patients at their first appointment; review of follow-up patients; discussion and review of follow-up patients seen by Speciality Doctors and clinical nurse specialists (CNS); joint injections and other procedures.

There will be a commitment to supporting the education of medical students from Brighton (BSMS) in their placements, and the potential to develop managerial and research interests. There are strong links to the KSS Deanery and Brighton & Sussex Medical School.

Working for our organisation

At UHSussex, diversity is our strength, and we want you to feel included to help us always deliver Excellent Care Everywhere, as shown in our Outstanding for Caring CQC rating. Your uniqueness and experiences will be part of our creative and innovative community where everyone is encouraged to succeed. We have a range of staff networks to help break down barriers, and can offer abuddy to help new members settle in. title: CAMHS Consultant Psychiatrist, Coastal Community & Liaison (£45k RRP)
descriptionHtml:
This is an exciting opportunity for a Consultant Psychiatrist to join our Coastal Community CAMHS Team in Worthing providing leadership to deliver high-quality, person-centred care to Children and Young People.

You will work as part of a friendly and supportive multidisciplinary team which includes nurses, psychologists, systemic family therapists and child psychotherapists. This post will work alongside other Consultants and Specialty Doctors who work in Sussex CAMHS. You will also be part of a Trust wide Consultant network where there are opportunities to liaise with colleagues in other posts throughout the Trust and develop peer networks.

This is an established post. The post became available due to vacancy.

This job attracts a Recruitment and Retention payment of £45,000 (pro-rata for part time staff) structured over a three-year period as follows:o£15,000 payable upon successful recruitmento£10,000 payable at 12 months' serviceo£10,000 payable at 24 months' serviceo£10,000 payable at 36 months' service

The service we provide is in line with NICE Evidenced Based Treatment for those children and young people. You will provide high quality specialist clinical assessments, including relevant psychiatric and physical investigation to children, young people and their families in a range of settings, and work collaboratively with other members of the team to plan and deliver appropriate individually tailored treatment plans.

  • To provide medical psychiatric assessment and intervention, including pharmacology and mental health act assessments to CAMHS in Coastal West Sussex ( Chichester and Worthing Bases ) ensuring best quality and most effective psychiatric care, working within a multi-disciplinary team.
  • To work as part of the multi-professional team providing high quality specialist CAMHS clinical advice, assessment and intervention to children and young people in the area in a range of settings.
  • To engage families/carers in planning and provision of care.
  • To provide timely advice and consultation to GP's, social services and other referrers, facilitating appropriate access to services.

You will have the opportunity to make a real difference to improve the lives of children and adolescents, working with colleagues in the team to provide a full range of outpatient and inpatient services and helping to manage transition between these and other services through outreach services.

You will be joining a Trust rated 'Good' by the CQC and 'Outstanding' for caring, with a strong commitment to innovation, research, and continuous improvement.

At Sussex Partnership we are committed to providing opportunities for flexible working. If you would like to work differently or different hours to as advertised, please get in touch to discuss this in more detail.

employer: Harrogate and District NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant in T&O (Special interest in Hand & Wrist Surgery)
descriptionHtml:
Applications are invited for a Substantive Trauma and Orthopaedic Consultant with a special interest in Hand and Wrist Surgery at Harrogate and District NHS Foundation Trust.

The successful applicant will join the Trauma and Orthopaedic Department which comprises of 12 substantive consultants and a multi-disciplinary team including 4 Specialty Doctors, 4 Fellows, 2 Specialty trainees, 7 trainees on first on call rota.

employer: Greater Manchester Mental Health NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Psychiatrist - Bolton CMHT
descriptionHtml:
Bolton Community mental health teams (CMHTs) provide multi-disciplinary assessment, treatment, and care of individuals with severe and enduring mental health problems.

They service is available to residents of Bolton, aged 16 to 70 years, with a diagnosed functional mental health problem. This typically includes service users with:

  • Schizophrenia,
  • Severe Affective Disorder,
  • Complex Personality Disorder
  • Autism Spectrum Conditions
  • ADHD

Bolton operates a sectorised service. The sectors are defined by GP practice populations within the boundaries of the borough.

The South Sector post covers a population served by GP practices based at Stone hill, Level Chamber 1, Pikes lane, Orient House, Deane Clinic, Wyresdale, St Helen's Road, Peter House and Stable Fold Surgery. The sectors are reviewed in line with the changing profile of population and reflects the deprivation, referral patterns and throughput to ensure equitability among the four General Adult Community Consultants.

A full list of GPs and referral patterns are available.

The under 16 population is 60,000 and the over 65 population 40,000. The nominal catchment population therefore for each of the six General Adult Psychiatrists is just under 30,000.

The post holder will be based at the Barnett House, Community Mental Health Team on Weston Street, Bolton, where the other General Adult Community Psychiatrists are also based. He or she will be given an unshared office with a PC and fulltime secretarial support and is also to be supported by a full-time Core Trainee.

Greater Manchester Mental Health (GMMH) Foundation Trust employs over 7000 members of staff, who deliver services from more than 122 locations.

We provide inpatient and community-based mental health care for people living in Bolton, the city of Manchester, Salford, Trafford and the borough of Wigan, and a wide range of specialist mental health and substance misuse services across Greater Manchester, the north west of England and beyond.

Greater Manchester is one of the world's most innovative, original and exciting places to live and work. From the beauty of the surrounding countryside to the heart of the vibrant inner city with great shopping, entertainment and dining options.

Wherever you go you will experience a great northern welcome with people famed for their warmth, humour and generosity.

Our people enjoy their work, have opportunities to learn and develop their skills and are encouraged to generate new ideas that improve care for our service users.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
Streatfield Health Centre is looking to recruit Salaried GP for three to four sessions per week.

We are a friendly, forward-thinking and enthusiastic practice caring for approximately 7800 patients.The ideal candidate will be at least three years post-qualification and will share our commitment to delivering high-quality, person-centred care within a supportive and progressive practice environment.

employer: University Hospitals of Derby and Burton NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Hepatologist
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for a dynamic and enthusiastic Hepatologist to join our University of Derby and Burton Hospitals (UHDB) team of 6 Hepatology consultants and 8 specialist nurses.

The successful candidate will also work closely with our 14 luminal gastroenterologists in providing a 24/7 gastroenterology and liver service including a daily inpatient endoscopy list and endoscopy nurse supported out of hours GI bleed service.

This is a full-time position, but candidates wishing to work part-time or in a job-share are encouraged to apply. If a part-time or job-share person is appointed modification of the job content will be discussed with the appointee on a personal basis. Informal visits are welcomed.

Hepatology services are primarily based at the Royal Derby Hospital site, which is a level 2 liver centre. In 2023, the service achieved level 2 (full) IQILS (Improving Quality of Liver Services) accreditation. The assessment team highlighted several areas of excellence in the service. The unit is a tertiary referral centre for PTC and TIPSS and works closely with the Liver transplant unit in Birmingham in caring for patients pre and post liver transplantation.

Luminal and Hepatology services are provided on 2 separate dedicated wards at Royal Derby Hospital (RDH) and on 1 ward at Queens Hospital Burton (QHB). At RDH the Hepatology service is supported by 8 Clinical Nurse Specialists including 2 Viral Hepatitis, 2 Hepatology, and 4 HPB cancer nurse Specialists, together with alcohol liaison service. We have excellent endoscopy facilities which are all JAG accredited this includes a 3-room endoscopy suite at QHB and a 2-room endoscopy suite at SRP. We participate in the national bowel cancer screening programme across the Acute Hospitals.

As a trusted organisation at the heart of our communities, we recognise the important role we can play in supporting the public, patients, our own people and local partners in achieving the best of health for the local population and the communities in which they live by providing Exceptional Care Together

employer: Mersey and West Lancashire Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust

descriptionHtml:
The post is for a substantive Consultant in Plastic Surgery with a Skin Cancer and Mohs and Surgery interest.

This is an exciting opportunity for a highly motivated surgeon to join a dynamic, rapidly expanding team delivering multidisciplinary care within the Mersey Regional Burns and Plastic Surgery unit based at Mersey and West Lancashire Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust. The appointee will be expected to ensure their clinical service is in accordance with the principles of Clinical Governance which must include appropriate clinical audit, clinical targets, key performance indicators (KPI's), evidence-based practice, continued personal educational and professional development. Acute Care

title: Practitioner Psychologist (Preceptorship)
descriptionHtml:

Change Grow Live will enable you to further develop your skills and provide ongoing opportunities for professional development.

Location covering a service/s Blackpool

employer: University Hospitals of Derby and Burton NHS Foundation Trust

descriptionHtml:
University Hospitals of Derby and Burton NHS Foundation Trust is looking to recruit a Consultant UGI Surgeon, with special interest in Upper Cancer surgery.

Based at the Royal Derby Hospital the UGI department provides a full range of out-patient diagnostic services and inpatient elective operating services for benign, bariatric and malignant disease as well as outpatient clinics and day case sessions. The department has access to a 9 theatre inpatient suite and a 3 theatre Day Case facility. The inpatient theatre suite boasts two fully integrated laparoscopic theatres and the Trust offers Da Vinci Robotic cancer surgery in urology, colorectal, head and neck and UGI/HPB.

This post will be based across Royal Derby Hospital and with clinical activity also delivered at community sites across Derbyshire. employer: Sherwood Forest Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust

descriptionHtml:

title: GP Womens Health - Menopause Care
descriptionHtml:
An exciting to join the Berkshire West Women's Health Hub as part of our innovative and Community Gynaecology Service.

We are ideally looking for GP's who have Advanced BMS/CoSRH Certificate in Menopause Care.

We are looking for enthusiastic and experienced General Practitioners with significant experience and passion for Women's Health who wish to develop advanced knowledge and practical skills within a supportive, multidisciplinary team.

Working alongside experienced GPwERs, Community Gynaecologists, and collaborative partnership, you will deliver high-quality, evidence-based care closer to home whilst helping transform women's healthcare across Berkshire West.

We have multiple roles available, ideally we are looking for Salaried GP's however we will consider locums.

An exciting opportunity to provide specialist assessment and management of women referred into the Berkshire West Women's Health Hub, delivering high-quality, patient-centred care within agreed clinical pathways whilst further developing your specialist skills, through a structured and supportive environment for professional growth.

Responsibilities include:

  • A mix of triage, virtual and face to face consultations
  • Assessment, diagnosis and management of a wide range of benign gynaecological conditions within the Community Gynaecology Service.
  • Independent management of patients within agreed competency levels.
  • Performing community-based gynaecological procedures appropriate to training and competence such as
  • Removal of lost IUS
  • Difficult insertion of IUS
  • Cervical polypectomy
  • Assess and manage incontinence and prolapse symptoms including vaginal pessary
  • Cervical cautery
  • Participation in MDT and other clinical meetings where appropriate.
  • Contributing to clinical governance, audit, teaching and service improvement initiatives and ensure service is complaint with CQC legislation.
  • Supporting delivery of Berkshire West Women's Health pathways and promoting consistent evidence-based care across Primary Care.

The Primary Care Alliance is a primary care provider collaborative. We have 36 general practice members. The Alliance became a Community Interest Company in 2026.

Our mission

  • Our mission is to support and sustain the practice ownership model. We seek to do this through:
  • Acting as a united face of primary care across Berkshire West.
  • Supporting the collaboration of members whilst preserving local identity.
  • Giving members access to skills and capabilities they could not access by working alone.
  • Contracting for services that need to be provided at scale.

We are not:

  • Commissioners of health care services. We bid for services we think would best be provided through our primary care partners.
  • Legal or contractual representatives of general practices, these are the respective roles of the Local Medical Committee and the Integrated Care Board.
  • Competitors with practices and PCNs. If a component of primary healthcare is to be commissioned and is most appropriately delivered at practice or neighbourhood level then we are quite clear that the GP practice is sovereign, and in its turn, the PCN.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for an enthusiastic and dedicated Salaried GP for our two partners and three salaried GP practice in Brentford. We are looking for someone to join our team for 4 sessions, Tuesday all day and Thursday all day. We run a total triage appointment system.

Currently, our practice is fully staffed by a friendly and caring team who work together to provide excellent patient care. We have a team of skilled professionals consisting of 5 GPs, 1 ANP, 1 nurse, 2 HCAs, 1 pharmacist, and a pharmacist technician.

Our list size is about 8100 with an interesting mixed demographic. We are active within our PCN and our PCN staff consists of pharmacists, first contact physio, a social prescriber, mental health advisor, a paramedic and a diabetes specialist.

We are rated Good by CQC and we use SystmOne. We value best practice, support one another, and focus on professional development and flexibility for our staff. We have several meetings including clinical and practice meetings. We encourage progress in leadership and special interests.

Informal visits or discussions with GP partners are welcome.

The appointed Salaried GP will provide medical services for the practice population to a high standard, including day-to-day activities such as Online triage and advice, face-to-face consultations, telephone consultations, Home visits, checking and signing off electronic prescriptions, processing test results, scanning and appropriate administration to ensure accurate records, patient continuity and quality care.

We are within a purpose-built health centre with good facilities, including spacious and air-conditioned clinical rooms, a free staff car park and bicycle parking. The surgery is located opposite Brentford train station, near Kew and Brentford High Street. This is a supportive environment in which a salaried GP can develop special interests and engage with a wide range of services.

title: Locum Consultant Haematologist
descriptionHtml:
The post is for a consultant Haematologist on a fixed term on a 12 months contract and will be based at University Hospital Lewisham (UHL).

The successful applicant will have the opportunity to help develop a high-quality service in this busy district general hospital, delivering comprehensive Haemoglobinopathy, Haemato-Oncology, General Haematology & Laboratory Haematology services.

The trust is in the process of operationalising a number of exciting service transformations, such as an Emergency Department Bypass Unit to improve the outcomes and experiences of our patients with sickle cell. The department is also exploring opportunities for the expansion of our treatment capacity for malignant and non-malignant haematology and is in the process of developing a strategy to adopt innovative ways of working. The postholder will have the opportunity to contribute to the clinical leadership of these exciting developments.

This role will be delivered as whole-time equivalent amounting to 10 programmed activities per week, subject to job plan review. Any applicant who is unable for personal reasons, to work full-time will be eligible to be considered for the post. If such a person is appointed, modification of the job content will be discussed on a personal basis with the Trust in consultation with consultant colleagues.

The appointee will be based at UHL to provide a General Haematology service as well as Haem- Malignancy service. Interest in Haemoglobinopathy will be welcomed

The general Haematology workload includes providing full haematological support to all patients treated at Lewisham and Greenwich NHS Trust, GPs and the local Mental Health Trust (Oxleas). The population served is approximately 800,000. Traditionally the Haematologists have had good working links with the GPs and have provided a direct consultative service for interpretation of haematological tests and clinical problems. Anticoagulation services are partially moving into the community.

The post holder is expected to take an equal share in the delivery inpatient haematology services including Level 2B, laboratory haematology workload including blood film, bone marrow and Transfusion Management.

The post holder may be required to undertake other duties appropriate for a Consultant Haematologist not otherwise specified.

title: Locum Consultant Psychiatrist in Substance Misuse
descriptionHtml:
The post will be based in the community between the Two West teams. The exact breakdown of cover and location can of work can be agreed depending on the preference of the candidate and their area of residence.

The post will provide medical support to the community teams on a full-time basis working closely with the current SAS and Specialist doctors.

The post holder will be encouraged to obtain and maintain section 12(2) approval of the Mental Health Act 1983 (2007) and Approved Clinician status in Wales in order to participate in the on call rota for MHLD and to undertake assessments in the community, police custody, 136 suites.

title: Speciality Doctor Child and Adolescent Psychiatry Interventions Team
descriptionHtml:
Applications are invited for a Specialty Doctor post to support the delivery of care within the Emotional Wellbeing and Mental Health Care Group for under 18s in Cardiff and Vale.

The Emotional Wellbeing and Mental Health Care Group is driving forward the transformational agenda for CAMH services in Wales with the development of existing services in line with the new Mental Health strategy and stepped care model.

Our new colleague will be an enthusiastic and committed psychiatrist with an interest in service development and with a strong desire to help service users and families.

Working alongside the teams, you will provide specialist psychiatric assessment and management to contribute to formulation and diagnosis, and the delivery of care.

As a psychiatrist, you will have experience and knowledge in carrying a service user caseload, including assessing service users with complex needs, and supporting families with care planning.

Care co-ordination, consultation, supervision and supporting other members of the multi-disciplinary team will be key aspects of the role, as well as partnership working with health, education and social care. The post holder will be supported in this role by a Consultant Child Psychiatrist and with appropriate areas of skill that require development and further training.

This is a 0.5 WTE - 5 session permanent post within the EWMH interventions team

Our Single Point of Access (SPOA) manages queries, advice, consultation and the referral process into our services. This model has reduced the number of referrals through providing accessible signposting and advice to both families and professionals. Contacts with SPOA result in a monthly average of circa 200 young people and families being offered a Choice appointment with our core assessment team. Referrals identified as specifically relating to an eating disorder (ED) at SPOA are assessed within the multidisciplinary ED clinic.

The Post Holder will work in the Core Interventions team (previously generic CAMHS) providing Part 1 & Part 2 work under the Mental Health Measure (Wales 2010)

The Main responsibilities of the post:

psychiatric assessment and intervention including pharmacological treatment and Mental Health Act Assessments within the Core Intervention Team

Involvement in prescription rota (depending on working days)

Involvement in Peer Group

Support teaching to medical students and other staff

Maintain CPD

No out of hours duties.

The Consultant Psychiatrists in the Core Intervention Team provide consultation sessions for the wider service to provide advice, manage any necessary medical investigations and identify when and how young people require direct psychiatric input which may result in allocation to partnership work or the offer of one-off joint appointment.

Cardiff and Vale University Health Board is one of the largest Integrated Health Boards in the UK, employing over 17,000 staff, providing over 100 specialist services. Working across 6 hospital sites, we have a diverse range of career opportunities to offer. Serving over 500,000 people living in Cardiff and the Vale, we are focussed on the health and care needs of our local population whilst working with our partners to develop regional services. Together we are committed to improving health outcomes for everyone, delivering excellent care and support.

Our mission is "Living Well, Caring Well, Working Together", and our vision is that every person's chance of leading a healthy life should be equal. Our 10-year transformation and improvement strategy, Shaping Our Future Wellbeing, is our chance to work collaboratively with the public and our workforce to make our health board more sustainable for the future.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
An exciting opportunity has arisen for a Salaried GP to join the Team for 5 sessions per week.

We are an established training practice for GP registrars and medical students with a practice list size of 11,000 patients. We work out of privately-owned premises.

We are a dispensing practice, use Systmone and achieve high QOF scores.

Barnard Castle lies in the rural beauty of Teesdale, being 1 hour drive to the Lake District and 30 minutes from Darlington, with rail connections to London or Edinburgh in around 2 hours.

We are the largest practice in our innovative and effective Primary Care Network and are part of Durham Dales Health Federation.

The post holder will be expected to undertake all the normal duties and responsibilities associated with a GP working within Primary Care.

In accordance with the Practice timetable, the post holder will make themselves available to undertake a variety of duties including both face to face and telephone consultations and home visits as well as dealing with administration work including prescriptions, results, letters and reports. Timetable includes outside appointments at local Community Hospital.

We promote continuity of care with a usual GP system.

The practice endeavours to provide top quality primary care to patients in a courteous and professional manner.

We are the sole practice in the pleasant market town of Barnard Castle with 6 Partners, 3 Salaried GP's, 3 ACP's, supported by an excellent practice nursing, administration and pharmacy team.

We have a culture of openness and continuous learning and improvement.

We are supportive of clinician's interests and the development of portfolio careers.

We have weekly clinical meetings and clinicians meet daily at coffee time.

13 patients in a standard surgery with 15-minute appointments.

Low number of house visits, which are supported by community paramedics.

Integrated clinical pharmacists, active care coordinator and social prescribers and practice based mental health practitioners.

Very well organised and efficient with a stable clinical and administration team.

An administration sub-team scan and code incoming letters and arrange medication changes and follow up tests.

title: PCN Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
North East Ipswich PCN is looking to welcome a PCN Salaried GP to the team based solely at their Felixstowe Road Medical Practice. This position is offered on 4 sessions per week. Working as part of our multidisciplinary team, you will have the opportunity to support and care for a diverse patient group. The role will include all general duties and responsibilities associated with a GP working within primary care.

  • Undertaking a variety of duties including surgery consultations, telephone consultations and queries, visiting patients at home, checking and signing repeat prescriptions and dealing with queries, paperwork, reports and correspondence in a timely fashion;
  • Making professional, autonomous decisions in relation to presenting medical problems, whether self-referred or referred from other healthcare workers within the organisation;
  • Assessing the healthcare needs of patients with undifferentiated and undiagnosed problems;
  • Screening patients for disease risk factors and early signs of illness;
  • Developing care plans for health in consultation with patients and in line with current practice disease management protocols;
  • Providing health education;
  • Recording clear consultation notes to agreed standards;
  • Collecting data for audit purposes and complying with QOF requirements;
  • Delivering enhanced services;
  • Compiling and issuing computer-generated acute and repeat prescriptions;
  • All general duties and responsibilities associated with a GP working within primary care.
As an employee of North East Ipswich Primary Care Network, you will enjoy the following benefits:
  • Genuine responsibility from day one.
  • Work with a strong social purpose.
  • A permanent employment contract.
  • A competitive salary with increments based on professional development.
  • Membership of the NHS pension.
  • Support to guide your personal and professional development.
  • Excellent training and development opportunities.
  • 27 days annual leave plus 8 bank holidays (pro-rata), increasing with continual years of NHS service.

title: Consultant Physician Care of the Elderly
descriptionHtml:
The Health Board wishes to appoint an additional Consultant Physician / Geriatrician to join the existing Care of the Elderly team in the West division of Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board (BCUHB), North West Wales. This post is based in the district general hospital, Ysbyty Gwynedd in Bangor, and we would consider part-time working for the correct candidate.

The successful candidate will have a sub-specialty interest and we are open to considering a range of sub-specialty areas for the right candidate. This reflects our ambitions to develop a dedicated frailty unit within the acute hospital, alongside expanding community-based initiatives aimed at reducing avoidable hospital admissions. In view of the continued expansion of the North Wales Medical School, opportunities to undertake teaching and educational supervision commitments could be considered.

The successful applicant will be expected to:

  • Develop and support a recognised sub-specialty interest, such as acute frailty, community geriatrics or orthogeriatrics.
  • Provide supervision, teaching and support to junior medical staff and other healthcare professionals.
  • Contribute to undergraduate and postgraduate medical education, including students from Bangor, Cardiff and Swansea Universities.
  • Participate in clinical governance, quality improvement, audit, appraisal, revalidation and continuing professional development activities.
  • Contribute to service development and transformation projects across acute and community geriatric services.
  • Participate in research, education and innovation opportunities where appropriate

Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board (BCUHB) is Wales's largest health organisation, with a budget of over £2.4 billion and a workforce of over 20,000 staff.

BCUHB provides a full range of primary, community, mental health, acute and specialist hospital services for the population of North Wales, across 3 acute hospitals and a network of communityhospitals, healthcentres, clinics, and mental health units. It alsoco-ordinates or provides the work of GP practices and NHS services provided by dentists, opticians, and pharmacists across the region.

The Health Board is an integrated health system that strives for excellent, compassionate care delivered in partnership with the public sector and other statutory and third sector organisations.

title: Employment Specialist Ref: 0187ZS
descriptionHtml:
Join our team as an IPS Employment Specialist in Torquay.

Do you believe you have the skills to help people return to employment, do you take pride in what you do, and can you think creatively about how different organisations can work together to deliver a better service? Are you happy to talk with employers and help match people into meaningful work? Are you a compassionate and motivated individual who wants to change peoples lives? Our team in Torquay is looking for an individual who is passionate about supporting people into work, to join them in providing high-quality recovery support to a diverse client group. If you are enthusiastic, creative and have a genuine desire to help others, wed love to hear from you.

As a leading charity supporting people with drug, alcohol, and mental health challenges, we operate over 80 services across England and Scotland, providing free and confidential support to more than 100,000 people each year.

Please use the Job Description to support your application.

Closing date: Sunday 12th November 2026. Please note this role may close earlier than the stated deadline if we receive a high volume of applications, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible. All applicants must submit a CV along with a cover letter explaining why they should be considered for this role.

As an IPS Employment Specialist, we offer a starting salary of £29,325 rising each year in line with our pay progression salary bands to £33,960 per year (This includes a Cornwall allowance of £1,000). For further details please reach out to a member of the recruitment team.

As an IPS Employment Specialist, you will support the IPS model as a specialism within a community substance misuse service and deliver support to people who are in treatment or recovery into employment. You will work directly with employers to secure

We have an exciting opportunity for an IPS Employment Specialist to join our team.

Our Individual Placement and Support (IPS) team aims to increase the number of people moving into employment from our drug and alcohol support service. This is an exciting opportunity to help make a real difference to people's lives.

The role will deliver supported employment to people in community treatment for substance use. You will be based at Shrublands House, Torquay working alongside the Torbay Drug and Alcohol Service, an established integrated community service supporting people aged 18 and over with substance misuse issues in Torbay. The team is a friendly, supportive, multidisciplinary team made up of recovery workers, nurses, social workers, doctors, peer supporters, and volunteers. You will work closely with the recovery team to support a small caseload of service users into employment opportunities.

As an organisation, we continue to build an inclusive culture that encourages, supports and celebrates the diverse voices and experiences of our staff. We know that representing the communities we serve is key to us meeting our vision of a future where everyone lives a life free from the harm associated with drugs and alcohol. We welcome the unique contributions that you can bring and we encourage people from underrepresented communities and backgrounds to apply to join our team, including people with lived experience, people with disabilities, people from racialised communities, LGBTQ+ people, people of all ages and armed forces veterans.

As part of our commitment to the Armed Forces Covenant we provide a guaranteed interview scheme for candidates that are veterans and meet all the essential criteria for a role. With You is also a Disability Confident Employer and we offer a guaranteed interview scheme for candidates with a disability and meet all the essential criteria for a role.

If you have a disability, a learning difficulty such as dyslexia or a medical condition which you believe may affect your performance during any aspect of our selection process, well be happy to make reasonable adjustments to enable you to perform at your best.

Please review our recruitment FAQs before submitting your application.

Internal Applicants - please note that fixed term roles will be offered as secondments.

  • Undertaking a variety of duties including surgery consultations, telephone consultations and queries, visiting patients at home, checking and signing repeat prescriptions and dealing with queries, paperwork, reports and correspondence in a timely fashion;
