title: Consultant Psychiatrist
descriptionHtml:
An exciting opportunity has become available for a Consultant Psychiatrist to join the Newport West Adult Mental Health Community Mental Health Team, based in Goldtops, Newport. This post is a 10-sessions post providing senior medical input into community care for a defined population in the area of Newport West. The post holder will join a forward thinking and enthusiastic CMHT. They will positively respond to requests from Team Members who need advice in the day-to-day management of adult patients within the borough and contribute to the development of the Adult Mental Health Services.

The post holder will be a senior member of the Newport Mental Health Service. They will work alongside existing Consultants in the Newport Borough and together will provide senior medical input to the community mental health team.

Integral responsibilities of this post include:

  • Ensuring the provision of a high quality and safe clinical service
  • Provide effective leadership to all staff engaged in the specialty
  • Sustain and develop teaching and research wherever appropriate
  • Undertake all work in accordance with the Health Board's procedures and operating policies
  • Conduct clinical practice in accordance with contractual requirements and within the parameters of the Division's and Health Board's service plans
  • Maintain the confidence of business plans and development strategies formulated for the specialty, the Medical Division or the Health Board

Aneurin Bevan University Health Board (ABUHB) is amulti award-winningNHS organisation serving the communities of Gwent. With more than 15,000 staff and volunteers, we provide safe, high-quality, and compassionate care across hospitals, GP practices, community services, and mental health settings. As a University Health Board, research, education, and innovation are central to our work, supporting evidence-based practice and continuous improvement.

Our work is guided by the Gwent Strategy 2025-2035, which sets out our long-term ambition to create a fairer and healthier future for our population. We focus on prevention, reducing health inequalities, and working in partnership with local authorities, voluntary organisations, and communities to improve health and wellbeing.

We are committed to creating an inclusive, supportive workplace where people feel valued, respected, and able to develop. Our values ofKindness, Integrity, and Respectshape how we care for patients and how we treat one another.

We offer a wide range of learning and development opportunities, flexible working where possible, and a comprehensive NHS benefits package. Working for ABUHB means being part of an organisation that values its people and offers the chance to build a meaningful and rewarding career while making a real difference to the lives of others.

title: Consultant Stroke Physician
descriptionHtml:
Aneurin Bevan University Health Board is seeking to appoint an enthusiastic and committed Consultant Stroke Physician to join its established and progressive Stroke Service. This post offers an excellent opportunity to contribute to the delivery and ongoing development of high-quality, patient-centred stroke care across the Health Board. The successful candidate will play a key role in supporting service transformation, improving clinical outcomes, and delivering national stroke standards, working collaboratively within a multidisciplinary team across the stroke pathway. This is an exciting opportunity to influence the future direction of stroke services within an organisation committed to innovation, quality improvement, and excellence in patient care.

Within the Stroke Directorate, you will play a pivotal role in advancing stroke care and contributing to the vision of providing excellent care to the people of Aneurin Bevan UHB. You will join colleagues in a very dedicated and dynamic team providing a comprehensive stroke service across multiple settings, including Grange University Hospital, Ysbyty Ystrad Fawr Hospital, and Royal Gwent Hospital.

Aneurin Bevan University Health Board provides a comprehensive and integrated stroke pathway, delivering high-quality care from prevention through to rehabilitation and long-term support. Patients benefit from hyper-acute stroke management at The Grange University Hospital, home to the Southeast Wales Hyper Acute Stroke Unit, with access to specialist interventions including thrombolysis and thrombectomy pathways. Ongoing rehabilitation is provided through a dedicated stroke rehabilitation unit at Ysbyty Ystrad Fawr, supported by a comprehensive Community Neurological Rehabilitation Service and psychology provision. The Health Board also delivers robust stroke prevention and TIA services, ensuring patients receive timely assessment, treatment and support at every stage of their recovery journey.

Aneurin Bevan University Health Board (ABUHB) is a multi award-winning NHS organisation serving the communities of Gwent. With more than 15,000 staff and volunteers, we provide safe, high-quality, and compassionate care across hospitals, GP practices, community services, and mental health settings. As a University Health Board, research, education, and innovation are central to our work, supporting evidence-based practice and continuous improvement.

Our work is guided by the Gwent Strategy 2025-2035, which sets out our long-term ambition to create a fairer and healthier future for our population. We focus on prevention, reducing health inequalities, and working in partnership with local authorities, voluntary organisations, and communities to improve health and wellbeing.

We are committed to creating an inclusive, supportive workplace where people feel valued, respected, and able to develop. Our values ofKindness, Integrity, and Respectshape how we care for patients and how we treat one another.

We offer a wide range of learning and development opportunities, flexible working where possible, and a comprehensive NHS benefits package. Working for ABUHB means being part of an organisation that values its people and offers the chance to build a meaningful and rewarding career while making a real difference to the lives of others.

title: Pharmacy Technician
locations: Sunderland Tyne and Wear, United Kingdom
descriptionHtml:

Details

title: Community Urgent Care GP - Oxfordshire
descriptionHtml:

title: Experienced Clinical Pharmacist  General Practice
descriptionHtml:
Bharani Medical Centre is seeking an experienced and confident Clinical Pharmacist to join our established general practice team in Slough.

We are looking for a pharmacist with previous NHS general practice experience who is familiar with EMIS Web, Ardens and primary care clinical workflows, and is comfortable working with a high degree of professional independence.

The role will focus on clinical correspondence, medicines reconciliation, QOF and long-term-condition management, prescribing safety and medicines optimisation.

Key areas include diabetes, hypertension, asthma, COPD, high-risk medicines monitoring, gabapentinoid reviews and medication optimisation in chronic kidney disease.

Flexible working arrangements are available, including remote or hybrid working where appropriate.

We would ideally like to engage someone on a self-employed basis initially, subject to appropriate contractual arrangements, with potential to progress to fixed-term or permanent salaried employment.

Informal discussions are welcomed.

  • Reviewing hospital discharge summaries, outpatient letters and clinical correspondence through Anima Documents.
  • Undertaking medicines reconciliation, updating EMIS Web records and actioning appropriate medication-related tasks.
  • Reviewing QOF registers and conducting structured medication reviews for patients with diabetes, hypertension, COPD and asthma.
  • Identifying patients requiring monitoring, treatment optimisation and follow-up.
  • Managing prescribing safety searches, including monitoring for patients prescribed DMARDs, DOACs and other high-risk medicines.
  • Undertaking medicines optimisation reviews, including gabapentinoids, polypharmacy and prescribing in chronic kidney disease.
  • Using EMIS Web and Ardens searches to identify and manage relevant patient cohorts.
  • Conducting remote or face-to-face medication reviews and documenting appropriate clinical actions.

Minor illness management may be included where appropriately trained. Prescribing decisions must remain within the pharmacists prescribing authority, with appropriate GP escalation where required.

Bharani Medical Centre is an established, GP-led practice providing NHS primary care to approximately 18,000 patients across three nearby sites in Slough.

Our multidisciplinary team includes experienced GP partners, salaried GPs, advanced nurse practitioners, clinical pharmacists, first-contact physiotherapists, practice nurses and administrative staff.

We place a strong emphasis on high-quality clinical care, medicines safety, evidence-based prescribing and proactive management of long-term conditions.

Our practice uses modern digital systems, including EMIS Web, Ardens, Anima and Accurx, to support efficient clinical workflows, population health management and medicines optimisation.

We value confident, proactive clinicians who can take ownership of defined responsibilities while working collaboratively with colleagues.

We offer a supportive professional environment, flexible working arrangements and opportunities to contribute to clinical improvement and patient safety initiatives.

We are committed to developing our clinical services and welcome pharmacists who want to make a meaningful contribution to modern general practice.

The Specialty Doctor is an exciting and enriching role which holds a case load across the neurodevelopmental, emotional and behavioural pathways from which cases will be allocated. They will attend weekly meetings and see children as part of the duty rota, and also participate as duty prescriber. There are many opportunities for service development, teaching and quality improvement, in addition to engaging in wider trust activities as part of CAMHS transformation. The Specialty Doctor will offer the following: - Participate actively as a core member of the multi-disciplinary team (MDT), collaboratively with colleagues including psychologists, nurses, therapists, and administrative staff. - Offer specialist clinical input into the assessment, formulation, diagnosis, and treatment planning for children and adolescents with complex mental health needs which will include contributing to neurodevelopmental assessments. - Contribute to the management and care planning of young people with ADHD and emotional difficulties. - The service is currently undergoing a review of the job roles of staff, including medical staff, so that clinicians are assigned to specific clinical care pathways appropriate to the needs of the service and the skills and experience of the clinicians concerned. There may thus be amendments to the clinical pathway(s) involvement for this post holder. On-call responsibilities: The post does not currently include on call responsibilities. If Section 12 approvNELFT NHS Foundation Trust provides mental health and community services for over 4.9 million people living in the London Boroughs of Waltham Forest, Redbridge, Barking and Dagenham, Havering, and across Essex. We work to ensure our patients, their friends and family, feel confident that their health needs are well met. With an excellent reputation for research and development, our skilled health professionals are at the cutting edge of evidence-based innovation, opening up the possibilities for better ways of working and delivery of care.

title: Consultant Psychiatrist (Female PICU)
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking an experienced full time Consultant Psychiatrist who will work at Cygnet Hospital Beckton and provide senior medical cover on Svanna ward, our 12 bed PICU service for women.

The post holder will be the Responsible Clinician and will oversee and maintain the care of all ward inpatients as required and will also have responsibility for auditing the medical services rendered at the ward and ensuring their good quality in accordance to GMC standards of good medical practice and other relevant professional guidelines.

In this role, your expertise will be the driving force for life-changing treatment fully supported by a Specialty Doctor and first-class multidisciplinary team including qualified nurses, psychologist and occupational therapist.

You'll also have the opportunity to progress to Medical Director Level through our management schemes.

Cygnet Hospital Beckton has four different specialist wards including PICU, acute admissions and personality disorder services. We accept emergency and planned, pre-assessed admissions. Our aim is to support individual service user recovery and integration back into the community, as quickly as possible.We have a multi-disciplinary team of specialists and offer a very broad range of therapies.

The post holder will be the Responsible Clinician and have overall medical responsibility of patient treatment plans, whilst liaising closely with the Multi-Disciplinary Team (Psychologists, Occupational Therapists, Registered Mental Health Nurses, Social Workers etc.)

The post holder will be expected to act as a positive role model, maintaining and demonstrating a positive attitude towards patients, their families, visitors and other staff.

Cygnet have been providing a national network of high-quality specialist mental health services for more than 30 years. We have built a reputation for delivering pioneering services and outstanding outcomes. Our expert care enables thousands of individuals to consistently make a positive difference to their lives.

We maintain a good relationship with our quality regulators and undergo regular inspections, with 85% of our services rated Good or Outstanding. We also operate an internal system of quality care, treatment and positive outcomes.

title: GP
descriptionHtml:
• Salaried GP Haven Health, Felixstowe, Suffolk
  • 6-8 Sessions

Why Join Haven Health ?

A supportive team: Work alongside an approachable partnership, experienced clinicians and highly trained multidisciplinary teams

A focus on clinical care: Benefit from well-developed systems and workflows designed to reduce administrative burden and support efficient working

Professional development: As a teaching practice covering a full range of specialties, we encourage learning, teaching and the development of individual interests.

A high achieving practice: We are proud of our strong QOF performance and high patient ratings.

Support at every stage: Whether you are experienced GP or newly qualified, we offer in-house learning and ongoing support to help you develop your skills and achieve your career ambitions.

A sustainable working pattern: We value work-life balance and aim to provide a positive environment where our GP's feel supported and able to thrive.

We are looking for someone who is approachable, compassionate and adaptable, with a positive attitude towards teamwork and continuous improvement. The successful candidate will be keen to contribute to the life of the practice, share ideas and help us deliver the best possible care for our patients.

Who are we looking for?

We are offering 6-8 sessions per week, with flexibility to discuss working arrangements.

You will provide high-quality, holistic care to our diverse patient population, including routine consultations, the management of acute and chronic conditions, and preventative healthcare.

You will also have opportunities to contribute to the ongoing development of practice services, pursue areas of clinical interest and become involved in teaching and quality improvement initiatives.

We are committed to supporting the next generation of GPs and helping our clinicians build rewarding, sustainable careers within our organisation.

We welcome applications from experienced and newly qualified GPs who share our commitment to excellent patient care, enjoy working collaboratively and are keen to contribute to a positive team culture.

If you are looking for a practice where you can develop professionally, enjoy working as part of a supportive team and make a real difference to your patients, we would love to hear from you.

Join Haven Health and be part of a practice that combines clinical excellence, innovation and a welcoming and progressive working environment.

Suffolk Primary Care (SPC) is a forward-thinking partnership of GP surgeries across Suffolk. Our collaborative approach enables doctors and staff to share resources, ensuring the continued delivery of high-quality healthcare.

We are committed to equal employment opportunities and encourage applications from all qualified individuals.

Benefits of Working with SPC

  • Defined benefits scheme

At SPC, we invest in our staffs professional growth and well-being, fostering a positive work environment that benefits both our team and the communities we serve.

title: Locum GP (Bank)
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking experienced and dedicated GPs to join the Vertis Locum GP Staff Bank. This is an exciting opportunity to provide high-quality, patient-centred care across a variety of primary care, urgent care and community healthcare settings, while enjoying the flexibility to choose shifts that fit your availability.

As a Bank Locum GP, you will play a vital role in assessing, diagnosing and managing patients with a wide range of healthcare needs. Working as part of a multidisciplinary team, you will deliver safe, effective and compassionate care, support service delivery during periods of increased demand, and contribute to positive patient outcomes. This role is ideal for clinicians who are adaptable, confident in autonomous decision-making, and committed to delivering excellent standards of care.

Key Responsibilities

  • Assess, diagnose and manage patients across urgent, primary and community care settings.
  • Prescribe, investigate, refer and escalate care as clinically required.
  • Deliver face-to-face, telephone and remote consultations.
  • Maintain clear and accurate clinical records.
  • Provide high-quality patient communication and safety-netting.
  • Work effectively within multidisciplinary teams and established clinical pathways.
  • Support safe, patient-centred care while meeting governance and safeguarding requirements.
  • Contribute to service quality, patient safety and continuous improvement initiatives

About Vertis Services

Vertis delivers and supports a range of primary care and urgent care services. Current and developing opportunities may include Primary Care Services at or around local Emergency Departments, out-of-hours medical cover for community hospitals, and other services mobilised in response to local system need. Joining the staff bank does not restrict a GP to one service and does not guarantee a minimum number of shifts. Offers of work will reflect service demand, commissioning arrangements, competence, availability and completion of service-specific onboarding.

employer: Chelsea and Westminster Hospital NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant in HIV Medicine and Sexual Health – 56 Dean Street
descriptionHtml:
The post is for a 10 PA Consultant in Sexual Health & HIV Medicine.

56 Dean Street is an award winning HIV and sexual health service based in Soho with a particular emphasis on HIV prevention and the sexual health care needs of LGBTQI+ people. It is Europe's busiest sexual health clinic with an attendance of approximately 110,000 patients per year. It cares for the third largest HIV cohort in the country with approximately 4,600 patients. The clinic also runs an Integrated Gender Dysphoria Service called TransPlus, we are particular interested in candidates who have an interest in Gender Dysphoria Care as part of these Job Plans includes time developing experience within TransPlus.

The HIV inpatient service merged with the Imperial College Hospitals Trust service in 2019 and now provides care on Ron Johnson ward at the Chelsea and Westminster Hospital site for inner northwest London as well as Hertfordshire.

The AAC for this post will be held on 10th December 2026

The post-holder will, in conjunction with the existing consultants, have responsibilities for providing advice, screening, diagnosis and treatment of patients with STIs, including HIV infection. They will be committed to developing integrated HIV & sexual health services, optimize cost efficiency of the service, implement new technologies and develop new initiatives. The post holder will have an opportunity to work within our TransPlus service.

The post-holder will also be required to participate in quality improvement, research and management of the service. It is anticipated that the post-holder will engage in specific management tasks and contribute to monthly departmental meetings in agreement with the Clinical Lead. The post-holder will also be expected to work with the other consultants at Chelsea and Westminster NHS Foundation Trust to deliver and improve outpatient HIV care, including recruitment to clinical trials. They will be expected to manage their own HIV cohort.

They will also be expected to work alongside the other consultants in providing educational supervision for the multidisciplinary team and participate in Wednesday morning educational activities, the virtual clinic and the weekly Directorate HIV resistance meeting. In particular, the post-holder will have educational supervisory responsibility for nominated junior staff. This role will include appraisal of the individuals concerned.

Chelsea and Westminster Hospital NHS Foundation Trust is one of England's top-performing and safest trusts. We operate two main acute hospital sites--Chelsea and Westminster Hospital and West Middlesex University Hospital--along with award-winning clinics across North West London.

Our nearly 7,500 staff care for a diverse population of 1.5 million, providing full clinical services, including maternity, A&E, and children's services, plus specialist HIV and sexual health clinics. The Care Quality Commission rates us 'Good' in safety, effectiveness, care, and responsiveness, and 'Outstanding' in leadership and resource use.

We continually invest in our facilities, including a £30m expansion of critical care at Chelsea and Westminster and an £80m Ambulatory Diagnostic Centre at West Middlesex.

We are committed to equal opportunities and believe that diversity drives innovation and excellence. As part of our dedication to equity, we actively welcome applications from individuals from the global majority, veterans and underrepresented communities. We value the unique perspectives and experiences that diverse teams bring and are committed to creating an environment where all voices are heard, respected, and empowered to succeed."

If you haven't heard from us within three weeks of the closing date, your application was likely unsuccessful. Employment is subject to a six-month probationary period.

Some roles may require weekend shifts at multiple sites.

employer: St George's University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
title: Locum Consultant Anaesthetist with an interest in Neuro Anaesthesia
descriptionHtml:
Applications are invited for Locum Neuro Anaesthesia Consultant post 10PAs and the post holders will join the Neuro on-call rota.

Upon appointment the post holder will be paired with a mentor for the first year. Furthermore, our set-up has much valuable support on-site as every day of the week, there is a senior Anaesthetic Consultant, acting as the Duty Floor Anaesthetist (DFA) for the overall smooth running of the operating theatres and providing urgent help and/or matching skills/experience of allocated anaesthetists with operating lists.

The post holder will join the Group of Neuro anaesthetists which consists of approximately 16 Consultants including Neuro Intensivists. This is a friendly, approachable, dynamic and diverse group, who are enthusiastic in both teaching colleagues and learning new skills from colleagues. There is emphasis in wellbeing and supporting each other. The case mix at St George's tends to be complex and challenging. Given the huge expertise in the department, it is easy to seek advice / discuss with an expert in a certain field or acquire new skills.

The post is for full time posts of 10 PAs, with 9 PAs for direct clinical care (DCC) and 1 for SPA in support of personal CPD, preparation for GMC appraisal, additional responsibilities of the post holder and revalidation with an opportunity to increase as interests develop.

The job plan template is based on an alternating working pattern, weeks AC and weeks BD. Some operating lists are three session lists, for continuity of care and theatre efficiency.

Session times (inclusive of CRA (clinical related activity time)

AM - 08:00-13:00 (5 hours - 1.25PA)

PM - 13:00-18:00 (5 hours - 1.25PA)

EVE - 17:00 - 21:00 (4 hours - 1PA)

All inpatient day sessions start at 08:00 and run until 18:00; 10 hours which equates to 2.5PAs. Half day sessions are 5 hours which equates to 1.25PAs. Three session lists equate to 3.5PA's.

The consultant job plan includes 'annualised sessions' which can be worked flexibly to meet the needs of the individual and the department. Each annualised session is equivalent to the PA value of the session worked. This flexibility allows individuals to organise working patterns to support a better work life balance, whilst also ensuring we have cover within the department. It is expected that the post-holder will contribute to a proportion of annualised sessions within the field of neuroanaesthesia. The remaining annualised sessions will be within the general anaesthesia subspecialties with in the skill mix of the individual anaesthetist.

The St George's Hospital Atkinson Morley Neurosurgical Unit is a leading UK centre for both adult and paediatric neurosurgery. It is a designated trauma centre with a specific neurosurgery service that manages all head injury patients. The Department of Anaesthesia covers all surgical specialities and is currently involved in many exciting initiatives. This is an excellent opportunity for an individual with the appropriate skills to join a first class team in an active and progressive London teaching hospital environment.

employer: Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Dermatologist
descriptionHtml:
Be part of a dermatology service recognised for clinical excellence, innovation and specialist care, serving patients across Oxfordshire and the Thames Valley.

Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is seeking a Consultant Dermatologist to join our highly regarded Dermatology Department. As a regional centre for dermatology and skin cancer care, we provide specialist and general dermatology services to a large and diverse patient population, supported by exceptional facilities and a strong multidisciplinary team. The total workload is 10 PAs and you will be based at the Churchill Hospital, Oxford but may be required to support clinical activity at other clinics.

This role offers the opportunity to develop your clinical interests within a department that combines high-quality patient care, teaching, research and service innovation. You will join an experienced team of consultants, specialist nurses, trainees and allied health professionals, working in a supportive environment that encourages collaboration, professional development and continuous improvement

With increasing demand for dermatology services across the region, this is a chance to help shape the future of the specialty while contributing to one of the UK's leading teaching hospital trusts.

Care to join us...?

As a Consultant Dermatologist, you will provide expert clinical care across a broad range of dermatology services, including general dermatology, vulval dermatology and leg ulcer clinics. Working within a consultant-led service, you will deliver high-quality care for both outpatient and inpatient populations while supporting the continued development of specialist services.

You will:

  • Deliver consultant-led dermatology clinics and specialist services.
  • Participate in the dermatology on-call rota and Advice and Guidance service.
  • Support the education, supervision and development of dermatology trainees and junior doctors.
  • Contribute to clinical governance, audit, quality improvement and service development initiatives.
  • Participate in teaching and training within a leading teaching hospital environment.
  • Work collaboratively with multidisciplinary colleagues and primary care partners to deliver outstanding patient-centred care.
  • Help drive innovation and service improvements to meet the evolving needs of patients across the region.

Joining our team means becoming part of a department with an outstanding reputation for dermatology, skin cancer care, education and research, backed by modern facilities and a shared commitment to delivering exceptional patient outcomes.

Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is one of the UK's largest and most respected NHS teaching trusts, providing world-class healthcare across four hospitals: the John Radcliffe Hospital, Churchill Hospital, Nuffield Orthopaedic Centre and Horton General Hospital and over one hundred satellite sites. Find out more information here OUH at a Glance 2026/27

You'll become part of an organisation at the forefront of patient care, research, education and innovation. You'll have access to excellent learning and development opportunities, work alongside highly skilled multidisciplinary teams, and contribute to services that make a real difference.

Our commitment to Delivering Compassionate Excellence is at the heart of everything we do. Guided by our values of compassion, respect, learning, delivery, improvement and excellence, we strive to create an environment where staff feel supported, valued and empowered to thrive. Watch how we set out to deliver compassionate excellence via the OUH YouTube channel and the OneTeamOneOUH - LIVING OUR VALUES video.

We are committed to creating an inclusive, respectful and safe workplace for everyone. As signatories to the NHS Sexual Safety Charter, we have a zero-tolerance approach to inappropriate behaviour and are dedicated to fostering a culture where all colleagues feel welcomed, respected and able to be themselves. We pledge zero tolerance for inappropriate sexual behaviour and commit to the ten core principles.

title: Medical Examiner
descriptionHtml:
"The next of kin are at the heart of everything we do"

We are seeking to appoint a proactive and self-motivated doctor to join our team of medical examiners at North & Mid Hampshire Medical Examiner Service.

Since 9 September 2024 when the service became statutory, all acute, non-acute and community deaths that do not require a coroner's referral must be scrutinised by a medical examiner before the death can be registered.

The successful applicant will

  • provide independent scrutiny of non-coronial deaths
  • ensure the appropriate referral of deaths to the coroner
  • contribute towards a better service for the bereaved, including an opportunity for them to raise any concerns
  • improve the quality of death certification
  • support local learning and improvement by identifying matters that require escalation to local clinical governance and other processes
  • improve the quality of mortality data

The ME service interacts with many clinical specialities from both the acute and non-acute setting, strengthening links between the health services, coroners' offices and register offices.

Medical Examiners are senior doctors from a diverse variety of clinical specialties in secondary and primary care. Relevant governance experience would be a strong bonus. This could be mortality or other case record reviews in secondary care; or actively considering similar issues in the context of team meetings in primary care. You will work closely with our team of Medical Examiner Officers, who are vital to the efficient running of the service.

Hampshire Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is the major provider of hospital services to the population of North and Mid Hampshire and surrounding areas. The hospitals in Basingstoke and Winchester provide a comprehensive range of acute services as well as being a tertiary referral centre for colorectal, liver, peritoneal carcinomatosis, haemophilia and pseudomyxoma surgery.

employer: Tees Esk and Wear Valleys NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Psychiatrist in Forensic Psychiatry
descriptionHtml:
This is a replacement post. The post is located at Roseberry Park Hospital, Middlesbrough, where inpatient forensic beds and clinical and managerial offices are all co-located.

There is a need for a Consultant on Ivy/Clover/Kestrel ward a low secure female learning disability ward.

There is a system of weekly MDT meetings for the ward which the post holder is expected to attend, in addition to meetings for CPA (6 monthly), formulation and risk management meetings. The length of stay currently on the ward is around five years.

The consultant will be supported by a ward manager, clinical lead working on each ward. In addition, they will receive support from occupational therapist, psychologist and social worker. Pharmacist will attend when support is required. A SAS/trust doctor, which is shared (50% time) will be supporting the post holder. The post holder can be the identified supervisor for the junior doctor. There will be opportunity to become a trainer for trainees in the future.

All patients will be detained under the Mental Health Act. As Responsible Clinician, the post holder will be expected to write statutory reports and attend First Tier Tribunals, Hospital Manager Hearings, S117 and MAPPA meetings as appropriate.

Referral rates for the ward are anticipated to be 4 per year from both internal and external sources. They can be seen jointly with the other staff members (psychologist/ nursing staff). The average length of stay on the ward is approx. 5 years.

Within the Secure Inpatient Services Directorate, the post-holder will be working alongside 14 consultant colleagues, 4 specialty grade doctors, and up to 3 core trainees.

We are one of the largest specialist mental health and learning disabilities trusts in the country providing a range inpatient and community services to 2m people living in County Durham, the Tees Valley, Scarborough, Whitby, Ryedale, Harrogate, Hambleton and Richmondshire. We also provide additional specialist services to other parts of Northern England.

From education and prevention, to crisis and specialist care our talented and compassionate teams work in partnership with our patients, communities and partners to help the people of our region feel safe, understood, believed in and cared for.

We nurture the recovery journey of anyone in need of our help. In Our Trust, everyone has a say in how they are supported and treated because we listen to every person in our care until they feel understood. Our patients, their families and carers work together with us towards better mental health.

We're committed to new thinking that improves the wellbeing of our region. We connect with our communities and partners to get mental health care right, in areas that really need it.

We won't rest until everyone in our region has the mental health care they need, to lead their best possible life.

Psychiatrists are essential contributors to the majority of our mental health teams. Service users expect and are justified to expect collaborative relationships with dedicated psychiatrists who work consistently as part of effective services.

employer: St George's University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
title: Acute Trauma Radiology Consultant
descriptionHtml:
Applications are invited for a Consultant Radiologist to join a friendly and cohesive team of radiologists with diverse expertise in a busy department and a strong record in teaching and training. The applicant would be expected to join the existing radiologists in providing a comprehensive diagnostic radiology service and providing support for multidisciplinary meetings. The post-holder will also support the running of service in our main department at St George's Hospital.

The successful applicant will be expected, in collaboration with the other radiologists in the department, to oversee and ensure the provision of high-quality clinical services within the Radiology Department. This would consist of providing a comprehensive diagnostic radiology service which includes general plain radiography,, CT, ultrasound, and MRI.

In addition the post will contain general diagnostic adult sessions in CT and plain film reporting. The successful applicant would take part in general oncall and have participation in training and quality improvement activity would also be expected.

The post-holder will also participate in a full-time diagnostic on-call rota (approximately 1:15), alongside regular weekend working (with time off in-lieu).

It is expected that applicants will have the Fellowship of the Royal College of Radiologists and a CCT in Radiology or equivalent training and experience.

St George's University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is one of the largest healthcare units in the UK accommodating more than 1000 beds and employing 6000 members of staff, and is closely integrated to the St George's Hospital Medical School, part of the University of London. We have an established national and international reputation as a leading hospital for specialist care including neurosciences, cardiac care, stroke and oncology. We provide an integrated mix of secondary care and specialist services to children of Wandsworth, Merton and South West London, Surrey and further afield. We have a comprehensive range of paediatric medical and surgical specialist services supported by PICU and NICU and are a joint treatment centre for oncology with the Royal Marsden Hospital. The Trust is a designated level 1 Major Trauma Centre and has been granted Foundation Trust status.

title: Consultant Ophthalmologist
descriptionHtml:
Do you share our Health Board values; Caring for each other; Working together; Always improving? If so, we would love for you to come and work for Swansea Bay University HB.

Applicants are invited for a full time Ophthalmology consultant with a specialist interest in Cataract surgery

The post will be available from May 2026 and based at Singleton Hospital in Swansea where the successful applicants will joina team of 16 Consultants responsible for the provision of Ophthalmology services to the Health Board.

The successful applicant will participate in the current 1 in 11 on-call rota at Singleton Hospital, with prospective cover. In exceptional circumstances it may also be necessary to undertake duties at other locations with the Health Board. Travelling as necessary between hospitals / clinics may be required to undertake such duties. Travel expenses will be remunerated according to the Health Board policy and procedures for claiming. The Surgical Specialties Directorate is an integrated directorate serving Neath Port Talbot Hospital in Port Talbot, and Morriston and Singleton Hospitals in Swansea. The Directorate also provides regional services to patients living along the M4 corridor in South Wales and to the population of West Wales.

You will provide a clinical service, with colleagues, which will include the responsibility for the prevention, diagnosis and treatment of illness.

Working with consultant colleagues and the multi-professional team you will have continuing responsibility for the well-being of all patients under your care; allowing for proper delegation to, and training of staff. In partnership with clinical and managerial colleagues you will also have responsibility for the safe, efficient and effective functioning of the services in which you work in line with the values, operational policies and integrated medium term plan (IMTP) of the Health Board. You are encouraged to consider how services can be improved and to report any concerns about safety.

You will be required to adhere to the principles of good medical practice as laid down by the General Medical Council.

You will be required to participate in the Health Board's risk management process, clinical governance and any other healthcare governance activities within the department, the Surgical Division / Neath Port Talbot Singleton Service Group and the Health Board.

Swansea Bay University Health Board has responsibility for the health of around 390,000 people in the Neath Port Talbot and Swansea areas, with a budget of around £1 billion and employing 12,500 people. We are a University Health Board working in partnership with Swansea University, Swansea School of Medicine, the School of Health Science and the Institute of Life Science. The HB has three major hospitals providing a range of services: Morriston and Singleton hospitals in Swansea and Neath Port Talbot hospital in Baglan, Port Talbot

The Health Board is part of A Regional Collaboration for Health (ARCH), which is a partnership with Hywel Dda UHB and Swansea University. Aimed at improving the wellbeing and wealth of Southwest Wales.

Swansea is Wales' second largest city and sits on the five-mile sweep of Swansea Bay. An ideal base for exploring South-West Wales, there is also much on offer for visitors in Swansea itself. Swansea has a range of shops, cosy cafes, great restaurants, art galleries as well as being able to offer good outdoor lifestyle with its beautiful coastline and beaches on the Gower Peninsula. Swansea also has excellent sporting facilities including the Wales National pool and Swansea.com stadium home to the Ospreys and Swansea City Football Club.

title: Consultant Psychiatrist - CAMHS Recovery and Support Pathway
descriptionHtml:
We are recruiting for a full-time Consultant Psychiatrist to join our Buckinghamshire CAMHS Recovery and Support Pathway and work with a well-established multi-disciplinary team in the Sue Nichols Centre, Aylesbury and Saffron House, High Wycombe.

You'll provide psychiatric clinical input and leadership within a recently redesigned service delivering targeted mental health care to children and young people with predominantly emotional disorders, including neurodivergent young people.

The Recovery Teams are structured to support two cohorts: young people who benefit from Focussed Intervention and Recovery Support (FIRS) and Specialist Intervention and Recovery Support (SIRS). These teams are a core part of Buckinghamshire CAMHS providing support for young people who are experiencing a moderate to severe mental health condition such as depression, anxiety disorders, PTSD, and bipolar disorder.

You'll work 10 programmed activities with a job plan typically comprising 75% direct clinical care and 25% supporting professional activities, in line with Royal College of Psychiatrists' guidance. Opportunities are available to develop interests in service development, quality improvement, and teaching and training within a well-established, supportive multidisciplinary team and consultant peer group.

Join us in shaping brighter futures for children and young people at one of the UK's leading mental health Trusts; we would be delighted to hear from you.

This is a great opportunity to join a welcoming and supportive group of substantive consultants within the wider service, and work with a team who truly value working together to provide the holistic care young people and families need from one of the core teams within CAMHS. The Service as a whole has a strong focus on areas such as quality improvement and wellbeing, supporting staff with a flexible approach to help their work-life balance, and has established itself as a great place to train for resident doctors in recent years.

Buckinghamshire is also a fantastic place to live for those looking to move, with great opportunities for family life (including nationally renowned schools), access to beautiful country side in the Chilterns, as well as easy access to London and Oxford for those who value the cultural opportunities the different cities provide. It is also an easy commute for those living in neighbouring areas such as north London, Hertfordshire, Bedfordshire and Oxfordshire.

We offer rewarding career development with protected SPA time as part of your job plan, encouraging you to take leadership courses to enhance your skills. We also offer a relocation allowance of up to £8,000 for external applicants (subject to eligibility criteria).

Oxford Health is a great place to work and to be able to showcase the best of yourself when making an application please read the "candidate guide to making an application" and ensure your supporting statement is tailored to the role you are applying for and addresses any essential criteria.

As a Trust we provide physical, mental health and social care for people of all ages across Oxfordshire, Buckinghamshire, Swindon, Wiltshire, Bath and Northeast Somerset. Our services are delivered at community bases, hospitals, clinics and people's homes, delivering care as close to home as possible. Our vision is that no matter who you are or where you are, you will tell us that you receive: "Outstanding care delivered by an outstanding team"

Our values are: "Caring, safe and excellent"

We offer a wide range of benefits designed to support your career and wellbeing. These include:

o Excellent opportunities for career progressiono Access to tailored individual and Trust wide learning and developmento 33 days annual leave, plus bank holidays, rising to 35 days with continuous serviceo NHS Discount across a wide range of shops, restaurants and retailerso Competitive pension schemeo Lease car schemeo Cycle to work schemeo Employee Assistance Programmeo Mental Health First Aiderso Staff accommodation (please note waiting lists apply)o Staff networking and support groups hosted by our Equality, Diversity & Inclusion team

title: Practice Nurse
descriptionHtml:
Role: Practice NurseLocation: East DulwichFull-time or part-time roles availableCompetitive salary/package, dependent on experienceWe are seeking an enthusiastic and motivated Practice Nurse to join our established team and make a real difference in patient care.

As a GP Practice Nurse, you will work within a GP practice delivering assessment, screening, and treatment services. You will provide advice to patients on general health and minor ailments, referring to GPs when necessary.

You will also support pathology processes, including the collection, storage, and dispatch of specimens, and assist with administrative and professional duties, ensuring smooth practice operations.

You will be part of a diverse, multi-skilled team of clinical and non-clinical colleagues, delivering high-quality, person-centred, and holistic care to patients registered with Omnes Healthcare practices.

Key Responsibilities

Provide assessment, screening, and treatment services to patientsAdvise patients on general healthcare and minor ailments, referring to GPs when appropriateCollect, store, and dispatch pathological specimens in line with practice protocolsSupport administrative and professional responsibilities, including QOF management and clinical auditsWork collaboratively with the multidisciplinary team to ensure safe, efficient, and effective patient care

Who we are

Omnes Healthcare is a growing, forward-thinking organisation delivering NHS Primary and Secondary Care services since 2006. Supporting patients across multiple sites, we combine clinical excellence with innovation to improve lives.

As part of the Evergreen Group, we also lead on digital health and genomics projects, including the Evergreen Life app, which empowers people to take control of their health.

Our mission is to enhance healthy and happy life years through high-quality, personalised, and accessible care. Our vision is to be a trusted leader in healthcare, known for innovation, compassion, and real impact.

We live by four core values:

Caring – Respect and compassion in everything we doInclusive – Empowering diverse voices and teamworkEvolving – Driving continuous improvement and innovationAmbitious – Striving for high standards and real impactWhether your role is clinical or corporate, it matters. We’re committed to creating a positive, inclusive, and supportive environment where all colleagues can thrive.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:

The successful applicant would be expected to work as an autonomous practitioner, responsible for the provision of medical services to the practice population, delivering an excellent standard of clinical care whilst complying with the GMS contract.

Furthermore, the post-holder will adhere to the GMC standards for good medical practice, contributing to the effective management of the practice, leading by example, maintaining a positive and collaborative working relationship with the multidisciplinary team.

Fernbank Surgery has a positive working relationship with many external stakeholders in the local area and we would be keen for the successful applicant to continue with these positive relationships.

Fernbank Surgery is a busy practice made up of a team of 5 very versatile partners, who are supported by a host of salaried GPs, ANPs, Clinical Pharmacists, Practice Nurses, Health Care Assistants, a Management Team and a pillar of administration and reception staff members. Lytham has plenty to offer in the local community from sea front walks, picnics in the park or a vast choice of bars and restaurants Lytham really does cater for all.If you are interested in the post and want to visit the Practice or find out more, please contact Stephanie Sweeney, Practice Manager by email onlscicb-fw.fernbankmanagers@nhs.net

title: Critical Care Clinical Research Fellow
descriptionHtml:
This 6, 12 or 18 month post offers candidates the opportunity to gain experience in Intensive Care Medicine (ICM) within a busy District General Hospital. Accreditation as the University Department of Critical Care Medicine was awarded in 2022 and in parallel with exceptional clinical experience, this post will also offer the exciting opportunity for dedicated clinical research time.

This job would be ideally suited to individuals who are committed to or strongly considering a career in ICM or a related acute speciality, and who are hoping to develop an ongoing interest in clinical research. It would also be appropriate for Faculty of Intensive Care Medicine (FICM) trainees seeking their special skills Stage 2 training with appropriate prospective approval. Some experience of ICM is strongly desirable.

The clinical training programme is outcomes-based and follows the curriculum developed by FICM. This is described in detail in FICM's guidance on outcome-based training and assessment (http://www.ficm.ac.uk).

Our ICU has recently been rated 'Outstanding' for patient care by the CQC and the Trust overall has a 'Good' rating. The unit currently admits nearly 1100 level 2 and level 3 patients per year into 23 beds. The case mix is predominantly medical with trauma and surgical patients making up about 20%. Around 90% of our admissions are emergencies with the remainder being high risk surgical cases including, colorectal & urological procedures. There are about 60 paediatric admissions and stabilisations a year, the vast majority of which are retrieved via the Southampton and Oxford Retrieval Team (SORT), but some remain for the initial stages of their stabilisation and treatment. The Trust is a tertiary referral cancer centre and includes all specialties except neurosurgery, transplant, vascular and cardiothoracic surgery. The trust has a primary coronary angioplasty service with the fastest door to needle times in the country as well as the fastest door to needle times for stroke thrombolysis. There is an excellent interventional radiology department with 24-hour service provision and frequent close working with ICU. We also receive excellent support from our microbiology department with daily ward rounds on the ICU.

descriptionHtml:

Birmingham, Leicester, Peterborough, Northampton, Nottingham, Bournemouth, Portsmouth, Reading, Richmond, London East, Finsbury Park, Merseyside, Doncaster, Leeds, Middlesbrough.

BPAS are looking for dynamic, skilled doctors who can work as part of a multi-disciplinary team to support our national services. You will hold a Bachelor of Medicine or equivalent, full GMC registration with a license to practice, and are passionate and committed to reproductive healthcare.

  • We can provide substantive, fixed term and casual contracts.

  • Carry out termination of pregnancy by the appropriate method to evacuate the products of conception and ensure complete abortion and in accordance with BPAS clinical policies and procedures
  • Complete client consultation if needed and complete the statutory documentation
  • Assess and provide advice on the management of clients with medical or other conditions which may affect the abortion process.
  • Be present in the operating theatre throughout each procedure and remain on site until all clients have been assessed fit for discharge from recovery or passed to the care of another on-site doctor

We are also looking for:

  • Experience of independent practice for any abortion procedures/gestations relevant to the post, or willingness to be trained in-house.
  • Knowledge of termination of pregnancy procedures and the assessment and management of complications
  • Strong communication skills with the ability to be pro-active and flexible

  • Willing to travel to other locations within the region and/or work flexibly

The British Pregnancy Advisory Service (BPAS) is the UK's largest independent reproductive healthcare charity, providing evidence-based, not-for-profit reproductive healthcare. We work mainly on behalf of the NHS, offering abortion care, contraception, and STI testing and treatment across the country.

When you join BPAS, you become part of a values-driven organisation where compassion, professionalism, and choice guide everything we do. You will help remove barriers to safe reproductive care while supporting people to make informed choices about their health and futures.

title: CAMHS Practitioner – Eating Disorders Transitions Worker
descriptionHtml:
Join our specialist Community Eating Disorders Service and play a key role in supporting young people and their families as they transition from CAMHS to Adult Eating Disorder Services. This rewarding role offers the opportunity to provide expert assessment, therapeutic intervention, care coordination and advocacy, working collaboratively across multidisciplinary teams and partner agencies. We are looking for an experienced and compassionate mental health professional with a passion for eating disorders, strong clinical skills, and a commitment to delivering high-quality, person-centred care while helping shape and develop innovative services across Rotherham, Doncaster and North Lincolnshire.

  • Deliver evidence-based therapeutic interventions, including individual, family and group work, for young people with eating disorders and their families.

  • Provide clinical supervision, training and support to colleagues, students and other professionals.
  • Contribute to service development, quality improvement, audit and research activities to enhance outcomes for young people and families.
  • Promote innovative, evidence-based practice and support the continual development of eating disorder services across Rotherham, Doncaster and North Lincolnshire.

Rotherham Doncaster and South Humber NHS Foundation Trust (RDaSH) employ around 4000 talented colleagues who are very much appreciated, valued, and respected.

title: Clinical Pharmacist
descriptionHtml:
Highcroft Surgery is a well established GP Practice serving 11,000 patients in the heart of Arnold.

We are looking for a Clinical Pharmacist to work full time in our Practice and become part of a friendly, supportive and forward thinking team, committed to delivering high-quality, patient-centred care. We offer a collaborative working environment, manageable workloads, and strong multidisciplinary support. With involvement in service improvement and strong team work, this is an excellent role for a Clinical Pharmacist seeking job satisfaction, balance, and a welcoming Practice culture.

* Structured Medication Reviews - Carry out face to face and telephone call reviews for patients with complex needs or those taking multiple medication

* Long-Term Condition Management - Monitor, manage and adjust treatments for chronic illnesses

* Acute and Repeat Prescriptions - Handle medication requests, reauthorise repeat prescriptions and address acute queries

* Safety and Medicines Optimisation - Reconcile medications for patients recently discharged from the hospital to prevent discrepancies, identify high-risk medications (such as monitoring blood tests for specific drugs) and implement strategies to reduce adverse effects and counsel patients on how to use their medicines safely and effectively to reduce wastage

Our organisation is supported by a dedicated team of 30 staff members, including 2 GP Partners, 4 Salaried GPs, 1 Nurse Partner, 3 Nurses, 1 Nurse Associate, 2 Health Care Assistants, 1 Practice Manager, 1 Operations Manager, alongside teams including Pharmacy, Reception and Administration. We also have a number of ARRS staff supporting the Practice.

We all work together to deliver high-quality, patient-centred care. We pride ourselves on a warm, welcoming atmosphere where people feel valued, supported and respected. The work ethic is collaborative and professional, with a strong emphasis on teamwork, mutual support and continuous improvement.

Working here offers the benefits of a positive workplace culture, open communication, and opportunities for learning and development. Staff are encouraged to contribute ideas and take pride in their work, creating an environment where both employees and patients can thrive.

We use clinical systems including SystmOne, Ardens and eConsult.

descriptionHtml:

title: GP Practice Pharmacy Technician
descriptionHtml:
We require a Pharmacy Technician to work 25 hours per week to work as part of the multidisciplinary primary care team to support the safe, effective and cost-efficient use of medicines within the GP practice. The post holder will undertake medicines optimisation activities, support prescription management processes, contribute to medication reviews, and assist in improving prescribing systems and patient outcomes.

  • Assist with medication reviews by identifying potential issues requiring pharmacist or GP input.
  • Promote safe, evidence-based and cost-effective prescribing.
  • Support implementation of national and local prescribing guidance.
  • Identify opportunities for deprescribing and medication optimisation.
  • Support the Practice Prescribing Clerks in processing repeat prescription requests in accordance with practice policies.
  • When required, review prescription requests for appropriateness and identify any anomalies.Manage prescription synchronisation and medication queries, escalating any complex queries to Practice Pharmacist / GP.Support patients requiring medication on repeat dispensing (batch) services.

  • Identify discrepancies and liaise with relevant healthcare professionals to resolve issues
  • Escalate complex clinical concerns to the Clinical Pharmacist or GP
  • Use clinical systems to identify patients requiring monitoring or review
  • Support prescribing audits and quality improvement initiatives.
  • Extract and analyse prescribing and medicines-related data where appropriate.
  • Contribute to achievement of Quality Assurance and Improvement Framework (QAIF) and other contractual requirements.

title: Consultant Orthopaedic - Complex Upper Limb Surgeon
descriptionHtml:
Applications are invited for this full time Complex Upper Limb (Shoulder / Elbow / Wrist / Hand) & Trauma Surgery Consultant in Trauma & Orthopaedics, on a 10-11PA basis. This post is to join the existing Consultant Orthopaedic team based across two DGH sites at Hastings and Eastbourne. This post is initially on a locum basis, with a view to conversion to a substantive role.

The East Sussex Healthcare NHS Trust (ESHT) provides a comprehensive service in orthopaedic specialties for the surrounding districts of Hastings and Eastbourne. The post is required to support the surgical needs of the elective and trauma patients and supporting/lead the multidisciplinary team based on the trauma wards to enhance the quality and recovery of patients following trauma episodes.

The Eastbourne and Hastings Hospitals have an integrated Trust for the past 13 years. In line with reconfiguration of our service, orthopaedic trauma has been centralised on the Hastings site with elective surgery continuing both sites.

The orthopaedic department has long standing links with both GKT Medical School in London and Brighton Medical School and we receive regular medical students within the Orthopaedic department from both institutions.

Potential AAC Date: 13th January 2027

  • KEY SPECIALTY RESPONSIBILITIES/INFORMATION:
  • Surgical care of Trauma & Orthopaedic patients.
  • Pre-op, perioperative and post-operative care of trauma and orthopaedic patients.
  • Maintaining the highest clinical standards in the management of patients on the trauma, elective, outpatient units and other clinical areas, as required.
  • To share with colleagues' responsibility for the day-to-day management of the Trauma & Orthopaedic patients within our unit, in line with national and local clinical guidelines.
  • Teaching and training of junior staff, medical students and Allied Health Professional
  • To have responsibility for ensuring active participation in continuing medical education (CME)
  • To actively participate in both departmental and Trusts matters concerning Clinical Governance and audit
  • To attend meetings as appropriate.
  • Fulfil duties of weekly timetables, including out of hours and weekend duties in-line with the Consultant of the Week (7 days) and on call night rota.
  • The post holder will be expected to record their findings and investigate appropriately, optimising their patients prior to their orthopaedic surgery or other treatment and maintain the patients' surgical care during their inpatient episodes.
  • The post holder will be required to attend the 8am daily Trauma meeting when on duty and may be required to present patients as needed.
  • The post offers excellent experience in all aspect of Trauma & Orthopaedic care.

A wide range of staff benefits are available to our staff including staff development, enrolment in the NHS pension scheme, auto-enrolment to our Temporary Workforce Service, access to nurseries at Conquest Hospital and Eastbourne District General Hospital, staff restaurants and on-site staff accommodation.

In addition to an internal Occupational Health department, all staff also have access to free psychological support through our confidential Employee Assistance Programme which is available to staff 24 hours a day 7 days a week. Onsite parking is available for a small administration fee.

There has never been a better time to join East Sussex Healthcare NHS Trust, submit your application today.

Use state-of-the-art technology, equipment and facilities 
Supervise, support and develop junior members of the team 
Provide high-quality perioperative care in a multidisciplinary team setting
Create high-quality care and patient experiences that are clinically effective and evidence based

The Nuffield Health hospital in Hereford is located in the beautiful Herefordshire countryside and sits just half a mile north of Hereford City Centre. A hospital, offering exceptional private healthcare to the local community and surrounding counties. Offers a vast range of first-class medical and surgical services performed by a team of expert consultants. The Ward consists of 20 inpatient beds, and a busy ACU with the majority of patients receiving elective Surgical procedures. Catering for both inpatient and day case surgery, providing a broad range of surgical specialties including General Surgery, Orthopaedics, Endoscopy, Gynaecology, Urology, ENT, Plastics and more. Working with leading consultants, Hereford hospital prevents and treats many medical conditions and offers a wide range of complex surgery and services. The working atmosphere is highly professional and stimulating, yet friendly and collaborative like that of a large family unit.

title: Occupational Health Physician
descriptionHtml:
Job Title: Occupational Health Physician

Location: Northern Ireland / Hybrid working

Salary: up to £135,000 (FTE) per annum depending on experience

Contract Type: Permanent

Hours: Full Time or Part Time 22.5 - 37.5 hours per week between Monday to Friday (8-4/9-5/0830-1630)

We are looking for an Occupational Health Physician (OHP) to join our team supporting customers across Northern Ireland. The role combines home working with onsite delivery when required.

We welcome applications from doctors with previous Occupational Health experience, as well as doctors who have completed a Diploma in Occupational Medicine (DipOccMed) and are looking to develop their career in Occupational Health.

For doctors who are new to Occupational Health, we provide the training and support needed to develop your skills and confidence in the role. You will receive comprehensive training and ongoing support as you build your practical Occupational Health experience, allowing you to apply your DipOccMed knowledge in a clinical setting.

We are therefore keen to hear from doctors who have completed their DipOccMed and have a genuine interest in pursuing a career as an Occupational Health Physician, even if you have not yet gained hands-on Occupational Health experience.

You will be required to carry out:

  • Telephone and face-to-face consultations
  • Sickness absence management
  • Attendance and performance case management
  • Ill-health retirement advice
  • Pre-placement consultations
  • Health surveillance
  • HAVS Tier 4 assessments

Optima Health is the UK's largest provider of Occupational Health and wellbeing services, supporting organisations across both the public and private sectors. With a heritage dating back to 1947, we have been helping employers create healthier, high-performing workplaces for generations, and we continue to evolve with innovative, practical solutions that make a real difference. At the heart of our story are our people. We bring together like-minded professionals who are passionate about improving workplace health and wellbeing and delivering meaningful support to the organisations we work with across the UK. When you join Optima Health, you become part of something bigger. We invest in our people/you through structured induction, ongoing training and tailored career development, helping you build the skills and experience to grow your career. Together, we live our values: One Team There are no barriers in our business. We trust each other and work together as one team to deliver what our clients need. We all have a part to play in our future, and everyone's contribution is important and valued. Doing the Right Thing We operate to the highest standards. Success is underpinned by honesty and integrity, and by doing what we say we will do. We care about the impact of our work on our people, our clients, their employees, society, and the world we live in. Caring for our colleagues' wellbeing and respecting their time, energy and balance is fundamental to this value.

title: General Practitioner
descriptionHtml:
Meddygfa Glan Cynon is seeking an enthusiastic and motivated Salaried GP to join our friendly, supportive and forward-thinking training practice in the heart of the Cynon Valley.

Working alongside experienced GP Partners and a skilled multidisciplinary team, you will provide high-quality, patient-centred care to a diverse and welcoming community. The role offers a varied mix of routine and urgent clinical work, opportunities to develop specialist interests, and involvement in undergraduate and postgraduate medical education.

We are committed to clinician wellbeing, continuity of care and professional development, offering a collaborative working environment, modern premises, EMIS Web, a working day aligned to BMA recommendations and genuine flexibility around working patterns.

The successful candidate will provide high quality primary medical care to our patient population through a mixture of routine and urgent clinical appointments, including house calls and low frequency on call requirements.They will work collaboratively with the wider multidisciplinary team to deliver safe, effective and patient-centred care.

The role offers opportunities to develop individual clinical interests, contribute to teaching and training activities, participate in quality improvement initiatives and support the ongoing development of practice services. The successful applicant will be encouraged to work autonomously while benefiting from the support of experienced GP Partners and a welcoming clinical team.

This is a varied and rewarding position within a practice that values continuity of care, innovation and professional development.

Meddygfa Glan Cynon is a friendly, supportive and forward-thinking training and teaching practice located in the heart of Mountain Ash, serving the communities of the Cynon Valley. We are proud of our reputation for delivering high-quality, patient-centred care while maintaining a positive, collaborative and enjoyable working environment for all members of the team.

Our clinical team consists of five experienced GP Partners, Salaried GPs, Practice Nurses, Healthcare Assistants, Clinical Pharmacists and a wider multidisciplinary team. We foster a culture of teamwork, mutual respect and open communication, where everyone's contribution is valued and professional development is actively encouraged.

As an accredited teaching practice, we are heavily involved in both undergraduate and postgraduate medical education. Clinicians have opportunities to participate in teaching, mentoring and supervision activities, alongside developing their own specialist interests and clinical skills.

We operate from modern, well-equipped premises using EMIS Web and benefit from strong administrative and clinical support systems. We are committed to clinician wellbeing and work-life balance, with a working day aligned to BMA recommendations, a manageable approach to workload and a culture that recognises the importance of supporting one another.

title: Trust Locum Consultant Diabetes and Endocrinology
descriptionHtml:
This is a post for a Trust Locum Consultant Physician with a special interest in Diabetes & Endocrinology for the Cardiovascular Clinical Unit within Medicine at East Sussex Healthcare NHS Trust

The team is housed within the Bending and Sheppard Centre for Diabetes and Endocrinology in Eastbourne and at Conquest the team is housed within the Diabetes and Endocrine centre in the Hospital.

The department has a wide variety of sub-specialty interests including:

  • Pre and antenatal Diabetes & Endocrine care.
  • Multidisciplinary Foot Team (MDFT) - Urgent and planned Diabetic foot care.
  • Inpatient Diabetes.
  • Intermediate care.
  • A large cohort of CSII & CGMS patients with engagement across the ICB to adopt HCL
  • Diabetes and renal disease.
  • Pituitary tumours as part of the Sussex Pituitary Tumour Network. Bi-weekly MDT and monthly Combined Pituitary clinic.
  • Adrenal disease - including an established biweekly MDT meeting.
  • Parathyroid disease - including MDT meeting.
  • Young adult and transition diabetes clinic.
  • Community Diabetes Clinics

We are proud to provide 'Outstanding' care and be a great place to work

We provide safe, compassionate and high quality care to half a million people living or visiting East Sussex. We are one of the largest organisations in East Sussex, the only integrated provider of acute and community care in Sussex. Our extensive services are provided by 7000+ members of staff working from acute hospitals in Hastings and Eastbourne, three community hospitals in Bexhill, Rye and Uckfield, over 100 community sites and in people's own homes.

In 2020 the Care Quality Commission (CQC), rated us as 'Good' overall, and 'Outstanding' for being caring and effective. The Conquest Hospital and our Community Services are rated 'Outstanding'. Eastbourne DGH rated 'Good'.

In 2020 the Trust launched its ambitious 'Building for our Future' programme. This once in a lifetime programme aims to repair, redevelop and expand our hospitals, transforming the environment in which we provide care for generations to come.

title: Senior Care Assistant
descriptionHtml: As a Senior Care Assistant at HC One, Kindness will be at the core of everything you do. It touches upon every aspect of our Dementia, Nursing, Residential and Specialist care homes. Every single person who works here understands that our residents are people just like them with their own stories to tell. And, by joining us, youll have a wonderful opportunity to give something back to those people.For you, that will mean planning and implementing the kind of care that will give our residents a real sense of security, dignity and independence. You will get to know our residents and their families  helping to ensure we deliver truly personalised care plans. Leading a team of Care Assistants, you will be responsible for maintaining the highest standards of care and youll be a real influence on the rest of the team. Whether you are showing someone how to use a walking frame, helping someone at the end of their life to eat a meal or talking to a residents family on the phone, youll do so with a sense of kindness, above anything else. Assisting the Registered Nurse and Care Manager, you will be involved in providing essential physical and mental stimulation through a range of social and recreational activities, as well as administering medication.At HC-One, our purpose is to support those in our care to lead their best lives. As the Kind Care Company, it is our mission to provide the kindest support and care to Residents living in our care homes, as we strive to be the first-choice care provider for Families, our Colleagues and Commissioners in each of the communities that we serve.

title: Nurse
descriptionHtml:
Join our growing Lung Cancer Screening Programme and play a vital role in the early detection of lung cancer and other respiratory conditions.

Working across our mobile screening locations, you'll help identify patients at risk, support healthier lifestyles, and contribute to a service that is transforming lives through earlier diagnosis and intervention.

This is an excellent opportunity to combine your clinical expertise with patient education, health promotion and autonomous clinic management, all whilst enjoying a compressed working week of just three shifts per week.

  • Deliver virtual and face-to-face nurse-led clinics as part of the lung health assessment pathway.
  • Carry out comprehensive respiratory assessments and identify patients at increased risk of lung disease.
  • Refer suitable patients for Low-Dose CT scans to support early cancer detection.
  • Provide evidence-based smoking cessation advice and ongoing health education.
  • Promote healthier lifestyle choices and empower patients to take control of their respiratory health.
  • Recognise and escalate safeguarding concerns, red-flag symptoms and medical emergencies appropriately.
  • Maintain professional competencies and complete training requirements, including IRMER and ARTP spirometry accreditation where required.

InHealth is the UKs largest specialist provider of diagnostic and healthcare solutions, working in partnership with the NHS for more than 30 years to make healthcare better for more than 5 million patients each year.

For clinical colleagues, that means delivering high-quality care within modern settings, with state-of-the-art equipment across a wide range of community, hospital and mobile settings.

With flexibility, strong learning and development opportunities, and the chance to support people at important moments in their healthcare journey, you can build a rewarding career while making a real difference locally and nationally.

InHealth is a place where you're trusted to do your job well, supported by people who value your expertise and give you the space to act on it. Teams show up for each other, leaders back your judgment and help remove blockers rather than create them.

New opportunities open as we grow - whether that's progressing, moving sideways or taking on something different as your strengths evolve. And everything we do is focussed on making healthcare better - for patients, partners and the people delivering care.

Read more about us here: Who We Are - InHealth Group
