title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
Cherry Hinton Medical Centre, Cambridge

Wish you could prioritise continuity of care and make a difference to your patients? No problem.

Want a manageable workload? How about 25 appointments per day, 15-minute f2f appointments, capped duty session and no private work!?

Miss the old days where being duty doctor was about orchestrating the symphony: hands-off triage, dealing with emergency queries and catching up with admin? No problem.

Not keen on ward rounds? OK, no care homes.

£13,128.51 a session with full CPD allocation as per BMA model contract? Plus paid indemnity

Want the BMA model contract and to never have to ask for the DDRB uplift it will just happen? Read more!

4 sessions a week available:

Working pattern:

Thursday 2 sessions AM/PM

Friday 2 sessions AM/PM

12-13 patients per session, blocked time for home visits, blocked time for daily clinical meeting

Capped duty sessions, no care homes

BMA model contract

Monthly clinical closure afternoon for training and team building

SystmOne practice with full Ardens templates

Time allocated for shared administrative and prescription tasks

Welcome to Cherry Hinton Medical Practice and CGPN

Cherry Hinton is a traditional Cambridge practice supporting face-to-face high-quality consulting, that is led by a GP Federation; Cambs GP Network, CGPN, so you can focus on patients.

We understand for you to deliver high quality care you need an environment that allows you to thrive! That means feeling valued and protected, which is why all of our GPs work to the BMA salaried model contract and detailed job plan, which means; 15minute appointments; 80% of clinical correspondence, all private work outsourced; in-house pharmacy teams for the med reviews; adopter of Cambs LMC/BMA guidance to protect you from workload dumps.

We have an excellent team of GPs, Pharmacy team, PCN Physio, SPLW/Care-coordinator and full in-house management team. Together we enjoy social events, group training events and daily protected clinical meetings.

CGPN is a Federation of Practices across Cambridge with a social enterprise ethos, wholly owned by our local member practices. CGPN adopted Cherry Hinton Medical Practice 3years ago, since the practice has seen massive improvements in QOF achievement (95+%), turnaround in FFT/PPG feedback (now excellent!) protected workloads for clinicians (focus on supporting clinicians to deliver holistic longitudinal care), a revitalised non-clinical and management team. Come and join us to be part of this fantastic, revamped practice!

title: Social Prescriber
descriptionHtml:
We are looking to recruit to the post of social prescribing link worker, to work within our primary care network multi-disciplinary healthcare team, providing 1:1 personalised support to people who are referred to them by team members and local agencies. The social prescriber will work across the practices who are part of the West Enfield Collaborative Primary Care Network: Winchmore Hill Practice, Abernethy House Surgery, The Town Surgery.

This post empowers people to take control of their health and wellbeing by giving time to focus on what matters to me. The social prescribing link worker will build trusting relationships with people, create a shared personalised care and support plan and connect them to local, diverse and culturally appropriate community groups, VCSE organisations and services. They will also work with a diverse range of partners to provide support to community groups and VCSE organisations involved in social prescribing.

This role helps people to work on their wider health and wellbeing, specifically addressing health access and outcomes and wider determinants of their health, such as debt, poor housing and physical inactivity, as well as other lifestyle issues and low-level mental health concerns by increasing peoples active involvement with their local communities. This approach particularly helps people with long term conditions (including support for mental health), people who are lonely or isolated, or who have complex social needs which affect their wellbeing.

title: GP Cardiologist
descriptionHtml:
OUHFT seeks to recruit qualified GPs to be trained to deliver cardiology services as part of a unified team at one of a number of community locations in the region.

The roles are part time, and GP Cardiologists are asked to consider undertaking 1-2 sessions per week (with time off for annual leave, study leave and CPD). Full training will be provided, as will a shadowing programme at OUHFT.

This approach to community cardiology is highly innovative, and seeks to integrate primary and secondary care; to make care more accessible and closer to home; to improve patient experience; to improve outcomes and quality of care, particularly via the identification and holistic treatment of risk factors and co-morbid conditions - including mental health conditions - in patients with known or suspected heart disease.

Each clinic will be supported by a healthcare assistant and secretarial support, who will support you with administrative tasks and enhance the patient experience. Consultant cardiologists will act as mentors, and will be available for advice and help when you need it.

The GP will be a substantive employee of Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, and will have access to the resources of this tertiary centre cardiology service. It is anticipated that, when trained and where appropriate, GP Cardiologists will be able to refer patients directly for cardiac procedures, including advanced imaging, angiography, cardioversion, ablation and pacing.

Integration between primary and secondary care is widely acknowledged to bring advantages to patients and their families through, increased accessibility and improved patient experience; to health care economies through enhanced cost-effectiveness and better value; and to practitioners who may experience opportunities for enhanced professional satisfaction.

OUH seeks to appoint several GP-Cardiologists to develop our services to patients closer to home. Our approach to Community Cardiology is to recruit and train a of motivated, high-caliber general practitioners, who are committed to seeking high standards of patient care for those with known or suspected cardiovascular disease, and who are committed to enhancing both the patient experience of care, and the value created by the healthcare system.

The aims of the posts are

  1. To improve access to expert cardiovascular care
  2. To improve patient experience and provide care closer to home
  3. To enhance holistic patient assessment and treatment, particularly to improve the identification and treatment of co-morbid conditions, including mental health conditions
  4. To create value in the healthcare system by allocating resources effectively
  5. To strengthen primary care by enhancing interactions with secondary care and providing a wider variety of career paths for GPs.

GP Cardiologists will contribute to the management, organisation, governance, educational and academic programs of the clinical service unit. GP Cardiologists will attend and contribute to teaching sessions; will contribute to the intellectual development and academic activities of the department, and may contribute to teaching and training.

City & Hackney Specialist Child and Adolescent Mental Health Service

Consultant Child & Adolescent Psychiatrist

A Consultant Child and Adolescent Psychiatrist is required for City & Hackney Child and Adolescent Mental Health Service. These clinical sessions are located within our Behaviour Support and Outreach Pathway. These are long-established consultant sessions, with the vacancy having arisen following the previous post holder moving on to a new role.

The post-holder would be expected to provide Consultant input and clinical leadership to the Behaviour Support and Outreach Pathway three days per week as well as contribute the assessment clinic and the consultant duty rota. AAC panel date: TBC

This post has arisen due to the previous post holder moving to a new role.

The role of the consultant is to provide psychiatric assessment and treatment where appropriate, contribute a psychiatric perspective, provide senior clinical leadership to the multidisciplinary team, offer consultation to other professionals and agencies and facilitate the development of the team and wider service. In particular, the Consultant Psychiatrist will provide clinical input to psychiatric and crisis assessments, medication reviews, risk assessments and management as well as consultation to the multidisciplinary team. title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
Sanford Surgery is under new management. However, we will still be delivering the same exceptional, patient focused service and working hard to develop the practice even further. With this being our main priority, we are looking for a GP to join the family centric practice on a salaried basis.

This role is a great opportunity for an experienced General Practitioner.

The following are the core responsibilities of the General Practitioner. There may be on occasion, a requirement to carry out other tasks; this will be dependent upon factors such as workload and staffing levels

  • Perform clinical examinations of patients to assess, diagnose and monitor conditions
  • Carry out patient consultations at home and within the surgery
  • Monitor patients' conditions and wellbeing
  • Carry out clinical examinations
  • Diagnose and treat various illnesses/ailments
  • Carry out minor surgery where required
  • Take part in practice management and administration
  • Liaise with other healthcare professionals as part of multidisciplinary teams

Sandford Surgery is a well-established NHS General Practice located in Wareham, Dorset, dedicated to providing high-quality, patient-centred primary healthcare. The practice focuses on delivering safe, effective, and compassionate care for individuals and families.

Our mission is to offer comprehensive medical services that promote health and wellbeing while maintaining a culture of respect, confidentiality, and continuous improvement. We value clinical excellence, patient satisfaction, and community engagement, ensuring care is tailored to individual needs.

Sandford Surgery is committed to maintaining the highest standards of clinical care and patient experience. Our experienced clinical and administrative staff work collaboratively to ensure timely access to services and continuity of care.

employer: North Cumbria Integrated Care NHS Foundation Trust
title: Trust Registrar - Ear, Nose and Throat
descriptionHtml:
NCIC are looking for an enthusiastic, motivated and dynamic Registrar to join our ENT Department.

This post is a Trust appointment and will be subject to the new Terms and Conditions - for NHS Doctors and Dentists (England) 2016.

Any offer of employment with the Trust will be subject to satisfactory pre-employment checks as defined in Health Service Circular 2002/008

The Registrar will be responsible for the day-to-day care of all patients under the ENT Consultants. The programme of training for each individual doctor will be flexible depending on his/her particular needs and stage of training. The candidate will have the same timetable and schedule as a registrar i.e. 4x lists and 3 clinics p/w plus attendance at specialist and combined clinics.

At NCIC, we have an ambition to deliver outstanding healthcare services to the population of North Cumbria. The Trust is committed to creating a centre of excellence in providing rural and remote healthcare and provides a wide range of community and acute services throughout our county.

Our 5 key principles demonstrate our belief in the delivery of 'safe, high quality care every time':

  • Being a clinically led organisation
  • Quality and safety at the heart of our Trust
  • A positive patient experience every time
  • A great place to work
  • Managing our money well

As an organisation we are serious about supporting a diverse workforce that reflects our local community and are very much focused on being an inclusive and compassionate place to work.

Across the North East and North Cumbria we are working together to deliver our ambition to be the greenest region in England by 2030. All staff are expected to support sustainability.

employer: University Hospitals of Morecambe Bay NHS Trust
title: ENT Consultant - Furness General Hospital
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking a Consultant to join the current ENT team in the Trust. You will work Cross Bay with Furness General Hospital as the main site. You will be contracted for 10 sessions per week with the option to increase along with service needs. You will need to have a broad experience in general ENT. Any subspecialty interest in Otology is required and will be actively supported although on calls will need general ENT experience.

University Hospitals of Morecambe Bay NHS Foundation Trust covers a large geographic area which encompasses the Furness peninsula, the city of Lancaster and the Lake District.

Morecambe Bay is nestled between the Lake District national park and the Yorkshire Dales as well as being in easy reach of the cities of Manchester and Liverpool, The area offers affordable accommodation with access to excellent grammar schools ranked as top in the country.

We provide a comprehensive range of acute and support hospital services to a population of 350,000 based around Morecambe Bay. One of the largest employers in the area, we have approximately 6,000 staff working across five sites; Furness General Hospital (Barrow in Furness), Royal Lancaster Infirmary, Westmorland General Hospital (Kendal) and Queen Victoria Centre (Morecambe). By joining us you will be part of a progressive team committed to diversity, excellence and achievement.

The ENT department has 5 consultants, 3 Associate specialists, 7 specialty ENT doctors and 2 junior doctors (CT1/2 at RLI, FY2 at FGH). We have two H&N Clinical Nurse Specialists, one Advanced Nurse Practitioner in post. There are specialized clinics such as a One stop Head & Neck clinic, Combined `Rhinology clinic, Paediatrics clinics, Voice and Vertigo clinic. There are regular audit meetings, radiology meetings and video link meetings for the regional Head & Neck Multi-Disciplinary Team. The weekend on call rota would be 1:5 and weekday 1:4.

We have facilities for Sialendoscopy, Balloon Sinuplasty, and Endoscopic ear surgery, Trans Nasal Oesophagoscopy, BAHA's and DCR's, navigation for endoscopic sinus surgery and nerve monitoring for parotid/ear/thyroid surgery. We aim to provide patient care close to home. Our H&N network is with Royal Preston Hospital but we also have excellent ties with Manchester Royal Infirmary for Skull Base pathology and Rhinology related conditions. For paediatric services we have ties with Alder Hey and Manchester Children's. An elaborate audiology service is available for adults and paediatrics. There is an opportunity for undergraduate and postgraduate teaching as well and we have strong connections with the Lancaster Medical School. We are a paperless department with e-prescribing and e-requesting. We are keen to develop our services further safely and to the highest standard possible keeping in view with our specific geographic demands. We have a high day case rate and encourage any innovation to improve patient safety and experience along with improved efficiency

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
6 Session Salaried GP

We are pleased to be advertising for a Salaried GP to join our established and supportive clinical team, initially on a fixed term basis. This is an opportunity to join a practice where we value continuity of care, collaborative working and a positive working environment.

Located in a pleasant Surrey setting with excellent transport links, Sunbury Health Centre Group Practice provides high-quality care to approximately 19,000 patients and has a strong reputation for teamwork, and clinical excellence.

The Role

We are seeking a committed GP who:

  • Delivers high-quality, patient-centred care
  • Works effectively within a multidisciplinary team
  • Has excellent communication and clinical decision-making skills
  • Is enthusiastic about service development and continuous improvement
  • Values collaborative working and continuity of care

The role includes a mix of routine and acute appointments, participation in clinical triage to support timely access to care and effective patient navigationwith opportunities to develop special interests and contribute to teaching, supervision, or service innovation.

We are a well-established training practice with:

  • 5 GP Partners and 6 Salaried GPs
  • GP Registrars and a strong teaching ethos
  • Experienced Prescribing ANPs, Paramedics, Clinical Pharmacists & Nurses
  • HCAs & Phlebotomists
  • A highly supportive management and administrative team

We are proud to be rated Good in all areas by the Care Quality Commission (CQC), consistently achieve high QOF performance, and maintain strong links with the local ICB and GP Federation.

Our multidisciplinary approach enables clinicians to work collaboratively while maintaining autonomy

What We Offer

  • Competitive salary depending on experience
  • 14 patients per session
  • 15 minute appointments
  • Fair and transparent Duty Doctor rota
  • Home visits undertaken primarily by our dedicated home visiting service
  • A welcoming and genuinely supportive team environment
  • Regular clinical meetings and peer support
  • Opportunities for professional development
  • Mentoring and support for newly qualified GPs if required
  • NHS Pension Scheme
  • High-quality clinical and administrative support
  • Free on-site parking
  • Convenient location with excellent transport links to South West London, Surrey and Berkshire

Informal Visits Welcome

We would be delighted to arrange an informal visit or conversation to tell you more about the role and our practice.

title: General Practitioner (ARRS)
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking an enthusiastic, motivated and patient-focused General Practitioner to join our Primary Care Network (PCN) under the NHS Additional Roles Reimbursement Scheme (ARRS).

This is an exciting opportunity for a GP looking to develop their career within a supportive, collaborative and forward-thinking primary care environment.

The post will be based at Soho Road Primary Care Centre (Dr Bathla), 247251 Soho Road, Birmingham, B21 9RY. The practice serves a diverse local community and is committed to delivering high-quality, accessible and patient-centred healthcare.

The successful candidate will work alongside our established multidisciplinary team, helping to improve patient access, deliver high-quality clinical care and support the growing needs of our local population.

The position offers 46 sessions per week, with an opportunity to contribute to the ongoing development of primary care services within the practice and wider PCN.

Provide high-quality, patient-centred care across the PCN.

Work collaboratively with a multidisciplinary team, including nurses, pharmacists, mental health practitioners, and social prescribers, to ensure integrated patient care.

Conduct consultations, assessments, and follow-ups with patients, utilising ARRS-funded services to support patient needs.

Contribute to the management of chronic disease, health promotion, and disease prevention in line with best practices and PCN goals.

Participate in clinical audits, training, and quality improvement initiatives to enhance patient care within the PCN.

Support the development and implementation of new care pathways that align with ARRS objectives.

Soho Road Primary Care Centre (Dr Bathla) is an established GP practice located at 247251 Soho Road, Birmingham, B21 9RY, serving a diverse and vibrant local community.

We are committed to providing high-quality, compassionate and patient-centred primary care, with a strong emphasis on improving access to healthcare, promoting wellbeing and supporting patients with a wide range of health needs.

Our practice values teamwork, professionalism and continuous improvement. We aim to provide a welcoming and supportive working environment where clinical staff can develop their skills, share knowledge and contribute to the delivery of excellent patient care.

Working collaboratively with our wider Primary Care Network (PCN), we strive to enhance local healthcare services, improve patient outcomes and respond to the evolving needs of our community.

We are looking for an enthusiastic and dedicated GP to join our team and play an important role in delivering accessible, safe and effective general practice services.

employer: South West London and St Georges Mental Health NHS Trust
title: Clinical Fellow in Psychiatry - Rose Ward
descriptionHtml:
Clinical Fellow in Psychiatry - Rose Ward

4 months Fixed Term Contract

Full Time - 40 hours per week

Applications are invited from suitably qualified candidate to work as Clinical Fellow in our Inpatient Wards in General Adult Psychiatry.

This is for Full time (40 hours per week) post at South West London and St George's Mental Health Trust, based at Springfield Hospital, Tooting, London

This post is being offered at the equivalent of Core Trainee level, and the appointment would be at a grade based on the qualifications and experience of the applicant. The post will be for 3 months initially to cover a gap in the Resident Doctor rotation. However, there is the possibility that the post may be extended for a further 4 months, subject to availability and funding.

As this is a short term role, there is no offer of sponsorship for a Skilled Worker visa.

Prospective applicants must ensure that they already have a right to live and work in the UK.

Successful applicants will work at Springfield Hospital, as part of an MDT in in-patient psychiatric wards. The clinical supervisor will be the ward consultant, who is solely based on the ward. The ward also has a GP trainee and Middle Grade doctor.

The post is suitable for doctors at several stages of their career including Post Foundation Year 2 and doctors seeking attainment of specific expertise in an FY3 year.

The post will also suit doctors seeking to enhance their portfolio to gain entry to the training grades and doctors already in non-training Grade positions e.g. SAS doctors or Trust Fellows who are seeking a formal educational structure to their posts.

Training, educational opportunities will be available to successful candidates, including attendance at the weekly academic programme.

There is no out of hours on-call duty for this role. However, there may be an opportunity to take part in the on-call rota to cover gaps, if desired and subject to availability.

Participation in the Daytime Duty Doctor cover is mandatory.

If you are an energetic and motivated doctor who would like to join our service, then we would like to hear from you. We look forward to receiving your application.

We are Proud to Belong at South West London and St George's Mental Health NHS Trust.

We have expert services, a rich history and a clear commitment to providing the best quality care for those with mental ill-health. The Care Quality Commission already rates our services as 'good' - we aspire to be 'outstanding'.

This is a great time to join us. We are transforming the way we care for our communities to support our mission of Making Life Better Together. We have built two brand new mental health facilities at Springfield University Hospital, which are amongst the best in the world. More developments are planned across our sites and services.

We are inclusive and diverse and strive to be actively anti racist. We want to attract people from all backgrounds and experiences to enrich the work we do together. We are proud to co-produce and involve our local communities in all that we do.

We offer flexible working, career development and a variety ofbenefits to enable a positive, welcoming environment in which our people and their careers can thrive.

employer: Kettering General Hospital NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant in Neurology
descriptionHtml:
The postholder's duties will be primarily at Kettering General Hospital. Time for specialist interest clinic/ research and to carry out teaching duties as required could be arranged according to the interest of the appointee. The postholder will be responsible for providing a comprehensive general outpatient neurology service to the catchment area of Kettering General Hospital, alongside the existing Neurology consultants and Neurology specialist nurses.

The postholder will also be providing specialist inpatient review where required, if inpatient beds required the postholder will have access to inpatient beds at Kettering general hospital. JD Pending Royal College Approval

Responses should reflect your own experience, skills and knowledge, as over-reliance on AI-generated content may result in generic answers that do not accurately represent your abilities.

Working together enables us to share expertise, strengthen services and create greater opportunities, and there may be a requirement to work across sites depending on service needs.

Our Excellence Values are Compassion, Accountability, Respect, Integrity and Courage. UHN welcomes applications from all backgrounds and is committed to an inclusive working environment. We are proud signatories of the Armed Forces Covenant and hold the Gold Award under the Employer Recognition Scheme. Candidates who identify as members of the Armed Forces community and meet the essential criteria will be guaranteed an interview.

employer: The Shrewsbury and Telford Hospital NHS Trust
title: Specialist in Plastic Surgery (Skin)
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for a specialist plastic surgeon to deliver dermatology skin procedures in an outpatient setting with 1 session a month in theatres. If you are looking for a specialist post where you can genuinely shape the future of dermatology in Shropshire, train your dermatology colleagues to expand their surgical scopes of practice, influence major service redesign and integration with our community partners, and be part of one of the most ambitious hospital transformation programmes in the NHS -- this is it.

Our Trust is on the brink of a once-in-a-generation change. Backed by £312 million of investment, the Hospital Transformation Programme will create:

o A single acute site at The Royal Shrewsbury Hospital, home to a new 30-bed Critical Care Unit, a modern Emergency Department, and a state-of-the-art Women's and Children's Hospitalo A dedicated planned care site at The Princess Royal Hospital, supporting high-quality elective surgery and improved patient flowThis is your opportunity to join us at the perfect moment -- early enough to influence the design and delivery of future services, but close enough to opening that you'll see your impact become reality.

Our dermatology service will be undergoing significant improvement. We are looking for a specialist grade who wants to continue this momentum -- colleagues who are energised by improvement, motivated by challenge, and excited to help shape a service that women and families can trust.

Main Clinical Duties include:

  • Undertake outpatient dermatology skin procedures.
  • Partake in the skin MDT as a core member.
  • Undertake 1 session per month skin surgery in theatres.
  • Provide support to the dermatology service and medical students by actively contributing to training and continuity of service.
  • To have excellent team-working skills with the abilities and professional attitude to work well in a multi-professional team.
  • The post holder will also contribute to service development. This may involve contributing to Ockenden recommendations, QIPs, audit projects, guideline updates or teaching and training. Including supporting the shift of elective activity out of a theatre environment and into an outpatient setting inline with GIRFT.
  • To deliver clinical and quality targets agreed both nationally and locally with clinical teams and commissioners.

The Shrewsbury and Telford Hospital NHS Trust (SaTH) is the main provider of acute hospital services in Shropshire, Telford & Wrekin and mid Wales.

Our main service locations are the Princess Royal Hospital (PRH) in Telford and the Royal Shrewsbury Hospital (RSH) in Shrewsbury which are located 20 minutes' drive apart. Together they provide 99% of our activity. Both hospitals provide a wide range of acute hospital services including accident & emergency, outpatients, diagnostics, inpatient medical care and critical care.

Our Poppy's Promise Commitment

We believe that compassionate care sits at the heart of everything we do. Every member of our team -- clinical or non-clinical -- plays a vital role in ensuring that patients, families, and colleagues are treated with dignity, empathy, and respect at all times.

We expect all staff to demonstrate compassion not only through their words, but through their actions: by listening attentively, communicating clearly and kindly, and recognising individual needs, feelings, and circumstances of those in our care.

Effective communication is central to safe and high-quality healthcare. We value colleagues who take the time to understand others, explain information in a meaningful way, and respond to concerns with patience and understanding.

By joining our team, you are committing to uphold these values -- ensuring that every patient feels heard, respected, and valued, and that compassion is embedded in every interaction, every day.

title: Training Programme Director - Nuclear Medicine London
descriptionHtml:
An outstanding individual or individuals is sought to fulfil the role of Training Programme Director for Nuclear Medicine for London.

The role of Training Programme Director is to work with and support the Postgraduate Dean in leading the delivery of a wide range of functions within their specialty, aligned to the NHS England mandate. The Programme Director will ensure that both national standards, determined by the Royal College and also guidelines and standards established withinMedicine are met.

The successful applicant will work closely with the Head of School, other Medicine TPDs, LaSE team including; PGMDE Business Manager, Postgraduate Dean, and other key departments including Quality.

They will work with the Postgraduate Dean to produce doctors who will strive for the highest standards of patient-centred care and commit themselves to a lifetime of professional development.

The Programme Director will ensure that both national standards, determined by the Royal College, and guidelines and standards established within Nuclear Medicine are met. Responsibilities will include:

  • To oversee the Specialty's Regional Training Programme
  • Specialty-specific matters and trainee/trainer concerns
  • Recruitment to training posts and programmes
  • Postgraduate programme management, including assessments, progression, rotations, support and remediation, OOP management, trainee management careers support, less than full-time training, inter-deanery transfer, academic training and other related work-streams.

The ideal candidate will be an experienced NHS Consultant with a thorough understanding of Nuclear Medicine across the region and who will also have strong leadership and communication skills and be able to work effectively as a member of a multi-professional team.

NHS England has a wide range of statutory functions, responsibilities and regulatory powers. These are focused on supporting the wider NHS to deliver high quality care, as well as doing those things that are best done once for the whole NHS.

Our staff bring expertise across clinical, operational, commissioning, technology, data science, cyber security, software engineering, education, and commercial specialisms -- enabling us to design and deliver high-quality NHS services.

In March 2025, the Government announced that NHS England and the Department of Health and Social Care will increasingly merge functions, ultimately leading to NHS England being fully integrated into the department.

If you currently work within the NHS and if successful at interview, we will initiate an Inter Authority Transfer (IAT) via the Electronic Staff Record (ESR).This retrieves key data from your current or previous NHS employer to support onboarding, including competency status, Continuous Service Dates (CSD), and annual leave entitlement. You may opt out at any stage of the process.

Colleagues with a contractual office base are expected to spend, on average, at least 40% of their time working in our offices.

We cannot offer visa sponsorship for any vacancies.

title: Newly Qualified GP Opportunity  Central and South PCN (ARRS Role)
descriptionHtml:
Employed by Roby Medical Centre on behalf of Central & South PCN

We are looking for a newly qualified GP to join Central and South Primary Care Network, employed by Roby Medical Centre. This is a structured and well-supported opportunity to build confidence, develop clinical practice, and work within a collaborative system.

This role is funded through the Additional Roles Reimbursement Scheme (ARRS) and is open to GPs within two years of CCT who have not yet held a substantive post.

The Role

You will work within a supportive PCN model, delivering high-quality care across one, or at most two, practices within the network (depending on sessions agreed).

You will:

  • Deliver face-to-face and telephone consultations
  • Manage acute and routine presentations
  • Prescribe safely in line with local and national guidance
  • Complete clinical administration including referrals, results and prescriptions
  • Undertake home visits where clinically appropriate
  • Work within a multidisciplinary team to deliver coordinated care

Contribute to extended access services on a pro-rata basis

Support, Supervision and Development

You will have:

  • Structured supervision and mentorship
  • Dedicated education and supervision sessions built into the role
  • Access to experienced GP Partners and Clinical Directors
  • A network-wide MDT including pharmacists, ACPs, paramedics and care coordinators

A culture of shared learning and clinical support

About Central & South PCN

Central and South PCN is a collaborative network of 11 practices delivering care to a diverse population, with a shared workforce model and a focus on sustainable general practice.

Apply by sending your CV and a short supporting statement to: Jenny.turner2@knowsleyccg.nhs.uk

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
Salaried GP - 4 to 8 sessions per week.

Are you a mid-career GP seeking a move to a forward looking innovative practice?

Are you a highly motivated, newly qualified GP looking for a well supported first substantive role?

Yes? Then please read on

Stowhealth is a friendly, innovative and exciting GP practice which prides itself on outstanding patient care, excellent patient access and good systems to support our clinicians.

Why not join us?

Salary competitive + NHS pension and indemnity cover

title: Consultant Paediatric Interventional Cardiologist
descriptionHtml:
This is a new substantive consultant post to join eleven other consultants in delivering cardiology services to the paediatric population of the West Midlands. The Cardiac unit at the Birmingham Children's Hospital is an established centre of excellence and also acts as a supra-regional and international referral centre for cardiology and cardiac surgery. The post is designed to reduce the overall commitments of the current consultant body by redistribution of existing workload, in particular the delivery of non-invasive services provided by the department.

The successful candidate is expected to participate in the management of the current cardiac patient population and will be expected to develop specialised areas of interest to complement the clinical practice of the existing consultants.

Applicants must be registered with full GMC and must be eligible to practice in the UK. It would be preferable that they have completed Higher Specialist Training in Paediatric Cardiology and be eligible to be on the Specialist Register to have their CCT or be expecting their CCT within 6 months of advertising the post.

This position has been created to support the existing interventional cardiology team. The post holder will work in cooperation with the present consultants to provide a strong consultant presence in clinical areas which in turn will reduce the clinical workload of junior and middle grade medical staff and thereby improve the training. The post is suitable for a new or early career interventional paediatric cardiologist with a view to working with an experienced interventional team.

The successful candidate will take part in the existing on-call structure and be a part of the invasive on-call team. The current working pattern is 1 in 11 on service weeks, with the on-service consultant covering Monday-Thursday, and the following weekend. The interventional cardiology team provides interventional on call cover during on call by a non-invasive cardiologist (1:4).

There is a flexible approach to sharing facilities for when not on service.

There are regular outreach clinics throughout the region of which the post holder will be expected to support.

Birmingham Women's and Children's NHS Foundation Trust is the first of its type in the UK. Our Trust was formed in February 2017 to drive forward our commitment to provide the highest quality, world-class care for our women, children and families. Uniting our hospitals means more seamless care; more investment to make greater advances in our specialist treatment and world-leading neo-natal and fetal work. Importantly, it also gives us a greater voice in shaping the future of family-centered care.

Birmingham Children's Hospital is a UK leading specialist paediatric centre with an international reputation in several areas.

Birmingham Women's Hospital is one of two dedicated women's hospitals in the UK, with the busiest single site maternity unit, delivering more than 8,200 babies a year offering a full range of gynaecological, maternity and neonatal care.

Our Trust is committed to creating the best place to work. title: Consultant Endocrinologist  West of England Gender Clinic
descriptionHtml:
This is a distinctive opportunity for a Consultant Endocrinologist to help shape to continue high-quality gender healthcare at the West of England Specialist Gender Identity Clinic. Working remotely for one programmed activity each week, you will bring specialist endocrine expertise to an experienced multidisciplinary service and provide advice on gender-affirming hormone therapy for the prescribing team. The role is primarily advisory and supervisory rather than one of routine direct patient management. You will support medical and non-medical prescribers with complex clinical decisions, strengthen prescribing governance and help develop evidence-based practice across the service. You will have scope to influence protocols, education and service development while working collaboratively with colleagues who are committed to person-centred care and continuous improvement. We welcome applications from consultants who want to use their endocrine expertise in a focused, clinically influential role. Job-share applications are welcomed.

You will provide specialist endocrine advice to the clinics medical and non-medical prescribing teams on medical readiness for GAHT, treatment initiation, adjustment, monitoring and ongoing management. You will advise on complex cases, including physical health comorbidity, treatment complications, atypical blood results, contraindications, clinical risk and uncertainty about treatment options. You will review cases submitted through the agreed referral process, provide documented specialist recommendations and contribute to multidisciplinary discussion when required. This includes advising on individualised care for people with non-binary gender goals and liaising with primary, secondary and specialist services where needed. You will contribute to the weekly hormone prescribing forum, offering case-based advice and teaching as time allows. You will also support the development and specialist review of prescribing guidelines, standard operating procedures, clinical protocols, shared-care agreements and teaching materials. The role includes supporting prescriber education and safe practice, and contributing to clinical governance, audit, quality improvement and service development relating to endocrine care and prescribing.

employer: University Hospital of North Midlands NHS Trust
title: Consultant Musculoskeletal Radiologist
descriptionHtml:
An exciting opportunity to join a team of 48 WTE Consultant Radiologists, including 8 substantive Consultants with sub-specialty interest in musculoskeletal imaging.

At UHNM the cross-sectional radiologists work closely with their colleagues in the Surgical and Medical Directorate through cancer MDT meetings and joint clinico-radiological meetings.

The successful applicant will share responsibilities to support the Trauma and Orthopaedics, Spinal and Rheumatology Departments through Multi-Disciplinary team meetings. Currently Spine, Rheumatology, Diabetes, Orthopaedic and Tumour MDTs are in place and there is rotation between all relevant radiologists.

Duties will include providing a comprehensive diagnostic and interventional musculoskeletal imaging service across the Trust. The post holder should be a dedicated clinician wishing to actively assist and further develop Musculoskeletal Radiology services in the Trust.

There is a well established skill-mix within MSK with a large number of advanced practitioners and consultant radiographers who report plain films, sonographers who perform and report MSK diagnostic US examinations and an advanced practitioner who reports knee and spine MRI exams.

As a MSK consultant radiologist at UHNM you will be working with some of the latest equipment available in a purpose built department.

UHNM is a tertiary referral centre for Trauma and Orthopaedics serving Staffordshire, Shropshire, South Cheshire and Wolverhampton. The Trauma and orthopaedics department has 28 consultants and 3 SAS and the spinal team has 9 dedicated spinal consultants and 1 SAS surgeon providing all aspects of trauma and orthopaedics and spinal services including deformity correction, oncology surgery and trauma. There is a huge demand for MSK intervention services for procedures including image guided injections, arthrography, myelography, biopsies, nerve root blocks and vertebroplasty and the post holder is expected to contribute to this type of work.

The department performs and reports approximately 400,000 examinations per annum, with a high proportion of complex imaging and procedural radiology.

A Community Diagnostic Centre opened in Spring 2026.

We use an award-winning PACS which allows for easy streamlined, efficient and trouble-free reporting from either centre utilising PACS based reporting.

The post holder will contribute to the delivery of a high quality radiology service within a busy imaging department providing both general and specialist services in diagnostics and interventional imaging.

You will contribute to the weekday on-call service on rotation with also a 1 in 8 rota for Saturdays or Sundays.

The job plan will include CPD SPA

We are the specialist centre for major trauma for the North Midlands and North Wales. The Trauma and orthopaedics department provides all aspects of trauma and orthopaedics and spinal services including deformity correction, oncology surgery and trauma. There is a huge demand for MSK intervention services for procedures including image guided injections, arthrography, myelography, biopsies, nerve root blocks and vertebroplasty and the post holder is expected to contribute to this type of work.

The Haywood Hospital has specialist services for rheumatology and rehabilitation. The Rheumatology centre at the Haywood Hospital welcomes patients from North Staffordshire, Derbyshire and Cheshire. title: ENT Specialty Doctor
descriptionHtml:
An opportunity has arisen to join the Department of Otolaryngology / Head & Neck Surgery at University Hospitals Bristol & Weston NHS Foundation Trust. We have a 1-year fixed term position available from January 2027.

The job roles will comprise of otology, rhinology & Head and Neck outpatient clinics both face to face and telephone clinics, and will include theatre attendance.

The ENT service provides adult and paediatric outpatient and inpatient ENT activity at the major teaching hospital in Bristol, but also provides outreach clinics and inpatient support and advice across a range of other sites including Southmead Hospital and Weston General Hospital.

The Trust is the regional centre for otolaryngology, major head and neck surgery, skull base surgery, major ear surgery and hearing implantation.

The posts would suit a doctor who has completed core surgical training (or equivalent) and has experience in ENT.

It is also anticipated that the successful candidate will contribute to the academic, research and teaching aspects of the posts as it is based within the major regional teaching hospital.

Clinical duties

Clinical duties include outpatient clinics, operating and emergency care. These activities occur in the University Hospitals Bristol & Weston precinct and at Southmead Hospital NBT Trust, this post will require travel to all activity areas. The successful candidate will be expected to comply with all relevant Trust policies relating to administration of patient care.

Management and Leadership Responsibilities

The management responsibility of the post-holder will be to the departmental clinical lead and the Divisional Clinical Chair who is responsible to the Chief Executive and Trust Board.

University Hospitals Bristol and Weston NHS Foundation Trust (UHBW) is one of the largest acute Trusts in the country, bringing together a combined workforce of over 13,000 staff and over 100 different clinical services across 10 different sites, serving a core population of more than 500,000 people across South West England. UHBW has been rated by the CQC as 'Good' overall and our staff are proud to deliver excellent care to the people of Bristol, Weston and beyond. As a forward- thinking multi-award winning Trust and a digital exemplar committed to improving patient care, our world-leading research and innovations are having a positive local and global impact. Our hospitals are spread across Bristol and Weston, join us and you can enjoy the very best of both worlds; city living within a stone's throw of the countryside or beside the seaside, both with easy access to all that the South West has to offer. UHBW is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children, young people and vulnerable adults. As an equal opportunities employer actively working towards a diverse workforce we aim to recruit and retain a workforce which represents the rich diversity of the local population at all levels and are committed to designing our services around the needs of individual patients and those around them. title: Clinical Director for Obstetrics and Gynaecology
descriptionHtml:
An exciting opportunity has arisen for an experienced and inspirational Consultant Obstetrician and Gynaecologist to join Somerset NHS Foundation Trust as Clinical Director for Obstetrics and Gynaecology.

This full-time 10 PA leadership post offers the opportunity to shape the future of women's health services across Somerset at both Musgrove Park Hospital and Yeovil District Hospital.

As Clinical Director, you will provide strategic, professional and operational medical leadership across a broad portfolio including maternity, obstetrics, benign and acute gynaecology, specialist women's health services, diagnostics, workforce development and research.

Working closely with clinical, operational, nursing and midwifery colleagues, you will lead service transformation, quality improvement and workforce development to ensure the delivery of safe, effective and compassionate care for women, babies and families across the county.

This is a rare opportunity to influence strategy, drive meaningful change and leave a lasting legacy within one of England's most integrated healthcare organisations. We are committed to appointing the right individual and will work collaboratively to develop a job plan that reflects your experience, strengths and aspirations whilst ensuring the leadership requirements of the service are met.

We would be delighted to discuss the role, introduce you to colleagues across both sites and share our ambitions for the future of Women's Services in Somerset.

As Clinical Director for Obstetrics and Gynaecology, you will:

  • Provide visible clinical leadership across women's health services, fostering collaboration between Musgrove Park Hospital and Yeovil District Hospital.
  • Develop and deliver a clear county-wide strategy for Obstetrics and Gynaecology, aligned with Trust and system priorities.
  • Lead on quality, safety and clinical governance, ensuring learning from incidents, reviews, audits and patient feedback drives sustained improvement.
  • Support delivery of the Maternity and Neonatal Improvement Plan and provide strategic oversight of maternity, obstetric and gynaecology services.
  • Work with multidisciplinary teams to improve patient experience, access standards, elective recovery, cancer pathways and service performance.
  • Share accountability for workforce, operational, quality and financial objectives across the service.
  • Support recruitment, retention, succession planning and the development of future clinical leaders.
  • Lead transformational projects and pathway redesign across acute, community and primary care services.
  • Build strong relationships with patients, families, commissioners, education partners and regional networks to support the delivery of high-quality services.
  • Promote a culture of inclusion, innovation, research, continuous improvement and compassionate leadership.

At Somerset NHS Foundation Trust, we're committed to supporting our employees with a range of benefits designed to enhance your professional and personal life. We offer:

  • Flexible working options to help you balance work and life
  • NHS pension scheme for long-term financial security
  • Generous annual leave allowance to recharge and relax
  • A strong focus on career development to help you grow and achieve your potential

Additionally, you'll gain access to our Blue Light Card, unlocking exclusive discounts on shopping, dining, and leisure activities, as well as NHS-specific perks to support you both inside and outside of work.

We are proud to foster a diverse, skilled, and inclusive workforce, and we encourage applications from all backgrounds.

Why Somerset? Somerset offers the perfect blend of idyllic countryside, outstanding areas of natural beauty, and breathtaking coastlines, with vibrant cities like Bristol, Bath, and Exeter just a short drive away - and only two hours to London.

The region is home to excellent educational facilities, and with affordable housing compared to other parts of the country, it's a great place to build both your career and your future.

Somerset truly has it all - the peaceful countryside and cosmopolitan city life, with something for everyone to enjoy.

title: Consultant Rheumatologist
descriptionHtml:
This a new full time Consultant post for a consultant rheumatologist to join the 3 existing full time Consultant Rheumatologists and 1 part time consultant , based at Northampton General Hospital. It is essential that the post-holder should hold the MRCP (UK) or an equivalent qualification and be on the GMC specialist register or will obtain a relevant CCT/CESR(CP) within 6 months of interview.

The successful applicant will join the existing consultant team and our team of specialist nurses in delivering outpatient rheumatology care. We are a training department with an ST3 (from the East Midlands Deanery), an IMT doctor (on the Leicester medical rotation) and medical students from Leicester Medical School. We participate in Leicester and Oxford regional training meetings.

This post has approval from the Royal College of Physicians for 10PAs in the first instance. The timetable will include 4-5 outpatient clinics per week, support for the nurse led helpline, cover for the inpatient advice service during working hours and admitting rights if required for rheumatology patients. These are generally managed with shared medical care from the ward based medical teams.

We have a full complement of biologic and chemotherapeutic services, administered via our medical day unit with dedicated nurses for infusions. We also offer the opportunity of involvement in clinical trials with an established research and development unit with an increasing number of rheumatology portfolio studies.

Please submit your application as soon as possible, as we reserve the right to close adverts once sufficient applications have been received.

descriptionHtml:
Consultant Radiologist

We are looking for General Radiologists, subspeciality interests are welcome and to be included in application.

The Radiology department is well-equipped, having two 128 slice Siemens CT scanners, two 1.5T Siemens MRI scanners, digital screening rooms and updated US machines. employer: Cambridge University Hospital NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant in Haematology (8PA)
descriptionHtml:
Applications are invited for the post of Consultant in Haematology (8PA) at Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (CUH), based at Addenbrooke's Hospital.

This post will strengthen our integrated clinical and laboratory haematology service, with leadership responsibilities for the general Haematology Laboratory in the trust and deputy leadership within the Specialist Haemoglobinopathy Team. The appointee will support immune haematology, thrombosis and haemostasis, diagnostic laboratory haematology and the regional red-cell apheresis network.

We are seeking an enthusiastic colleague committed to safe, kind and excellent care, multidisciplinary working, education, governance and service improvement. The post includes participation in the general medical haematology on-call rota, including support for Royal Papworth Hospital.

Interviews for this post will be held in person on 25 November 2026 at Addenbrooke's Hospital, Cambridge. Specific details will be provided to shortlisted candidates.

The successful applicant will work with consultant colleagues to deliver care for adults with general and non-malignant haematological disorders. Key duties include leading general Haematology Laboratory; acting as deputy lead for adult Haemoglobinopathy services; contributing to haemoglobinopathy, Immune haematology and Thrombophilia clinics; and supporting inpatient and GP liaison. They will provide consultant governance for red-cell apheresis in collaboration with UCLH and partner services in Ipswich and Luton, participate in blood-film reporting and laboratory supervision, and contribute to teaching for resident doctors, biomedical scientists and medical students. They will take part in clinical governance, audit, continuing professional development and the general haematology consultant-of-the-week and out-of-hours rotas.

They will be fully registered with the GMC and ideally have a CCT in Haematology or be within six months of award of CCT at the time of interview. Applications are welcomed from those unable to work full time for personal reasons or those wishing to job-share.

Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust combines local acute care with regional and national specialist services, teaching and research on the Cambridge Biomedical Campus. The Medical Haematology Department provides an integrated clinical and laboratory service and is a tertiary referral centre for complex non-malignant haematological disorders. The appointee will join a collaborative multidisciplinary team with strong links to the University of Cambridge, UCLH, NHS Blood and Transplant, Royal Papworth Hospital and regional partner trusts. Our CUH Together values are Safe, Kind and Excellent, and we welcome colleagues who will contribute to inclusive teamworking, evidence-based practice, education, research and continuous improvement.

The applicant must have demonstrable skills in listening, reading, writing and speaking in English that enable effective communication about medical topics with patients and colleagues, as set out in the GMC's Good Medical Practice (2013). Non-UK applicants must possess the IELTS/OET exam before obtaining a GMC licence to practice.

Applications from job seekers who require skilled worker sponsorship to work in the UK are welcome and will be considered alongside all other applications. For further information please visit the UK Visas and Immigration website.

Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is an Equal Opportunities Employer.

descriptionHtml:
oin our team as a Specialist Harm Reduction Worker in Fife on a fixed term basis.

Our Specialist Harm Reduction Workers play a vital role in supporting clients, providing information and advice in relation to reducing drug and alcohol related harm, including promoting safer drug use practices; working with individuals most at risk.

title: ARRS GP
descriptionHtml:

We place great value on teamwork, staff wellbeing, and professional development, creating an environment where colleagues feel supported to grow and thrive.

As a practice, we are passionate about serving our diverse patient population and making a positive difference to the health and wellbeing of our community every day.
