employer: Dorset HealthCare University NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Psychiatrist - Early Intervention in Psychosis & ARMS
descriptionHtml:
We have an exciting opportunity for a Consultant Psychiatrist to join our supportive and developing specialist service, where you will provide clinical leadership, contribute to service development and help shape the future of Early Intervention in Psychosis (EIP) and At-Risk Mental State (ARMS) services across Dorset. This is a newly created role with an exciting opportunity to develop the service.

Based at the Hillcrest Unit in Bournemouth, you will work as part of a pan-Dorset multidisciplinary team delivering high-quality, recovery-focused care. EIP supports people aged 14-65, while ARMS supports young people aged 14-35.

This varied role offers the opportunity to provide specialist clinical expertise in assessing and managing of complex mental health presentations, including psychosis. You will undertake new patient assessments, medical reviews, Mental Health Act assessments, tribunal work and care planning, delivered across clinic, community and home settings where appropriate.

You will join a supportive, forward-thinking specialist service committed to excellent patient outcomes. ARMS is primarily psychologically led, with medical oversight from the Consultant Psychiatrist. Referrals come from community, CMHT, primary care and inpatient services, providing an opportunity to work across the wider general adult pathway.

If you would like to discuss how this role could work for you please contact our Associate Medical Director, Dr Eman Shweikh 01202 492083

As Consultant Psychiatrist you'll provide clinical leadership and expert psychiatric assessment and management within EIP and ARMS. You'll work closely with multidisciplinary colleagues, including an Advanced Clinical Practitioner to deliver safe, effective and person-centred care in clinic and community settings

You'll contribute to assessments, medical reviews, Mental Health Act assessments, tribunals, discharge planning and collaborative care with community mental health teams, inpatient services and primary care. You'll support the interface between EIP, ARMS and wider general adult pathway.

This post attracts an Enhanced Recruitment and Retention: A payment of £20,000 to be paid as two lump sums. The first £10,000 will be paid on appointment in the role and the remaining £10,000 will be made on the anniversary of the start date. Both payments will be subject to deductions at source, plus a further relocation package of up to £10,000 if relocating to Dorset. We also offer flexible working, a supportive Consultant body, excellent NHS benefits, 10 days' study leave and an annual study budget of up to £1,000.

You'll have the opportunity to participate in the county-wide senior on-call rota, attracting a 3% availability supplement plus 0.75 APA per week, with an on-call frequency of approximately 1 in 21. Dedicated administrative support is provided, with opportunities for teaching, research, quality improvement and service development.

Join our Medical Team :: Careers Dorset

At Dorset HealthCare we're on a mission to empower people to make the most of their lives through our outstanding, joined-up healthcare services. We're a dynamic, forward-looking Trust, running 12 community hospitals, specialist inpatient facilities and a wide range of integrated community and mental health services for a population of almost 800,000 people.

We do things differently here - it's one of the reasons the CQC rated us 'outstanding' in 2019. It's also why 95% of patients across our services say they have a good or very good experience of our services and 89% of staff feel they can really make a difference. Whether you're looking to work with us in one of our bustling market towns, vibrant urban locations, thriving seaside spots, or among the rolling hills of Dorset, there are lots of ways you can make a difference in our communities.

We're an inclusive workplace, where everyone is welcome, everyone can be authentic, and we are all encouraged to be the best version of ourselves.

Working with us you'll be part of a strong team, challenge yourself, build a career, and teach us what we don't know. And you'll be working towards our vision to be better every day through excellence, compassion and expertise in all we do.

employer: Cambridge University Hospital NHS Foundation Trust

descriptionHtml:

title: Consultant Dermatologist
descriptionHtml:
An exciting opportunity to work within a busy, friendly and dynamic dermatology department based over two hospital sites, Royal Blackburn Hospital and Burnley General Hospital has become available.

title: GP with Entended Role
descriptionHtml:
ProcareHaslemere Community Hospital

We are looking for experienced and enthusiastic GPs to join the Haslemere Proactive Care Hub, working as part of a multidisciplinary team supporting people living with frailty, multiple long-term conditions and complex care needs.

The Hub brings together primary care, community services and specialist expertise to provide more proactive, coordinated care closer to home.

Our aim is simple: to identify people who would benefit from additional support earlier, bring the right professionals around them and help prevent deterioration and avoidable hospital admission.

GP with Extended Role Proactive Long Term Conditions Hub4-6 sessions per week

We are also looking for GPs who have a particular interest in frailty, complex multimorbidity, long-term conditions and proactive community care.

This is predominantly a clinical role, working directly with patients and alongside the wider Hub multidisciplinary team.

You will undertake comprehensive assessment of people with frailty and complex needs, including Comprehensive Geriatric Assessment (CGA); provide GP clinical review and sense-checking of specialist recommendations; support medication optimisation; develop personalised care and anticipatory care plans; and work alongside specialist clinicians, pharmacists, therapists, community nursing, social care, mental health and other members of the MDT.

A particularly important part of the role will be bringing the generalist GP perspective to complex care looking beyond individual conditions and ensuring that recommendations are practical, coordinated and appropriate for the person as a whole.

You do not need to be a specialist geriatrician. We are looking for experienced GPs with an interest in developing this area of practice and enthusiasm for working differently across traditional organisational boundaries

Why join us?

This is an opportunity to be part of a developing model of care that brings primary care and community services together around some of our most complex patients.

You will have the opportunity to work closely with experienced clinicians from across primary, community and specialist care, influence how the Hub develops and help demonstrate what genuinely integrated, proactive care can achieve for patients.

based primarily at Haslemere Community Hospital.

For an informal conversation about either opportunity, please contact Jane Fagan, Chief Operating Officer.

To apply: Please submit a CV outlining your experience, and what you feel you could bring to the Haslemere Proactive Care Hub to procare.people@nhs.net

title: Locum Consultant
descriptionHtml:
This locum consultant post will provide medical leadership and consultant psychiatric input to Hammersmith & Fulham's Complex Psychosis Team, which brings together the Community Rehabilitation Service (CRS) and Assertive Outreach (AO) function under a single clinical and operational structure.

During the appointment, the post holder will provide consultant input across both arms of the service, working closely with the Team Manager, Service Manager and multidisciplinary team, and providing supervision to the team's Specialty Doctor.

Provide overall medical leadership across both arms of the Complex Psychosis Team, working in partnership with the Band 8a Team Manager.

Undertake senior assessment and direct clinical input for the most complex cases across CRS and AO, including risk and medication management, diagnostic assessment, Mental Health Act assessments and CTO reviews.

Support the team's duty function for urgent concerns and assessments.

Act as named supervising consultant for the 1 WTE SAS doctor being recruited to the team (see Sections 8 and 10).

Lead, with the Team Manager and tri-borough steering group, on finalising the local clinical and operational model, SOPs and interfaces with MINT, EIP, inpatient services and primary care during the mobilisation and embedding phases (see Section 2).

Provide a liaison/advice function to GPs and Primary Care Networks and to referring teams (MINT, EIP, CATT, inpatients) regarding the AO/CRS pathway and thresholds.

Contribute to tri-borough clinical governance, audit and the service's evaluation metrics (attempted versus realised contacts, 14-day re-engagement, crisis presentations) reported to the Productivity Forum and H&F Local Services SMT.

West London NHS Trust is one of the most diverse healthcare providers in the UK, delivering a range of mental health and physical healthcare and community services. The Trust runs Broadmoor Hospital, one of three high secure hospitals in the country, with an international reputation.

Our high secure services care for patients from South of England and we provide low and medium secure services across eight London boroughs. The Trust also provides mental and physical healthcare in three London boroughs (Ealing, Hounslow and Hammersmith & Fulham). We employ over 5,000 staff, of whom 59% are BME. Our turnover for 2024-25 is over £500m.

The Trust is rated as 'Good' overallby the Care Quality Commission. Forensic services are rated as 'Outstanding'.

The Trust is an established partner and contributor in the development of the evolving North West London Integrated Care System and the Integrated Care Board. The Trust leads the NW London Children and Adolescent Mental Health provider collaborative.

employer: University College London Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
title: Trust Grade Doctor (Stroke)
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking a highly motivated ST3+ Trust Grade Doctor (SPR Level) to join the UCLH Comprehensive Stroke Service. Based at the National Hospital for Neurology and Neurosurgery (NHNN) in Queen Square and UCH on Euston Road, London, this role offers a unique opportunity to gain extensive experience in one of the UK's largest stroke services.

As a Stroke Fellow, you will rotate through core and specialist stroke roles, participate in governance and teaching programs, and work within a 24/7 mechanical thrombectomy service and hyperacute stroke unit. You will also engage in a variety of multidisciplinary teams and contribute to pre-hospital stroke video triage.

This position provides excellent training in the management of stroke across all stages of care, with ample opportunities for service development and clinical research. You will receive the same educational supervision as other stroke SpRs with NTNs and have the chance to observe and learn from a broad range of specialist neurological clinics.

NHNN is internationally recognized for its clinical care and research, offering comprehensive care for a wide range of neurological conditions. The role includes daily teaching opportunities and the chance to work closely with experts in various neurological fields.

Clinical Rotations:Engage in core and specialist stroke roles, including hyperacute and acute stroke units, general and specialist stroke clinics, and the 24/7 mechanical thrombectomy service. Participate in pre-hospital video triage and assessment for potential stroke cases in north London.

Patient Care:Deliver comprehensive care at all stages of stroke management, from pre-hospital to post-hospital. Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams such as cardiology, neurosurgery, and haematology for integrated stroke care.

Governance and Quality Improvement:Involve in clinical governance activities like audits, case reviews, and quality improvement projects to enhance stroke care services.

Teaching and Education:Engage in the teaching program, including grand rounds, bedside teaching, and tutorials. Participate in weekly protected teaching sessions related to the stroke curriculum.

Research and Development:Support clinical research at the NIHR-designated hyperacute stroke research center. Contribute to service development initiatives to improve stroke care delivery.

Supervision and Mentorship:Receive supervision and mentoring similar to stroke SpRs with NTNs. Mentor junior doctors and medical students within the stroke service.

University College London Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (UCLH) is one of the most complex NHS trusts in the UK, serving a large and diverse population. We provide academically led acute and specialist services, to people from the local area, from throughout the United Kingdom and overseas. Our vision is to deliver top-quality patient care, excellent education, and world-class research.

We provide first-class acute and specialist services across eight sites:o University College Hospital (incorporating the Elizabeth Garrett Anderson Wing)o National Hospital for Neurology and Neurosurgeryo Royal National ENT and Eastman Dental Hospitalso University College Hospital Grafton Way Buildingo Royal London Hospital for Integrated Medicineo University College Hospital Macmillan Cancer Centreo The Hospital for Tropical Diseaseso University College Hospital at Westmoreland Street

We are dedicated to the diagnosis and treatment of many complex illnesses. UCLH specialises in women's health and the treatment of cancer, infection, neurological, gastrointestinal and oral disease. It has world class support services including critical care, imaging, nuclear medicine and pathology.

We are committed to sustainability and have pledged to become a carbon net zero health service, embedding sustainable practice throughout UCLH. We have set an ambitious target of net zero for our direct emissions by 2031 and indirect emissions by 2040.

title: Maternity Locum (Salaried GP) 6 months from December 2026
descriptionHtml:

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
We're looking for a friendly, enthusiastic GP to join our welcoming team at Newport Surgery. Serving around 10,000 patients in a semi-rural community, we pride ourselves on delivering high-quality, compassionate care while maintaining the personal touch that general practice is all about.

As part of our supportive clinical team, you'll work alongside two GP Partners, five Salaried GPs, an ACP, Practice Nurses and a wide range of PCN-funded ARRS colleagues. We are a high-achieving QOF practice with a strong reputation for teamwork, continuity of care and excellent patient service.

    • Newport Surgery is a high-performing, patient-focused GP practice serving approximately 10,000 patients within a predominantly semi-rural community. employer: University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust
title: Locum Burns Consultant
descriptionHtml:
Applications are invited for the post of Locum Consultant Plastic Surgeon with a Special interest in Burns, at the University Hospital Birmingham NHS Trust.

The post holder will work as one of a team of Consultant Burns and Plastic Surgeons, covering the Regional Burns Service in the Midlands. The adult burns centre is based at Queen Elizabeth Hospital, University Hospital Birmingham NHS Trust. Paediatric burns management takes place at the Birmingham Children's Hospital. In addition, the post holder will have the opportunity to do an additional plastic surgery subspecialities depending on experience and interests. The postholder will become an integral part of the Burns MDT Team . They will join a well-established and active team of burn surgeons who work across both hospital sites to provide care in both the Paediatric and Adult Burn Centres in Birmingham, as part of the Midlands Burn Operational Delivery Network.

The Job Plan will comprise of 10 programmed activities, including burns on-call across the QE hospital and Birmingham Children's Hospital. The job plan will be subject to the needs of the service and experience of the successful candidate. The final time table will be constructed following discussion with the successful candidate and will result in an agreed job plan. The job plan will be mainly in burns, but there will some opportunities to take part in general plastic surgery.

The appointee will participate in the 1:7 burns on call rota covering the adult burns centre at Queen Elizabeth Hospital and the paediatric burns centre at Birmingham Children Hospital Birmingham Children's Hospital. Also, the appointee will be part of burns MDT at both QEHB and BCH.

The successful applicant will be expected to contribute to departmental teaching and support residents with projects leading to publications and presentations. The involvement in continuing medical education is an integral part of the advertised post and as such, the successful candidate will be expected to support recruitment to clinical trials and practice evidence-based medicine. The appointee will be expected to participate in all aspects of clinical governance as developed by the Trust to monitor, maintain and develop the quality and effectiveness of care.

University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust strives to have an inclusive culture where everyone feels like they belong, can thrive, knows that they add value and feels valued. We do this by developing compassionate and culturally competent leaders, being values driven in all that we do and by creating a welcoming and inclusive workplace that thrives on the diversity of our people. As such we want to attract and recruit talented individuals from all backgrounds, and for each of you to feel supported for the diversity you bring, to achieve your full potential. For those staff with a disability, including physical disability, long term health condition, mental health or neurodiverse condition, this also means being committed to making reasonable adjustments needed for you to carry out your role.

title: Consultant in Paediatric Anaesthesia
descriptionHtml:
Royal Manchester Children's Hospital (RMCH) is the largest tertiary Paediatric Hospital in the UK. The successful candidate would be joining a department of 47 Consultant Paediatric Anaesthetists delivering sessions across RMCH, MREH, Christie Hospital, Trafford Hospital and Wythenshawe hospital.

The department provides anaesthesia for a wide range of paediatric surgical specialities including neurosurgery, complex airway, hyperinsulinism, palatofacial surgery, burn injury, paediatric urology including bladder exstrophy, renal transplant surgery, and neonatal surgery.

The post attracts 10 PAs . The job plan may include sessions at any of the hospitals mentioned above (RMCH, MREH, Christie Hospital, Trafford Hospital and Wythenshawe hospital. Weekend elective work may be required in the future.

Candidates should demonstrate proven experience in Paediatric anaesthetics.

The new consultant will provide anaesthesia for the services provided by the hospitals: Vide Infra for contractual commitment. Provision of services, including a 1 in 16 on-call rota, will be shared with other consultant anaesthetists at the Royal Manchester Children's Hospital.

The appointee will be contracted for a 10 PA job, made up of 8.5 direct clinical care PAs and 1.5 supporting PA for revalidation, appraisal, job planning, teaching, audit, CME/CPD, mandatory training, clinical governance and other administrative duties.

The job plan is flexible to meet the needs of the service. The job plan October 2026 attached is an example and the exact timings of clinical sessions to be agreed through discussion and agreement with the Clinical Director dependent on service demands.

The clinical commitment will consist of a variety of surgical specialties, and the appointee would be expected to work at RMCH and all its affiliated sites and to cover for colleagues annual, study and sick leave.

Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust (MFT) is a leading centre of clinical excellence, renowned for pioneering patient care, advanced medical research, and a collaborative multi-speciality environment. We are the largest provider of specialist services, and our Oxford Road Campus in Manchester is the largest health academic campus in Europe - a great place to progress your career.

With over 30,000 employees, a turnover exceeding £3 billion, and 10 hospital and community services, join our team to help us deliver outstanding healthcare to our diverse communities.We offer an engaging and supportive environment, with access to state-of-the-art facilities and cutting-edge technology. Research and Innovation are at the heart of our work, offering opportunities to lead research that shapes the future of medicine, working alongside experts, advancing clinical practice, and improving patient outcomes.

At MFT, we foster a culture where every colleague is valued and empowered to thrive. Your expertise is recognised, your ambitions are supported, and your impact is felt at every level. Whether you want to develop your clinical skills, pursue research interests, or seek leadership opportunities, MFT provides the ideal environment to achieve your medical or professional aspirations.If you are dedicated to driving clinical innovation and delivering compassionate patient care, join us to shape tomorrow's healthcare; where clinical excellence, innovation, and your career will thrive.

title: Consultant in Geriatrics (Acute and Community)
descriptionHtml:
The Trust is looking to recruit a Consultant in Geriatric Medicine, based at both the Queen Elizabeth Hospital (QEH) in Woolwich and in the Greenwich Community Frailty team based at Memorial Hospital, Shooters Hill, Woolwich. The postholder will join a team of 10 consultants in QEH and be part of the community frailty team delivered by Oxleas Foundation Trust.

The post has been created to develop and consolidate new ways of working, enabling flow from acute settings to community teams. This is an opportunity for a Consultant Geriatrician to develop a broad range of experience, working across both the acute Frailty service delivered by Lewisham and Greenwich Trust and the community frailty service which is currently expanding to form part of the four integrated neighbourhood teams in Greenwich.

The post is full time (10 PAs) and based at Queen Elizabeth Hospital, Woolwich and Memorial Hospital, Shooters Hill.

A formal job plan will be agreed between the post holder and their Clinical or Divisional Director for Lewisham and Greenwich Trust and the Clinical Director or Service Director of Oxleas NHS Foundation Trust within three months of their commencement date. The role is equally split between the two Trusts.

To support the development on-going development of a comprehensive geriatric medicine service and development of Frailty within the Greenwich integrated neighbourhood teams

Support and develop the interface frailty services for ED and relevant clinical areas

Develop the Geriatrician role within the four integrated neighbourhood teams in Greenwich, specifically supporting the MDT needs of the moderately and severely frail population.

Support, lead and develop integrated care working with ICB's and community partners

Be an advocate for the care of older people within the organization.

Lead, support and mentor junior medical staff within the department and ensure training requirements are met.

Undertake work within a relevant area of interest

Our people are our greatest asset. When we feel supported and happy at work, this positivity reaches those very people we are here for, the patients. Engaged employees perform at their best and our Equality, Diversity & Inclusion (EDI) initiatives contribute to cultivate a culture of engagement. We have four staff networks, a corporate EDI Team and a suite of programmes and events which aim to insert the 5 aspirations:

  1. Improving representation at senior levels of staff with disabilities, from black, Asian, and ethnic minorities background, identify as LGBTQ+ and women, through improved recruitment and leadership development
  2. Widening access (anchor institution) and employability
  3. Improving the experience of staff with disability
  4. Improving the EDI literacy and confidence of trust staff through training and development
  5. Making equalities mainstream

employer: Leeds and York Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
title: Trust Locum Consultant Psychiatrist - Forensic Services
descriptionHtml:
Leeds and York Forensic Services provide Low Secure Inpatient Services based at two sites within Leeds & York Partnership NHS Foundation Trust (Clifton House, York and Newsam Centre, Leeds). The Forensic Service provides a high quality assessment, treatment and recovery service for people who represent a risk to others due to their mental disorder and are in need of either inpatient management, or support from a specialized community team. There are male acute and rehabilitation wards on each site and each site has a female ward. Each service focuses on patients who suffer with primary diagnosis of mental illness. Many have comorbid substance misuse and some may have comorbid personality disorder, autism spectrum disorder, or mild learning difficulties.

The postholder will provide medical RC responsibility for ward 2 which is an 11 bedded female ward. All patients are detained under the MHA. There is a community case load of about 15 female patients who are care coordinated by the forensic outreach team. Access assessments to the inpatient service and risk advice and management reports are conducted on behalf of the secure provider collaborative on an approximately 1-2 times per monthly basis. Referrals are received from medium security, prisons and acute mental health services within the West Yorkshire Secure Provider Collaborative footprint. Therefore the post holder will be required to travel to other hospitals and prisons.

Leeds Partnerships NHS Foundation Trust is seeking to appoint an 8 PA Consultant Psychiatristin the Leeds Low Secure Female Service based at the Newsam Centre.

Duties will be in line with those of an Approved / Responsible Clinician for low secure patients with complex needs. There will be a requirement for significant liaison with other services and agencies including MAPPA, police, courts, probation etc and support with advice and opinion to general adult colleagues who may seek consultation for patients presenting with particular risks in acute services.

The post holder, supported by the MDT, will provide:

  • Regular routine clinical reviews
  • Flexibility to accommodate urgent clinical reviews
  • Clinical input within the CPA framework
  • To hold Approved Clinician status as defined within the Mental Health Act (1983) and undertake the duties of Responsible Clinician for those subject to the MHA 1983 under their care
  • Complex prescribing and review
  • Effective liaison and collaboration with mental health providers within the trust and the West Yorkshire secure provider collaborative, and with statutory organisations in the effective delivery of safe and effective care and risk management
  • An expectation to work intensively and assertively with the client group
  • To provide professional leadership

The Leeds and York Partnership NHS Foundation Trust (LYPFT) is the main provider of Mental Health and Learning Disability services in Leeds. We also provide specialist inpatient services in York and some highly specialised services across the country. As a teaching trust with strong links to local universities, we are a centre of excellence for teaching, research and development.

There are many benefits of working for LYPFT including fantastic employee wellbeing support, 27 - 33 days annual leave, flexible working and remote working arrangements, the NHS Pension Scheme, coaching, support and opportunities for career development and training and education support alongside a range of exclusive discounts and payment schemes including for cars, extra leave days and more NHS Discount Offers.

We also have a bank department, offering variety of roles in nursing, allied health professions, healthcare support worker and administration clerical. Permanent employees are automatically added to bank.

Applicants should be aware that individuals requiring a visa to work in the UK, the Trust only provides sponsorship for registered healthcare practitioner roles(this does not include Healthcare Support Workers). This is an essential requirement, and the Trust is unable to offer you a role if you do not meet Trust requirements for sponsorship and Home Office requirements for a visa.

employer: University Hospitals Sussex NHS Foundation Trust (279)
title: Consultant in Integrated Sexual Health & HIV Medicine
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for an enthusiastic and committed Consultant to join the HIV/Sexual Health & Contraception team in Brighton - the first UK Fast Track City.

This is a substantive post, 7 sessions negotiable, joining the team of consultants providing integrated Sexual Health, Contraception and HIV services within the Brighton arm of University Hospitals Sussex NHS trust.

The post will be a key member of the team delivering a high quality fully integrated Sexual Health, Contraception & HIV service in Brighton & Hove and will encompass the full spectrum of specialist clinical work, supervision and training of nursing, junior medical staff and medical students and participation in research and service improvement.

The post holder will be part of the senior management team and will be expected to contribute to the administration and leadership of the department and participate in clinical governance and quality improvement as well as CME.

The post holder will be part of the non resident on-call rota (1:11) which includes staffing a Saturday sexual Health clinic (10.00-14.00) and covering HIV inpatients in the RSCH and providing telephone advice across the Sussex HIV network.

Clinical Duties

The post holder will be expected to:

Provide a regular HIV clinic (alternate weeks), including the supporting activities such as viral load and team meetings.

Provide complex case management in the Horizon (complex GU) clinic.

Provide medical leadership to Clinic T, a monthly clinic offering SH care to trans, non-binary or gender questioning people

To provide occasional cover in Clinic M (GBMSM clinic) < 6/annum

Take part and lead routine sexual health and contraception clinics

Take part in a Saturday sexual health clinic 1:11 when on call

Work closely / liaise with colleagues / external agencies

Support junior colleagues in clinics to provide excellent care for patients

To ensure there is appropriate specialist service provision during the working week across all clinical sites, with expert advice available for other service providers

On Call Commitment: non-resident HIV on call 1:11 covering HIV inpatients and potentially patients in the Sussex Beacon (reopening April 2027), including referrals for HIV advice from the Sussex Network and any urgent SHAC issues (e.g. post exposure prophylaxis).

Please see Job description for further details

At UHSussex, diversity is our strength, and we want you to feel included to help us always deliver Excellent Care Everywhere, as shown in our Outstanding for Caring CQC rating. Your uniqueness and experiences will be part of our creative and innovative community where everyone is encouraged to succeed. We have a range of staff networks to help break down barriers, and can offer a buddy to help new members settle in. We're proud to be a Disability Confident Employer (Level 3) and a Veteran Aware Trust.

employer: East and North Hertfordshire Teaching NHS Trust
title: Locum Consultant in Emergency Medicine
descriptionHtml:
This is an excellent opportunity to join the Emergency Medicine department at East and North Hertfordshire NHS Trust, we are looking to recruit to a 12-month fixed-term post to cover a career break. The successful candidate will join a service that prides itself in effective leadership, innovative thinking, and excellent teamwork. We strive to challenge our existing working practices and to constantly improve our service to deliver best practice guidance and to ensure that our patient outcomes are successful, and they feel valued during their visits to the Trust.

The successful applicant will join our Emergency Department as a Locum Consultant. Based at Lister Hospital in Stevenage the post comprises of 10 programmed activities (PAs) plus 1.5 indicative additional programmed activities (APAs) including on-call commitment, which could be modified for a candidate preferring to work 10 PAs or less than full time.

The main duties of the role are to provide a high-quality service to patients referred for treatment and care, liaising as necessary with clinical and associated colleagues in other specialties and disciplines.

  • Maintenance of high-quality patient centered care
  • Shared responsibility for the day-to-day management of the service and participation in strategic planning
  • Teaching and training within the multidisciplinary service
  • Active involvement in multidisciplinary team meetings and directorate clinical governance activity
  • Active participation in continuing medical education

At East and North Hertfordshire Teaching NHS Trust, we are proud of the range of general and specialist services we provide and our 6,000 or so dedicated staff ensure our patients get the best care. Our ability to be flexible and innovative in the way in which we work and deliver our services to our catchment has never been more important than it is now.

We run the following hospitals:

  • The Lister Hospital, Stevenage
  • New Queen Elizabeth II (New QEII), Welwyn Garden City
  • Hertford County, Hertford
  • Mount Vernon Cancer Centre (MVCC), Northwood

We have ambitious plans to become an outstanding, patient-led Trust where dedicated staff provide high-quality, compassionate care to our patients. We continue to undergo significant transformation and our staff and patients are at the heart of delivering this ambitious agenda.

We are committed to a positive work life balance for our employees. This means that any employee is entitled to seek to work flexible working patterns and we are committed to listen and consider all requests. Such requests, of course, have to be made and considered formally, and will need to be balanced against service needs, but our starting point will always be to find ways to support making them happen.

title: Consultant Gynaecological Oncology Surgeon
descriptionHtml:
The successful candidate will join the existing Gynaecological Oncology surgical team and will have an important role in the continued development and leadership of the service.

The post is particularly suited to an enthusiastic and ambitious clinician who wishes to develop their clinical, leadership, educational or service-development interests within a supportive specialist environment.

The job plan will be predominantly dedicated to the care of patients with gynaecological cancer and will be designed with a degree of flexibility to accommodate the successful candidate's individual career aspirations and areas of interest.

The job plan will be predominantly dedicated to the care of patients with gynaecological cancer and will be designed with a degree of flexibility to accommodate the successful candidate's individual career aspirations and areas of interest.

The anticipated job plan will include:

  • A minimum of two dedicated theatre sessions per week
  • One specialist Gynaecological Oncology clinic
  • One MDT session
  • Colposcopy activity
  • Participation in the general gynaecology on-call rota
  • Opportunities to contribute to service development, leadership, education and quality improvement

The successful candidate will be expected to take an active and visible leadership role within the Gynaecological Oncology service and MDT. Previous experience in service leadership or MDT organisation would be advantageous, although applications from candidates with the appropriate skills, enthusiasm and leadership potential are encouraged.

Please submit your application as soon as possible, as we reserve the right to close adverts once sufficient applications have been received.

We recognise that AI tools can support application writing; however, candidates are asked to keep their use to a minimum. Responses should reflect your own experience, skills and knowledge, as over-reliance on AI-generated content may result in generic answers that do not accurately represent your abilities.

University Hospitals of Northamptonshire (UHN) brings together Kettering General Hospital NHS Foundation Trust and Northampton General Hospital NHS Trust. As a group, we are committed to improving services for our communities through collaboration, modernising care delivery and striving for excellence. Working together enables us to share expertise, strengthen services and create greater opportunities, and there may be a requirement to work across sites depending on service needs.

Candidates who identify as members of the Armed Forces community and meet the essential criteria will be guaranteed an interview.

employer: Doncaster & Bassetlaw Teaching Hospitals NHS FT
title: Locally Employed Doctor in Emergency Medicine (ST3-5 Level)
descriptionHtml:
**Please note we have specified valid ALS, ATLS and EPALS (or equivalent) certifications as Essential Criteria in the Person Specification for this position. If you do not confirm you hold all three life support courses on your application, it will unfortunately be rejected**

The successful candidate will contribute to emergency care across the Emergency Care Group and will work as a part of the Emergency Department team with a full shift rota.

Post holder to be able to lead the team overnight so requires strong experience in a busy ED and leadership skills. Managing a whole spectrum of emergency patients

Assistance and supervision of the F1, F2 and GP VTS doctors with the management of patients.

Strengthening the delivery of a, high quality, General and Emergency Medicine service across the hospital and community.

Quality assurance of the service and individual practice

title: Clinical SIM Fellow in Undergraduate Medical Education
descriptionHtml:
This is an exciting opportunity for a motivated doctor to develop skills in medical education. The Clinical SIM Fellow will play a key role in delivering and developing SIMS and teaching for postgraduate-entry medical students undertaking a PBL-based curriculum.

This 9 month post offers 100% of time dedicated to education. The successful candidate will be responsible for developing and delivery clinical SIM sessions, as well as bedside teaching and contribute to curriculum development, supporting student assessment and pastoral care. Please note that this post is required to commence as soon as possible and is expected to run until August 2027.

1. Key Responsibilities

To deliver high quality teaching to TCMS postgraduate-entry medical students in line with the TCMS curriculum requirements

Maintain up-to-date clinical knowledge and skills

Contribute to patient care in line with Trust policies and GMC standards

Participate in clinical governance and audit activities where appropriate

We take pride in placing people at the centre of everything we do, working together as a united team. Driven by a shared ambition to continually grow, develop, and learn, we recognise and value every contribution. By combining our experience and skills, we not only support our vibrant, diverse communities, but also support one another.

With a team of over 9,000 employees, we are proud to be the largest employer in Gloucestershire and rank among the top 10 largest Trusts in the South West region.By joining our Trust, you will benefit from an excellent package that includes exclusive benefits, flexible working opportunities and the chance to gain valuable experience in one or both of our innovative hospitals.

As well as generous annual leave allowance, you will have access to the excellent NHS pension scheme, competitive bank rates, discounts at local shops and restaurants, access to two on-site nurseries, discounted public transport, reward and recognition and a range of health and wellbeing initiatives to support you.

title: Healthcare Assistant
descriptionHtml:
The Healthcare Assistant supports the GPs and practice nurse by carrying out routine clinical tasks and keeping the clinical areas running safely.

Why join us: Chineham Medical Practice offers a friendly, supportive team, training and development, and the chance to make a real difference to our patients every day.

Clinical: Health checks, blood pressure monitoring, urinalysis, blood tests, ECGs, glucose checks, weight and patient measurements, simple wound care and stitch removal, lifestyle advice and chaperoning. After training, they also do contraceptive pill and blood pressure checks, smoking cessation and measuring for support stockings. They also process laboratory samples.

Administration and practice duties: They keep accurate patient records and documentation, follow infection control guidelines, and prepare rooms and equipment, including for implanons and minor surgery. They restock and tidy clinical areas, check expiry dates, manage sharps and clinical waste, and order health promotion materials. They also help with campaigns such as flu, attend practice meetings, and contribute to practice policy and strategy.

About our team

Chineham Medical Practice is an NHS GP surgery with a friendly, close-knit team of GP Partners, salaried doctors, nurses, healthcare assistants, reception and administrative staff. We work closely together and look out for one another, and every member of the team, clinical or non-clinical, is valued for the part they play in caring for our patients.

Our atmosphere

We are a welcoming and supportive practice where people feel able to ask questions, share ideas and ask for help. Our management team is approachable, and we value open communication and respect for one another.

Our work ethic

We take pride in providing safe, compassionate and professional care. We are reliable, we work well as a team, and we are committed to doing the job properly. We encourage everyone to learn and develop, and we welcome new ideas on how we can improve the service we provide.

Benefits of working with us

  • A friendly, supportive team
  • Full induction, training and ongoing development
  • NHS pension scheme
  • Annual leave entitlement
  • The satisfaction of making a real difference to patients in our local community

employer: London North West University Healthcare NHS Trust
title: H&N Locum Clinical Fellow
descriptionHtml:
H&N Locum Clinical Fellow

Locum Clinical Fellow required for 30 hours per week from October 2026 to 31 March 2027. The post will provide dedicated clinical capacity within the Head & Neck service to support elective recovery, reduce long waits, improve access to first appointments and strengthen winter resilience. The post holder will be required to run 8 2ww H&N clinics per week, working closely with clinical, clinical fellows, nursing and CNS teams.

  • Providing high-quality care to head & neck cancer patients.
  • Participating in the 2-week wait cancer pathway, running a dedicated parallel clinics with a consultant.
  • Ensuring patients are appropriately staged and listed for MDT discussion within required timeframes where appropriate.
  • Undertaking middle-grade duties on the rota.
  • Maintaining good communication with patients to support shared decision making

London North West University Healthcare NHS Trust (LNWH) cares for the people of Brent, Ealing, Harrow and beyond.

Our team of more than 8,200 clinical and support staff serve a diverse population of almost one million people.

We run major acute services at:

  • Northwick Park Hospital: home to one of the busiest emergency departments (A&E) in the country. The hospital provides a full range of services including the country's top-rated hyper-acute stroke unit and one of only three hyper-acute rehabilitation units in the UK
  • St Mark's Hospital: an internationally renowned specialist centre for bowel disease

We are a university teaching NHS trust, in recognition of the important role we play in training clinicians of the future and bringing the benefits of research to the public.

Most importantly, we have a strong and supportive team culture. We are committed to investing in staff development and creating a positive working environment where individuals can thrive.

employer: Hull University Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust
title: Locum Consultant Cardiologist - Cardiac Imaging
descriptionHtml:
Hull University Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust is one of the largest acute trusts in the North of England with two hospitals serving a local population of 600,000, increasing to 1.2 million for tertiary services. The services provided by the Trust are split across Hull Royal Infirmary, situated close to Hull city centre, and Castle Hill Hospital, in Cottingham on the outskirts of the city. The Trust has an annual budget of £500m, employing over 10,000 staff who provide a wide range of emergency, inpatient and outpatient services

The cardiology department is staffed with energetic, forward-looking cardiologists, and we're looking for someone similar to join our team. In HUTH, we have the purpose-built £28 million John Cleland Heart Centre which includes 4 cardiac catheter labs equipped with GE Inova 2100 imaging systems, dedicated short stay and inpatient wards. The centre includes the cardiology outpatient and diagnostic departments, 3 cardiothoracic operating theatres and intensive care, high observation and cardiothoracic surgery beds.

We receive invaluable support from our highly experienced cardiac physiologists, radiographers, radiology colleagues, nuclear medicine colleagues and wider multidisciplinary team.

The Humber Health Partnership is one of the largest acute and community Partnership arrangements in the NHS, seeing well over one million patients every year and managing a budget of over £1.3 billion.

Made up of two Trusts - Northern Lincolnshire and Goole NHS Foundation Trust (NLAG) and Hull University Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust (HUTH) - our Partnership has significant ambitions and is committed to delivering world-class hospital and community services for the 1.65 million people we serve.

Together we employ nearly 20,000 staff. Our five main hospital sites are Diana, Princess of Wales Hospital, Scunthorpe General Hospital and Goole and District Hospital, for NLAG and Hull Royal Infirmary and Castle Hill Hospital for HUTH.

As Teaching Hospitals working with the Hull York Medical School, we both lead and contribute to research in many areas - biomedical research, primary care, palliative medicine, cardiovascular and respiratory medicine, vascular surgery, cancer surgery and oncology.

We believe that by developing a diverse, inclusive, innovative, skilled and caring workforce, we can deliver excellent care to our patients and a great future for our employees, our Partnership and our community.

title: Specialist in Gastroenterology
descriptionHtml:
Join our Gastroenterology team

The Isle of Wight NHS Trust is seeking an enthusiastic and forward-thinking Specialist in Gastroenterology to join our ambitious and compassionate team at St Mary's Hospital.

This post offers the opportunity to make a meaningful contribution to gastroenterology services for a defined Island population, working as part of a supportive multidisciplinary team at St Mary's Hospital. You will be comfortable working with appropriate professional autonomy while recognising the importance of multidisciplinary working and strong clinical leadership. You will contribute positively to the development of the service, support junior colleagues and play an active role in maintaining high standards of clinical governance, education and patient care.

It is an opportunity not only to deliver excellent clinical care but also to help shape and develop the future of gastroenterology services on the Isle of Wight.

If you are an enthusiastic and forward-thinking clinician looking for your next opportunity in Gastroenterology, we would be delighted to hear from you.

As a Specialist in Gastroenterology, you will provide a comprehensive inpatient and outpatient gastroenterology service alongside general medical responsibilities.

Working within the agreed job plan, you will take responsibility, with appropriate professional autonomy, for the diagnosis, treatment and ongoing management of general medical and gastroenterology patients.

Your duties will include:

  • Inpatient gastroenterology care
  • Outpatient gastroenterology clinics
  • Endoscopy
  • General medical duties
  • Participation in the general medical emergency on-call rota
  • Clinical administration
  • Multidisciplinary team meetings
  • Supervision and management of junior medical staff
  • Teaching and supporting the development of colleagues
  • Clinical audit and governance
  • Continuing professional development
  • Working collaboratively with clinical and operational colleagues to support safe, effective and efficient services

We are looking for a motivated, enthusiastic and committed doctor who will work collaboratively with colleagues across the service, combining professional autonomy with a strong commitment to safe, effective and patient-centred care and who is passionate about delivering high-quality gastroenterology and general medical care.

Working for our Trust brings a variety of benefits, including an onsite day nursery, cycle-to-work scheme, discounts at local businesses and gyms, and the opportunity to hire Trust's beach hut in Ryde. We offer many flexible working opportunities, speak to us about how we might be able to accommodate a flexible working arrangement for you and if it works for the service, we will do our best to make it work for you.

The Isle of Wight is a unique and stunning gem located off the South Coast of England, a short ferry journey from Portsmouth and Southampton, with journey times taking from as little as 10 minutes. London can be reached in 90 minutes by rail from Southampton or Portsmouth. The island offers an amazing coastline with beautiful countryside, year-round events, festivals and award-winning attractions.

title: Community Dermatology GPwER
descriptionHtml:
The GP with Extended Role (GPwER) in Community Dermatology will deliver high-quality, specialist dermatology care within an NHS England community-based service. The role supports the delivery of care closer to home, reducing unnecessary secondary care referrals and improving patient access in line with NHS Long Term Plan priorities. The post holder will work within agreed clinical pathways, national guidance, and local ICB commissioning arrangements.

We are seeking experienced and committed GPwER Dermatologists to participate in our community service. Undertaking sessional work you will manage your own caseload, as well as autonomous prescribing for patients in our BMJ Award 2021 shortlisted community service.

The role is contract based with a session lasting 3 hours. The number of sessions per week can vary based on clinician availability.

Pay is based on clinical activity.

Clinical Responsibilities

Provide specialist dermatology assessment, diagnosis, and management for patients referred from primary care under locally agreed referral criteria.

Manage a broad range of dermatological conditions, including inflammatory skin disease, benign and suspicious skin lesions, and chronic skin conditions.

Undertake dermatological procedures in line with competencies and service accreditation, which may include cryotherapy, curettage and cautery, punch and shave biopsies, and excision of low-risk skin lesions where approved.

Recognise and appropriately escalate or refer patients requiring secondary or tertiary dermatology services, including suspected skin cancers, in accordance with NHS England cancer pathways and local ICB policies.

Prescribe and monitor dermatological treatments safely and effectively in line with NICE guidance, local formularies, and shared care agreements.

Checking investigation results (commenting and filing)

Documentation & Governance: Maintain accurate and timely clinical records and adhere to governance, safety, and quality standards.

Conduct clinical practice in accordance with contractual requirements and within the parameters of Patient Firsts services plans

Work in face-to-face and telephone clinics as required

Work within changing service requirements as directed by PFSE management/service contract/ specification

Patient FirstSocial Enterprise (PFSE) is a, not for profit, community provider that operates, under NHS ICB contract, across northeast London. Since 2009Patient Firsthas provided a growing number of community services; currently our portfolio consists of: Dermatology, Minor Surgery, Cardiology, MSK and Physiotherapy and Gynaecology. We are a highly reputed service operating for the last 15 years.

The Dermatology service was shortlisted for the prestigious BMJ Dermatology Team of the Year in 2021. Our growing, consultant led, dermatology team consists of experienced GPwERs and specialist nurse prescribers. Operating at locations throughout northeast London (Newham, Tower Hamlets and Waltham Forest) on weekdays, evenings and Saturday mornings.

We are seeking experienced and committed GPwER Dermatologists to participate in our community service. Undertaking sessional work you will manage your own caseload.

descriptionHtml:
Coventry and Warwickshire Pathology Services (CWPS) invites applications for two replacement consultant cellular pathologists to join our forward-thinking and friendly team based at University Hospitals Coventry and Warwickshire NHS Trust (UHCW).

CWPS are a large pathology network in the Midlands, providing pathology services for UHCW, George Eliot Hospital NHS Trust and South Warwickshire University NHS Foundation Trust.We are seeking pathologists with sub-specialist interests in breast and gynaecological pathology, but would also consider dermatopathology, urology, haematolymphoid, thoracic, gastrointestinal and molecular pathology.

University of Warwick's Clinical Sciences Research Institute located on the UHCW site provides additional laboratory research facilities.

Informal enquiries should be addressed to Dr Sarah Read-Jones, Clinical Lead for Cellular Pathology: 02476 968320 sarah.read-jones@uhcw.nhs.uk

The appointee will provide a diagnostic consultation and advisory service to clinical colleagues in the Network and primary care. University Hospitals Coventry and Warwickshire (UHCW) NHS Trust, rated as good by the Care Quality Commission, is one of the largest teaching Trusts in the UK.

There has never been a better time to join our team.

title: Consultant in Emergency Medicine
descriptionHtml:
The Emergency Department (ED) was purpose built in 2014 and offers state of-the-art facilities. title: General Practitioner

title: Locum Consultant in Medical Oncology
descriptionHtml:
This Locum Medical Oncologist role sits within a cohesive and supportive multidisciplinary cancer service in Hywel Dda University Health Board, where consultant input is highly valued and integral to service delivery. You will undertake a varied and clinically engaging workload across systemic anti-cancer therapies and outpatient care, supported by an experienced and approachable team of consultants, specialist nurses, and allied health professionals.

Working in Hywel Dda offers a distinctive way of practising medicine. The combination of smaller, well-connected clinical teams and a close-knit population allows for continuity of care, meaningful patient relationships, and visible impact across the patient pathway. Clinicians here often value the ability to focus on quality of care without the pressures typically associated with larger urban centres.The area itself provides a high standard of living, with easy access to coastline, countryside, and outdoor activities, alongside significantly reduced commute times and a more manageable pace of life. This supports a sustainable balance between clinical responsibilities and personal wellbeing--something increasingly important for consultants at all stages of their careers.

You will deliver Consultant-led outpatient clinics, providing assessment, treatment planning, and ongoing care for patients receiving systemic anti-cancer therapies. This includes developing individualised treatment strategies aligned with national guidance and MDT recommendations, while taking into account patient preference and overall clinical context.

You will play a central role in multidisciplinary team meetings, contributing specialist expertise to guide diagnosis, staging, and treatment decisions. The service benefits from strong collaborative working across oncology, palliative care, radiology, pathology, and surgical teams, enabling well-rounded and timely clinical decision-making.

The role includes responsibility for prescribing and overseeing systemic treatments, managing toxicities, and supporting patients through complex treatment pathways. You willalso contribute to the management of acute oncology presentations, ensuring safe and responsive care when patients become unwell.

Working across inpatient and outpatient settings, you will support continuity and consistency of care. There is close day-to-day collaboration with oncology nursing teams, pharmacists, and wider professionals, allowing for a coordinated and patient-centred approach.

Hywel Dda University Health Board plans and provides NHS healthcare services for people living in Carmarthenshire, Ceredigion, Pembrokeshire, and bordering counties.

We have over 13,000 staff and together we provide primary, community, in-hospital, mental health and learning disabilities services.

We work in partnership with the three local authorities, as well as public, private and third sector colleagues, including our valued team of volunteers.

Our services are provided in:

  • Four main hospitals: Bronglais Hospital in Aberystwyth; Glangwili Hospital in Carmarthen; Prince Philip Hospital in Llanelli; and Withybush Hospital in Haverfordwest
  • Five community hospitals: Amman Valley and Llandovery hospitals in Carmarthenshire; Tregaron Hospital in Ceredigion; and Tenby and South Pembrokeshire hospitals in Pembrokeshire
  • Two integrated care centres: Aberaeron and Cardigan in Ceredigion, and several other community settings
  • 47 general practices (six of which are health board managed practices); dental practices (including four orthodontic); 97 community pharmacies; 43 general ophthalmic practices; and 8 ophthalmic domiciliary providers
  • Numerous mental health and learning disabilities services

employer: Cwm Taf Morgannwg University Health Board
title: Specialist Grade Doctor in Ophthalmology
descriptionHtml:
These are newly created Specialist Doctor posts developed as part of the Medical Workforce productivity programme.

Specialist doctors are senior and experienced clinicians who will work autonomously to a level of defined competencies, as agreed within local clinical governance frameworks. Specialists will be responsible for patients in their areas of practice as an 'expert decision maker'.

Specialist doctors provide expertise in a specialised area, whether delivering care in a specific specialty or in a generalist service and will manage the full range of presentations in their area of practice. The role will primarily focus on providing direct clinical care, meeting service delivery and improvement requirements. However, the role will be supported by suitable development opportunities including management roles and leadership responsibilities in, teaching, academia research and service development. The details of the balance between clinical care and other elements of the role would be dis- cussed during the job planning process.

Specialist doctors are also expected to be involved in deliver teaching and training of others. They will be able to work as a member of a multi-disciplinary team, leading MDTs where appropriate.

Fixed term for up to 12 months to cover a Secondment

Provide clinical expertise and leadership to a defined outpatient and inpatient teams where appropriate

Provide specialist assessment and clinical management of patients with Ophthalmology problems

Provide medical liaison and advice regarding patients to local Specialist Doctors and GPs as necessary.

Provide supervision for the speciality doctor and core trainee, and to a Specialty Training Registrar if the post holder is approved as an Educational Super- visor and if an ST is allocated to the team.

Liaise effectively with members of the team, other services within the Health Board, general practitioners and other agencies.

This post is advertised as Welsh Desirable. Whilst the candidate doesn't need to have skills in Welsh, we'll consider it an advantage when short-listing and selecting candidates. This isn't 'fluency', just Speaking & Listening skills at Level 3 (equivalent to CEFR B2) or above. Level 3 means being able to communicate in Welsh during routine clinical situations, such as welcoming patients, discussing straightforward aspects of their care and answering routine questions. If you're comfortable holding everyday conversations in Welsh, we encourage you to apply. Your Welsh language skills will help us provide person-centred care and enable patients to receive services in their language of choice. Have a look at our 'Croeso Candidate' booklet below for more information.

Cwm Taf Morgannwg (CTM) University Health Board, part of NHS Wales, serves a large population across a diverse and beautiful region, steeped in history and heritage. With nearly 13,500 staff, our health board is one of Wales's largest employers.

Together, we are Team CTM; a workforce dedicated to offering excellent patient care and support to the 450,000 people across our three regions, Bridgend, Merthyr Tydfil, and Rhondda Cynon Taf. We operate three District General hospitals, several community hospitals, primary and community care facilities.

CTM's location offers the best of South Wales, just 20 minutes from Cardiff's vibrant city life, the natural beauty of the Brecon Beacons, and the serene coastline at Ogmore. Whether you enjoy lively urban amenities, peaceful countryside, or seaside escapes, our location makes an ideal setting for both work and personal life.

Our CTM 2030 Strategy--Our Health, Our Future--focuses on uniting our region around shared health and wellbeing goals. Our values guide us daily:

o We treat everyone with respect

o We work together as one team

CTM employees enjoy benefits including; a leading pension, generous leave, flexible work, career growth, and access to ongoing learning and development.

At CTM, you'll find a welcoming, team-oriented workplace that values diversity and compassion, where you can take pride in your work and the difference it makes.

employer: The Shrewsbury and Telford Hospital NHS Trust
title: Locum Consultant Ophthalmologist with an interest in Oculoplastic
descriptionHtml:
The Shrewsbury and Telford Hospital NHS Trust is looking for a locum Consultant Ophthalmologist with a sub-specialist interest in Oculoplastic, who will be predominantly based at the Royal Shrewsbury Hospital (RSH) Shrewsbury with responsibilities across both hospital sites.

Contribution to an out of hours on call rota is core to this role.

Main Clinical duties include:

  • Provide Ophthalmic services.
  • Complete clinical sessions in theatre, specialist Oculoplastic clinics, and general clinics.
  • Complete supporting professional activities.
  • Receive and coordinate referrals from urgent eye clinics, optometrist and other ophthalmic colleagues.
  • To develop enhanced clinical skills, especially in the assessment and management of acutely ill patients.
  • To have excellent team-working skills with the abilities and professional attitude to work well in a multi-professional team.
  • To deliver clinical and quality targets agreed both nationally and locally with clinical teams and commissioners.
  • To follow patients throughout their clinical pathways.

The Shrewsbury and Telford Hospital NHS Trust (SaTH) is the main provider of acute hospital services for around half a million people in Shropshire, Telford & Wrekin and mid Wales.

Our main service locations are the Princess Royal Hospital (PRH) in Telford and the Royal Shrewsbury Hospital (RSH) in Shrewsbury which are located 20 minutes' drive apart. Together they provide 99% of our activity. Both hospitals provide a wide range of acute hospital services.

Our Poppy's Promise Commitment

We believe that compassionate care sits at the heart of everything we do. Every member of our team -- clinical or non-clinical -- plays a vital role in ensuring that patients, families, and colleagues are treated with dignity, empathy, and respect at all times.

We expect all staff to demonstrate compassion not only through their words, but through their actions: by listening attentively, communicating clearly and kindly, and recognising individual needs, feelings, and circumstances of those in our care.

Effective communication is central to safe and high-quality healthcare. We value colleagues who take the time to understand others, explain information in a meaningful way, and respond to concerns with patience and understanding.

By joining our team, you are committing to uphold these values -- ensuring that every patient feels heard, respected, and valued, and that compassion is embedded in every interaction, every day.

employer: Northern Lincolnshire and Goole NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Rheumatologist
descriptionHtml:
We are based on the Diana Princess of Wales Hospital (DPOW) site. We have outpatient clinics at Diana Princess of Wales, Scunthorpe General Hospital and Goole District Hospital and run these clinics throughout the week over the 3 sites. We see a total outpatient volume of over 13,000 a year across the 3 sites. There are opportunities to further develop MSK ultrasound and connective tissue disease clinics. We work closely with a broad range of services, including General Medicine, Radiology, Orthopaedic Surgery, Paediatrics, Neurology, Academic Chest Medicine, Ophthalmology and Immunology. Regular multidisciplinary meetings facilitate collaborative working and support the delivery of high-quality, effective and safe patient care.

The Rheumatology service provides specialist care to a population of around 450,000, serving communities across North Lincolnshire, North East Lincolnshire, the East Riding of Yorkshire, and Lincolnshire.

We provide inpatient specialist rheumatology care for complex conditions and receive referrals from other specialties across the Trust. There is a weekly rheumatology MDT and we have access to monthly vasculitis MDTs at Hull. This post is designed to support the continued development and delivery of Rheumatology general and specialised services. We would be delighted to support you with any sub-specialty interests. You will have continuing responsibility for patients in your care and to support the functioning of the department. You will be a team player and provide on a reciprocal basis, emergency cover for colleagues during periods of absence. You will carry out teaching duties as required and take an active part in the Undergraduate and Postgraduate Medical Education programme. These include the teaching of junior medical staff as well as the education of nursing staff, general practitioners and other clinical staff. You will have excellent communication skills and be able to work effectively as part of a multidisciplinary team. Ours and your motivation will be to provide high quality care to achieve the best outcomes for patients with common and complex rheumatological conditions.

The Humber Health Partnership is one of the largest acute and community Partnership arrangements in the NHS, seeing well over one million patients every year and managing a budget of over £1.3 billion.

Made up of two Trusts - Northern Lincolnshire and Goole NHS Foundation Trust (NLAG) and Hull University Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust (HUTH) - our Partnership has significant ambitions and is committed to delivering world-class hospital and community services for the 1.65 million people we serve.

Together we employ nearly 20,000 staff. Our five main hospital sites are Diana, Princess of Wales Hospital, Scunthorpe General Hospital and Goole and District Hospital, for NLAG and Hull Royal Infirmary and Castle Hill Hospital for HUTH.

As Teaching Hospitals working with the Hull York Medical School, we both lead and contribute to research in many areas - biomedical research, primary care, palliative medicine, cardiovascular and respiratory medicine, vascular surgery, cancer surgery and oncology.

We believe that by developing a diverse, inclusive, innovative, skilled and caring workforce, we can deliver excellent care to our patients and a great future for our employees, our Partnership and our community.

title: GP Consultant, East Cliff Practice
descriptionHtml:
Invicta Health has a GP Consultant opportunity available at East Cliff Practice.

East Cliff Practice is based in Ramsgate with its historic harbour and attractive coastline and on the high speed rail link to London. Our neighbours are the traditional seaside towns of Broadstairs with its blue flag beaches, and Margate, home to the Turner Centre and Old Town area.

East Cliff Practice is warm and friendly with a robust multi-disciplinary team, which includes Advanced Nurse Practitioners,, Nurse Practitioners and a Clinical Pharmacy team. The multi-disciplinary team is supported by an experienced reception and administration team who handle referrals, prescriptions, reports and other general tasks.

East Cliff Practice is one of seven GP Practices that sit under Invicta Health.We are a well known community interest company, devoted to supporting and improving primary care in the Kent area.

The role involves working collaboratively with GP Consultant colleagues, the Invicta Health leadership team, and practice staff to ensure the highest possible standards of patient care.

The postholder will provide clinical oversight, leadership, and direction for the site, with a particular focus on supporting and developing the GP and Advanced Clinical Practitioner (ACP) workforce.

This role requires a visible on-site clinical leadership presence, ensuring accessibility to all staff for advice, guidance, and decision-making to support the safe and effective operation of the practice.

The postholder will also work in partnership with wider health and social care providers to deliver safe, integrated, and patient-centred services. In addition, the role includes active engagement in local and national initiatives to support the development of sustainable, high-quality healthcare provision.

Invicta Health is a non-profit company, with a passion for primary care. We have a wide range of services such as hub-based GPs services, GP surgeries, services in Urgent Care Centres and A&E, a Community Primary Care mental health service, GP staff training service and the list is growing all the time.

We are formed by a federation of General Practitioners working in Canterbury and South Kent Coast areas of East Kent. Our aim is to provide local, high quality services for local people by collaborating with other established organisations in the health and social care community.

What perks can we offer you?

  • 90% indemnity reimbursement
  • Support for fellowship opportunities
  • Learning and Development opportunities
  • Tier 2 sponsorship
  • Approved blue light card provider
  • Salary Sacrifice Schemes
  • Company Car Scheme
  • Employee Assistance Programme
