title: Consultant Radiologist with a Special Interest in Breast Radiology
descriptionHtml:
Make a real difference to breast imaging services across West Wales as a Consultant Radiologist with a specialist interest in Breast Radiology, joining a supportive and established team within Hywel Dda University Health Board.

We are seeking a Consultant Radiologist with expertise in Breast Radiology and experience in both general radiology and symptomatic breast imaging. This is an opportunity to join a team of 24 consultants and contribute to the continued development of radiology services across the Health Board.

We welcome applications from candidates interested in full-time or less than full-time working, as well as those wishing to focus exclusively on breast radiology. There is also the potential to undertake screening sessions as part of the Welsh Breast Screening Programme delivered by Breast Test Wales.

The successful candidate will be based at Bronglais General Hospital, Ceredigion, with occasional travel to Prince Philip Hospital, Llanelli and Withybush General Hospital, Pembrokeshire to support symptomatic breast clinics in line with service requirements.

Working alongside experienced radiology colleagues, you will play an important role in delivering high-quality diagnostic services and supporting the continued development of breast imaging pathways across the region.

This is a new post based at Bronglais General Hospital, Aberystwyth joining 1 Consultant Breast Radiologist, 1 Speciality Grade Doctor and 1 Consultant Radiographer providing breast radiology services to the population of Hywel Dda University Health Board. The post holder should be competent in mammography reporting, breast and axillary ultrasound, and image guided biopsy of the breast and axilla. It would also be desirable if the Radiologist has experience in additional procedures such as vacuum assisted biopsy/ excision, preoperative localisation techniques, Digital Breast Tomosynthesis (DBT) and breast MRI reporting. Experience of contrast enhanced mammography would also be desirable. The post holder will be expected to undertake symptomatic breast assessment clinics and actively participate in the breast MDT. Cross-site collaboration with respect to reporting or MDT meetings is usually done via Teleradiology and video conferencing. Office accommodation, secretarial support and full IT facilities including access to intranet and internet is provided.

Hywel Dda University Health Board plans and provides NHS healthcare services for people living in Carmarthenshire, Ceredigion, Pembrokeshire, and bordering counties.

We have over 13,000 staff and together we provide primary, community, in-hospital, mental health and learning disabilities services.

We work in partnership with the three local authorities, as well as public, private and third sector colleagues, including our valued team of volunteers.

Our services are provided in:

  • Four main hospitals: Bronglais Hospital in Aberystwyth;GlangwiliHospital in Carmarthen; Prince Philip Hospital in Llanelli; and Withybush Hospital in Haverfordwest

  • Five community hospitals: Amman Valley and Llandovery hospitals in Carmarthenshire; Tregaron Hospital in Ceredigion; and Tenby and South Pembrokeshire hospitals in Pembrokeshire

  • Two integrated care centres: Aberaeron and Cardigan in Ceredigion, and several other community settings

  • 47 general practices (six of which are health board managed practices); dental practices (including four orthodontic); 97 community pharmacies; 43 general ophthalmic practices; and 8 ophthalmic domiciliary providers

  • Numerous mental health and learning disabilities services

title: Phlebotomist
descriptionHtml:
Job description

The University Medical Group is a dynamic and high-quality practice caring for 32 000 patients. We operate over one site. We have a diverse patient population with around 9,000 student as patients.

Due to our large, registered list size we are a single practice PCN. This has enabled us to employ 3 Paramedics, 7 Pharmacists and a Physician Assistant to work as a multi-disciplinary team alongside the Doctors and Nurses .

The Nursing team consists of 3 Nurses, a Diabetes Nurse Specialist, 1 Nursing Associate and 1 Health Care Assistant. The team is supported administratively by a Care-coordinator.

Part time, Permanent. Working Monday to Friday 08:00 - 15:30 and one Saturday per month 08:00 - 12:00.

Main duties of the job

The main duties of the job are:-

  • Phlebotomy
  • BP monitoring.
  • Re-stocking of all clinical areas and maintaining stocks and keeping all areas clean.
  • To maintain and order clinical supplies.
  • Using appropriate templates in EMIS/Ardens for all procedures, training will be given in this area.
  • Any other duties that are deemed appropriate.

Being a centre of education is one of our objectives , therefore staff development is a priority to us . We also have student paramedics, PA students, Pharmacy students and two GP trainees . There is an in-house educational programme with protected time given to attend and a GP supervisor each day available for learners plus the Urgent care team consisting of a GP and paramedic for those patients who are more unwell. This enables all clinicians to be supported if they have any clinical concerns about their patients.

High quality patient care is our top priority, and we are pleased and proud to have achieved Outstanding from CQC in its last two inspections.

We are seeking an experienced, passionate, and motivated practice Phlebotomist to join our friendly nursing team who has experience in primary care.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
Cuffley and Goffs Oak Medical Practice is looking to recruit a flexible, motivated and committed GP to join our friendly practice for six sessions per week, days to be decided.

Our practice is based over two sites (one mile apart from each other) in Cuffley and Goffs Oak, Hertfordshire which has accessible transport links into London. Access to own transport essential.

The role:

  • Provide high-quality patient care
  • Conduct surgery, telephone consultations and triage appointments.
  • Conduct home visits when necessary
  • Liaise with colleagues and external providers to ensure seamless care
  • Investigate and refer patients appropriately, in line with guidance and local pathways
  • Review results and correspondence promptly
  • Provide cover for colleagues when required
  • Collect and review data for audit and QOF purposes
  • Maintain excellent communication with patients and carers
  • Attend clinical, governance, and educational meetings
  • Work collaboratively and effectively within the team
  • Manage your own workload and resources effectively
  • Attend required training events and feedback sessions
  • Report and follow up on significant incidents.

We are a large practice based over two sites (just one mile apart) which are Valley View Health Centre and Cuffley Village Surgery.

We have a happy, established team that consists of GPs, nurses, HCAs and paramedics who are all supported by an experienced and organised admin team. We are also joined regularly and supported by colleagues from our primary care network. We use Ardens templates, AccuRx, eConsults, and TPP SystmOne, and offer services including microsuction and womens health services (coil and implant clinics).

Informal enquires welcome. Please contact the practice manager by email: claire.hourihan@nhs.net

What we offer:

  • Patient list size 13,500
  • Competitive salary
  • High QOF achiever
  • Supportive and established nursing and admin teams to help reduce GP administrative burden
  • We use SystemOne as our clinical system and also utilise Accurx and Footfall to support our processes.
  • Low home visiting rate
  • Part of a pro-active PCN
  • CQC good rating
  • Supportive and friendly environment
  • Peer support
  • 30 days holiday (pro rata) + Bank Holidays (pro rata)
  • NHS pension
  • Study leave
  • Free parking

title: Salaried GP - fixed term
descriptionHtml:
Mount Farm Surgery is seeking a salaried GP to join our friendly, supportive, and well-established practice team on a 6 month fixed term contract to provide maternity cover from September 2026. We are flexible to sessions worked so please apply to discuss.

We offer a competitive salary and flexible working pattern options, paid indemnity, paid gym membership, and a supportive and pleasant working environment.

Working as part of our multidisciplinary team, you will have the opportunity to support and care for a diverse patient group. The role will include all general duties and responsibilities associated with a GP working within primary care, as well as undertaking a variety of duties, including :

  • surgery consultations
  • telephone consultations and queries
  • visiting patients at home
  • checking and signing repeat prescriptions
  • dealing with queries, paperwork, reports and correspondence in a timely fashion

Mount Farm Surgery is an innovative and professional teaching practice in Suffolk, located on the outskirts of the cathedral town of Bury St. Edmunds with close links to the A14.

Our practice team consists of 10 GPs plus a dedicated clinical team including GP trainees, ECPs, ACPs, a clinical pharmacist, nurses, and HCAs. We have a dedicated management team, plus a large team of other administrative staff.

Our membership of Bury St Edmunds PCN ensures we have an extended team which includes a paramedic home visiting service, on site clinical pharmacists, a practice based social prescriber and 2 care co-ordinators.

  • Rated Good in all areas at most recent CQC inspection
  • SystmOne clinical system
  • Electronic Prescribing System
  • Highly respected training practice
  • Regular clinical/educational meetings
  • Mentoring scheme for salaried GPs and other clinical staff
  • Non-personalised lists with equitable division of workload and capped workload for salaried GPs
  • Paper light and embracing new technology

title: Consultant Gastroenterologist
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking an enthusiastic and experienced Consultant Gastroenterologist with a specialist interest in Clinical Nutrition to establish our Nutrition Support Team (NST) within a leading tertiary cancer centre. This substantive part-time post (5 PAs) offers a unique opportunity to focus exclusively on nutrition support, with no general gastroenterology, endoscopy, or on-call commitments.Based within the Nutrition and Dietetics Department, the successful applicant will work in close partnership with the Head of Nutrition and Dietetics and the Complex Artificial Nutrition Support Dietitian to provide clinical leadership for patients with complex nutritional needs, including cancer-related intestinal failure, malnutrition, enteral feeding, and parenteral nutrition.Working within a highly skilled multidisciplinary team, you will collaborate closely with dietitians, specialist nurses, pharmacists, oncologists, palliative care teams, and surgeons to deliver high-quality, patient-centred care. This is an exciting opportunity to help shape and develop a specialist nutrition support service within a world-renowned cancer centre while contributing to education, research, service development, and quality improvement. The role offers a predictable job plan and excellent work-life balance, making it ideal for consultants seeking a specialist leadership role in clinical nutrition

The postholder will provide specialist gastroenterology expertise to the Nutrition Support Team, supporting patients with complex nutritional needs requiring parenteral nutrition, and complex enteral feeding and including those with cancer-related intestinal failure and advanced gastrointestinal complications.Working alongside the Head of Nutrition and Dietetics and the Complex Artificial Nutrition Support Dietitian, the successful candidate will lead Nutrition Support Team ward rounds, outpatient clinics, and multidisciplinary discussions, ensuring safe, effective, and evidence-based nutritional care. They will provide expert advice to clinical teams across the Trust, support decision-making regarding home parenteral nutrition, and contribute to complex discussions around artificial nutrition, including palliative and end-of-life care.The role includes developing and enhancing the Nutrition Support Service, promoting best practice in line with national guidance, leading audit and quality improvement initiatives, supporting research activity, and delivering education and training to medical, nursing, pharmacy, and dietetic colleagues.We are looking for a collaborative consultant with expertise in clinical nutrition, excellent communication skills, and a commitment to multidisciplinary working and patient-centred care

The postholder will contribute to the delivery of high-quality consultant-led care across 7 days. This includes participation in planned weekend and weekday clinical activity to support safe, timely decision-making and continuity of care for patients.

The Christie is one of Europe's leading cancer centres, treating over 60,000 patients a year. We are based in Manchester and serve a population of 3.2 million across Greater Manchester & Cheshire, but as a national specialist around 15% patients are referred to us from other parts of the country.We provide radiotherapy through one of the largest radiotherapy departments in the world; chemotherapy on site and through 14 other hospitals; highly specialist surgery for complex and rare cancer; and a wide range of support and diagnostic services. We are also an international leader in research, with world first breakthroughs for over 100 years. We run one of the largest early clinical trial units in Europe with over 300 trials every year. Cancer research in Manchester, most of which is undertaken on the Christie site, has been officially ranked the best in the UK.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking an enthusiastic and dedicated GP to work alongside our clinical team to play an important role complementing and enhancing the Rise Park Surgery Team. This is a 4-6 session a week role; days of work by negotiation. We are open from 0700h on Wednesdays and Thursdays and every fourth Saturday morning and you may be required to cover these sessions occasionally.

We have recently undertaken an extension of our building and we are now looking for a like-minded team member to help us care for our patients. Successful applicants will be working in a brand-new clinical space which has been constructed and modified to our requirements.

We welcome applications from both experienced and newly qualified/early career GPs. We would support the successful applicant wishing to join the Phoenix program or who are on the GP retainer scheme.

Annual leave entitlement will be 30 days plus statutory bank holidays and 5 days study leave (pro rata). Additionally, your medical defence indemnity expenses will be covered by the practice for work undertaken at Rise Park Surgery.

Closing date for applications is 22 November 2026 however we reserve the right to close early if we receive sufficient applications for the role. Therefore if you are interested please submit your application as early as possible.

Please email your application (covering letter and CV) to David Marks at nnicb-nn.c84129.nhs.net.

The post holder will work as an autonomous practitioner, responsible for the provision of medical services to the practice population and delivering an excellent standard of clinical care (including being the duty doctor on call) whilst complying with the GMS contract.

Furthermore, the post holder will adhere to the GMC standards for good medical practice, contributing to the effective management of the practice, leading by example, maintaining a positive, collaborative working relationship with the multidisciplinary team.

Rise Park Surgery is a vibrant, forward thinking, team orientated Nottingham City General Practice serving 9700 patients. We have a great work ethic; caring for our patients, our community and the team around us is paramount to all that we do.

We are currently looking to add to our multi-disciplinary clinical team which is made up of GP Partners, Salaried GPs, Pharmacist, Advanced Clinical Practitioner, Practice Nurses, Healthcare Assistants, Prescribing Technicians and Phlebotomists. We also have a wide range of ARRS staff working with us at Rise Park Surgery including First Contact Practitioners, Social Prescriber, Health & Wellbeing Coach, Dementia Nurse and a Mental Health Worker.

Rise Park Surgery is also a training practice welcoming GP Registrars and Senior and Junior Primary Care Students. We are also a research accredited practice and encourage our clinicians to get involved.

The clinical team are supported by an excellent, friendly, proactive and efficient admin team. There is a full program of educational meetings and support and mentorship is available.

We hold a CQC 'Good' rating, we use 'systmone' and we are a leading practice within the Bulwell and Top Valley PCN.

We would welcome informal visits or a telephone call by prior arrangement.

employer: Kettering General Hospital NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant in Intensive Care Medicine and Anaesthesia
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking an enthusiastic and experienced Consultant in Intensive Care and Anaesthesia to join the expanding team at Kettering General Hospital, part of University Hospitals of Northamptonshire (UHN). This is an exciting opportunity to work within a modern 16-bed Intensive Care Unit, with planned expansion to 20 beds, alongside a broad and varied anaesthetic service. The successful candidate will provide consultant-led critical care and anaesthesia, contributing to the delivery of high-quality, safe and compassionate care across the hospital. The role offers an attractive balance between Intensive Care and Theatres, with opportunities to develop specialist interests and contribute to teaching, research, quality improvement and service development.

The post-holder will provide daytime consultant cover within Intensive Care, including leading multidisciplinary ward rounds, supervising resident doctors and supporting the management of complex critically ill patients. They will also undertake general anaesthesia across a broad range of surgical specialties and participate in the 1:10 Intensive Care on-call rota, supported by resident ICU doctors and established outreach services. The successful candidate will contribute to undergraduate and postgraduate teaching, clinical governance, audit, research and quality improvement, as well as supporting the continued development of the critical care and peri-operative services. This is an excellent opportunity to play an active role in shaping the future of the service as UHN progresses with critical care expansion, digital transformation and the HIP2 new hospital development.

University Hospitals of Northamptonshire (UHN) brings together Kettering General Hospital and Northampton General Hospital in a collaborative Group Model, providing opportunities to work across a progressive and developing organisation. We are committed to delivering safe, compassionate and clinically excellent care while creating an environment where our people can thrive, develop and make a difference.

Our Dedicated to Excellence values are at the heart of everything we do:

Compassion | Respect | Integrity | Courageous | Accountable

We are proud to offer a supportive and inclusive working environment, with excellent opportunities for teaching, research, professional development and service innovation. Joining UHN means becoming part of a forward-looking organisation with strong academic links, including our partnership with the University of Leicester, and an exciting future ahead as we develop our services and prepare for the HIP2 new hospital build.

title: GP for Maternity Cover
descriptionHtml:
Shefford Health Centre is situated within easy reach of Bedford, Hitchin and Luton, while offering the benefits of a pleasant market-town setting surrounded by beautiful Bedfordshire countryside, including the nearby Pegsdon Hills.

The practice also benefits from convenient access to the M1 and A1(M), with excellent transport links providing easy access to the wider region and London.

Our practice serves a growing patient population of approximately 20,500 patients, and we are committed to maintaining high-quality, patient-centred care while continually developing our services.

We are seeking an enthusiastic, committed and forward-thinking Fixed term contract GP to for maternity cover. The role is for 6 sessions per week, worked across Monday, Wednesday and Thursday. This contract to start at the end of March beginning of April 2027

Clinical consultations assess, diagnose, treat and manage patients presenting with acute, chronic and complex conditions, through face-to-face, telephone, video and online consultations.

Prescribing and medication management prescribe safely, review medication, monitor high-risk medicines and respond to medication-related queries.

Long-term condition management contribute to the management of diabetes, hypertension, cardiovascular disease, respiratory disease, mental health and other chronic conditions.

Investigations and results request appropriate blood tests, imaging and other investigations; review results; take appropriate action; and communicate outcomes to patients.

Referrals make appropriate referrals to secondary care, community services and other healthcare professionals, including urgent suspected-cancer pathways where indicated.

  • Clinical correspondence
  • Urgent and same-day care
  • Home visits
  • Clinical documentation
  • Safeguarding
  • Preventive medicine
  • QOF and contractual work
  • Clinical administration
  • Clinical governance Team working
  • Meetings and development
  • Professional responsibilities

Shefford Health Centre is a modern, purpose-built GP practice located on the edge of the historic market town of Shefford in Central Bedfordshire.

We are a friendly, high-performing and progressive GP training practice, with a strong emphasis on education, professional development and collaborative working. We are also the lead practice for our PCN, providing opportunities to work closely with a broad multidisciplinary team.

Our clinical team includes:

  • 5 GP Partners & 6 Salaried GPs
  • Paramedic support
  • 4 Practice Nurses

  • Clinical Pharmacists
  • Dedicated Medicines Management Team

We utilise Rapid Health's AI-supported triage system to help manage demand effectively and support our clinicians in delivering safe and efficient patient care.

title: Forensic Consultant Psychiatrist
descriptionHtml: Are you an experienced psychiatrist ready to lead forensic mental health services? If so join Aberbeeg Hospital as a Forensic Consultant Psychiatrist to provide strategic leadership, expert clinical oversight and recovery-focused care for people within the criminal justice system. Acting as Responsible Clinician under the Mental Health Act, you will ensure the highest standards of psychiatric care across medium and low secure services. In this role, you will lead the clinical management of a defined caseload, overseeing psychiatric assessments, formulations, and treatment planning. You will provide specialist advice to courts, probation, prison services and MAPPA, and prepare reports for Mental Health Review Tribunals, hospital managers hearings, and the Ministry of Justice. Working closely with multidisciplinary teamsincluding forensic social workers, psychologists, and occupational therapistsyou will ensure coordinated care and effective implementation of the Care Programme Approach. Beyond clinical leadership, you will play a key role in service development, shaping strategy, and contributing to pathway reconfiguration to meet evolving needs. You will actively participate in clinical governance, audits, and risk management prAs a Forensic Consultant Psychiatrist at Elysium Healthcare, you are expected to provide strategic leadership and expert clinical oversight for forensic mental health services at Aberbeeg Hospital. Your role focuses on managing a defined caseload and ensuring top-tier psychiatric care under the Mental Health Act's provisions for medium and low secure services. The position requires specialist advice to courts, probation services, and other stakeholders, while managing multidisciplinary teams that include forensic social workers and psychologists. The role extends beyond clinical duties to include essential service development, pathway reconfiguration, and ensuring compliance with CQC/HIW standards. A vital responsibility is the supervision of trainees and junior medical staff, plus leading research and quality-improvement projects. Candidates must have considerable postgraduate psychiatric experience, a strong knowledge of MHA/MCA, and proven leadership in multidisciplinary teams to guide and innovate across services. employer: Northern Care Alliance NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Hepatologist
descriptionHtml:
Our thriving and dynamic Gastroenterology department is based at Oldham, Fairfield and Rochdale, and is part of the Northern Care Alliance NHS Foundation Trust (NCA).

This is a unique and exciting time to join an NHS service that is focused on delivering the best healthcare services to our local population, demonstrated by recent investment in an award winning Community Diagnostic Centre in Oldham (CDC), away from the acute site.

This state of the art modular build has PET-CT (to be upgraded to one of the first digital PET CT scanners in the country), MR, CT, Ultrasound and physiological testing. It has been the focus of national attention, visited by the Prime Minister, Professor Sir Mike Richards & the National Clinical Director for Elective care. It recently won two HSJ Partnership awards and has featured in National news articles about diagnostics.

In Autumn 2024 the CDC will be enhanced further by a co located 3 room endoscopy unit with clinical rooms and on site decontamination. Our ambition at the CDC is to transform the way that we traditionally deliver healthcare and to explore new and innovative delivery models that reflect the needs of both our staff and our patients. There cannot be a better time to join our team.

We have an award winning Tertiary Inflammatory Bowel Disease Centre, led by Professor J.K.Limdi, recognised nationally and internationally for clinical services and research.

Team members have the opportunity to influence the development of services.

This subspecialty post is focused on expanding our dedicated Hepatology service line. The post holder will lead clinical governance for advanced liver diseases, drive the institutional expansion of non-invasive liver fibrosis screening, and manage specialized Liver MDTs and rapid hot clinic models.

The post holder will complement and develop existing services through the provision of specialist knowledge & expertise in Hepatology and General Internal Medicine. The post holder is therefore required to have full registration with the General Medical Council & a valid licence to practice and be on the specialist register (Gastroenterology and preferably also General Internal Medicine) or be within 6 months of CCT or equivalent at the time of interview.

Alongside the CDC, there are 3 endoscopy units across Oldham, Fairfield & Rochdale sites, making this one of the largest endoscopy services in the country. The Endoscopy service offers NHS Bowel Cancer screening colonoscopy, ERCP, HPB, EUS, advanced Lower GI EMR/ ESD.

The non elective inpatient services are centralised on The Royal Oldham Hospital site, the gastroenterology team provide gastroenterology in reach and outpatients at the 3 sites. There is an excellent, long established GI physiology department.

The Northern Care Alliance NHS Foundation Trust (NCA) provides hospital and integrated health and social care services to over one million people living across Greater Manchester. Our 20,000 colleagues care for people in hospital and in the community, working across Bury, Rochdale, Oldham, and Salford, to save and improve lives.As a large NHS trust we are committed to enhancing the health of our local population by delivering consistently high standards of care and collaborating closely with local authorities and key partners. We believe in our power and potential to make a difference and we are always looking for people who demonstrate our three core values - care, appreciate and inspire - to join our team.In return, we can offer you a job role with purpose and flexibility. The size and scale of the NCA means we can provide more challenge and opportunities so your career can always be moving in the right direction. By joining us you can also access a competitive benefits package, including, a fantastic annual leave allowance, flexible working opportunities and protected hours for health and wellbeing activities, helping you to achieve more personal downtime and a better work-life balance.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for a Salaried GP to join our friendly and supportive team at Walnut Tree Health Centre, working 4 to 8 sessions per week.

We are a growing three-Partner practice serving approximately 15,000 patients, with a strong focus on teamwork, mutual support and excellent patient care.

You will work alongside our GP team, experienced nursing and paramedic teams, and our wider Primary Care Network (PCN) team, including physiotherapists, mental health practitioners, social prescribers and clinical pharmacists.

We are looking for a GP who enjoys collaborative working and values being part of a supportive team. You will contribute to shared GP administrative responsibilities alongside your clinical work, with duties shared across the team.

We can offer:

  • 4 to 8 sessions per week
  • A friendly, supportive three-Partner practice
  • Approximately 15,000 patients and a growing list
  • Strong multidisciplinary team working
  • Experienced nursing and paramedic support
  • Access to a wide range of PCN professionals
  • Shared GP administrative responsibilities
  • Opportunities to contribute to practice development
  • A positive and welcoming working environment

We value our staff and encourage colleagues to share ideas, develop their skills and support one another. If you are looking for a practice where teamwork and high-quality, patient-centred care are valued, we would be pleased to hear from you.

The successful candidate will work as a Salaried GP for 4 to 8 sessions per week, providing high-quality, safe and effective medical care to our registered patients. You will work as part of our wider clinical team, making effective use of skills and expertise across the practice and PCN.

Main duties include:

  • Conducting face-to-face and telephone consultations.
  • Assessing, diagnosing and managing acute and chronic conditions.
  • Providing treatment, advice, safety-netting and follow-up.
  • Managing long-term conditions and contributing to preventative care.
  • Making appropriate referrals to secondary, community and primary care services.
  • Working collaboratively with GPs, nurses, paramedics, pharmacists and the wider MDT.
  • Supporting continuity of care and communication across the clinical team.
  • Reviewing investigations and taking appropriate clinical action.
  • Completing clinical correspondence and administrative work.
  • Contributing to shared GP administrative responsibilities, including prescription tasks.
  • Participating in practice meetings and service development.
  • Maintaining accurate clinical records and working within relevant guidelines.
  • Contributing to clinical governance, quality improvement and practice development.
  • Supporting a positive, respectful and collaborative working environment.

We are looking for a GP who communicates well, works effectively as part of a team and is willing to share the day-to-day clinical and administrative responsibilities of general practice.

Walnut Tree Health Centre is a well-established, supportive GP practice serving approximately 15,000 patients, with a growing list. We are a three-Partner practice committed to high-quality, patient-centred care and a positive working environment.

We work as a multidisciplinary team, with GPs, experienced nursing and paramedic teams, supported by our Ascent Primary Care Network (PCN). Our wider MDT includes physiotherapists, mental health practitioners, social prescribers and clinical pharmacists, enabling patients to access a broad range of expertise within primary care.

We are also a training practice, regularly supporting GP Registrars, F2 doctors on rotation and trainee nurses. We value the contribution trainees make and are committed to creating a positive learning environment where colleagues share knowledge, support developing clinicians and help bring the next generation of healthcare professionals into primary care.

We believe learning works both ways, encouraging all team members to share knowledge, reflect and continue developing their skills.

Teamwork is central to our practice. We encourage colleagues to share ideas, support one another and contribute to practice development. GP administrative responsibilities are shared across the team to support a fair and collaborative approach.

We are continually looking to improve our services, make best use of our multidisciplinary team and provide an excellent experience for both patients and staff.

employer: James Paget University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
title: Clinical Fellow in Paediatrics ST3
descriptionHtml:
Applications are invited for clinical fellow (middle grade) level jobs in the department of Paediatrics at James Paget University Hospitals NHS trust. This is a fixed term post (until August 2027) to meet the RCPCH standards for Paediatric middle grade rota. Applicants with experience in general paediatrics/Neonates and specialty paediatrics who wish to consolidate or gain experience in general paediatrics are encouraged to apply.

Applicants will be supported in gathering the experience and portfolio evidence needed to support their applications to the GMC for portfolio pathway (previously CESR), or to add to their existing training experience".

We are a friendly, motivated and flexible team and we would expect our new colleague to have similar qualities.

The department currently operates a Full Shift rota for the middle grade doctors. Current rota is 1 in 9. With this appointment the middle grade (registrar) rota will be 1 in 10. This rota will be reviewed following the success of recruitment into the new posts.

The Specialty Doctor will take part in the Middle Grade Rota which is a full shift system. He/she will:

o Be responsible for Paediatric and Neonatal admissions and ward care, as per the duty roster.

o Undertake ward rounds independently but with consultant supervision.

o Attend consultant ward rounds as appropriate.

o Participate in Paediatric clinics

The James Paget University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (JPUH) provides medical services for a population of approximately 230,000 living in South East Norfolk and North East Suffolk, plus a large number of visitors to the coast and Broads National Park during the summer months. In addition, it provides approximately a third of the secondary care teaching for the UEA Norwich Medical School. The Trust has foundation status and is highly regarded within the region.

The Trust is an equal opportunities employer and operates a no smoking policy.

The Hospital is situated in a mainly rural area in one of the most open, picturesque, safe and unspoilt parts of the country, offering a range of inexpensive properties, good schools, easy access to the coast and an abundance of outdoor, sporting and recreational activities. The post will appeal to candidates who seek a high quality of life combined with a practical clinical role within a secure and well-run hospital distinguished by its supportive and friendly culture.

title: Theatre Runner
descriptionHtml:
We have an exciting opportunity to join our purpose-built eye health clinic and surgical centre in Teesside as a Theatre Runner.

Theatre Runners are an integral part of our theatre team and will undertake a variety of duties. You will be assisting in setting up the theatre ready to accommodate patients. We can typically see 25 patients per list in our high-volume cataract provision, along with other ophthalmology specialities. Therefore you will thrive working in an efficient and fast paced environment.

  • Managing the relationship with the patient and the provision of appropriate information to them, ensuring that exceptional patient care is delivered.
  • To assist in the preparation of theatre equipment and instrumentation prior to a surgical list commencing.
  • Assist the team in positioning the patient for surgery and moving equipment.
  • To assist the scrub nurse and surgeon in theatre.
  • Attend and participate in team meetings, briefing and debriefing as required.
  • To assist with the administrative function of the surgical team, includng the accurate documentation of records.
  • To carry out theatre preparation of patient documentation.
  • To assist in stock checks, including expiry dates and restocking the clinical area.
  • Maintain patient confidentiality at all times.

Newmedica are one of the leading providers of NHS ophthalmology services in England, providing outpatients appointments, diagnostic testing and eye surgery. We aim to change lives through better sight and eye health.

We care for thousands of NHS and private patients a year in our specialist eye clinics across the country.

We are thrilled to say that, following an independently conducted survey of Newmedica colleagues, we have been certified as a Great Place to Work for the fourth-year running. This feedback has directly contributed to Newmedica being listed among the UKs top 50 Best Workplaces for 2026.

Please note, Teesside Newmedica Ltd do not hold a Sponsorship Licence.

title: Locum Consultant Histopathologist
descriptionHtml:
Gloucestershire Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is seeking to appoint a 12-month 10PA fixed term Consultant Histopathologist for maternity cover. The core service requirement for this post is diagnostic expertise in gastrointestinal pathology, and we particularly welcome applicants able to support these high-volume and clinically critical services. Experience in other subspecialties and non-gynaecological cytology is welcome.

The gynaecological pathology service is based at Cheltenham General Hospital and supports a large and well-established clinical service. This includes secondary and tertiary gynaecological cancer services to a population of approximately 1.4 million, covering Herefordshire, Powys and Worcestershire, as well as diagnostic, unit-level and tertiary management for the local Gloucestershire population of 652,000. The post therefore offers an opportunity to work within a busy, regionally significant service with strong MDT engagement.

The successful applicant will join a supportive, UKAS-accredited Cellular Pathology Department with established digital pathology since 2025.

The successful candidate will:

  • Provide high-quality diagnostic reporting, with a core contribution to gastrointestinal pathology, supporting both local and regional cancer services.
  • Support additional subspecialty areas aligned with experience and departmental need, including dermatopathology, urological, lung, GI or head & neck pathology and non-gynaecological cytology.
  • Participate in cut-up, supported by experienced dissection practitioners.
  • Attend and contribute to MDT meetings, including regional and tertiary gynaecological cancer MDTs as appropriate.
  • Take part in the department's longstanding second-signing process for quality assurance.
  • Use the digital pathology service fully.
  • Contribute to service development, audit and clinical governance in line with Trust policies.

Gloucestershire Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is the largest provider within the SWAG Cancer Alliance and delivers high-quality emergency, elective and specialist care across a wide range of services. The Cellular Pathology Department is based at Cheltenham General Hospital and supports both local and regional specialist clinical services, including tertiary gynaecological oncology.

Cheltenham is consistently rated as one of the best places to live in the UK, offering excellent schools, a vibrant cultural scene, green spaces and easy access to the Cotswolds.

The department has a strong culture of subspecialisation, a fully implemented digital pathology service, and an expanding Molecular Pathology Service, supporting modern diagnostics and flexible working.

employer: Mid and South Essex NHS Foundation Trust
title: Clinical Fellow (ST2) - Paediatrics
descriptionHtml:
Clinical Fellow (ST2) - Paediatrics (Fixed Term, 12 Months)

Are you considering a career in Paediatrics and looking for an excellent opportunity to gain valuable experience within a supportive and dynamic team? The Paediatric Department at Basildon Hospital, Mid and South Essex NHS Foundation Trust, is seeking enthusiastic Clinical Fellows (ST2 level) to join our team on a full-time, fixed-term basis to cover a 12-month maternity leave period.

Working alongside a dedicated team of consultants, specialty trainees, Foundation Year doctors and GP trainees, you will gain broad exposure to both acute and general paediatrics while delivering high-quality care to children and their families. Your clinical duties will be undertaken under the supervision of experienced consultants who hold overall responsibility for patient care.

We are committed to supporting your professional development. You will benefit from a structured educational programme, dedicated one-to-one supervision from an Educational Supervisor, and support to undertake and successfully complete MRCPCH examinations.

If you are a motivated and compassionate doctor with a passion for children's healthcare, we would love to hear from you. Join us and build your paediatric experience within a friendly, encouraging and forward-thinking department.

Provide assessment, diagnosis and ongoing management of children and young people across the Children's Ward, Paediatric Assessment Unit and Paediatric Emergency Department, including participation in emergency and resuscitation scenarios.

Deliver care within the Neonatal Unit, including the Level 2 Neonatal Intensive Care Unit, Labour Ward and Postnatal Ward, supporting the stabilisation and management of premature and unwell newborn infants.

Undertake newborn resuscitation and initial management of common neonatal conditions with appropriate senior support and supervision.

Assess and manage paediatric patients in outpatient clinics under the supervision and guidance of a Consultant Paediatrician.

Participate actively in the department's teaching programme, providing education and support to junior doctors, medical students and nursing staff through bedside teaching and formal presentations.

Engage in simulation training, supervised learning events (SLEs), departmental meetings, clinical audit and quality improvement activities to support professional development and service excellence.

Contribute to the assessment and management of safeguarding concerns, working closely with Consultant colleagues and multidisciplinary teams to ensure the safety and wellbeing of children and young people.

Work collaboratively with Consultants, Middle Grade Doctors, Nurses, Community Teams and other multidisciplinary colleagues.

Our ambition is to deliver excellent local and specialist services, to improve the health and wellbeing of our patients, and provide a vibrant place for staff to develop, innovate and build careers.

We aim to make the most of our skills and experiences so we can become the best we can be. As one organisation we will recruit the finest and retain more specialist staff due to more employment opportunities across our Trust.

employer: Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Radiologist with an Interest in Cardiothoracic Imaging
descriptionHtml:
Applications are invited for the above post at Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust. The post holder will provide imaging support for cardiothoracic patients and have on call and cross-sectional imaging responsibility for the Trust.

We are looking for enthusiastic Radiologists to join the team of cardiothoracic radiologists working cross site at any OUH site to provide imaging services to Oxfordshire and support the on-call service. The Trust is a cancer centre with a large oncology unit, a major trauma centre, a cardiothoracic surgical centre and a tertiary referral centre for interstitial lung disease and pleural disease.

The post holder will be part of the cardiothoracic radiology team and deliver imaging, intervention and biopsy services across the Trust. Additional subspecialty interests may be accommodated/supported e.g. in oncological imaging.

The Trust has installed Insignia PACS and has image sharing agreements in place with regional hospitals, to support multidisciplinary team meetings and allow access to comparative images across the region.

Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is one of the largest NHS teaching trusts in the country. It provides a wide range of general and specialist clinical services and is a base for medical education, training and research. Find out more here www.ouh.nhs.ukThe Trust comprises four hospitals - the John Radcliffe Hospital, Churchill Hospital and Nuffield Orthopaedic Centre in Headington and the Horton General Hospital in Banbury.Our values, standards and behaviours define the quality of clinical care we offer and the professional relationships we make with our patients, colleagues and the wider community. We call this Delivering Compassionate Excellence and its focus is on our values of compassion, respect, learning, delivery, improvement and excellence. These values put patients at the heart of what we do and underpin the quality healthcare we would like for ourselves or a member of our family. employer: Birmingham Women's and Children's NHS Foundation Trust
title: Locum Consultant Paediatrician
descriptionHtml:
This is an exciting opportunity to join the specialist Paediatric Palliative Care Teamand play a key role in the development of paediatric palliative and end-of-life care services across Birmingham and the West Midlands. The post combines direct clinical care for babies, children and young people with life-limiting conditions with the opportunity to support service development across the Shropshire, Telford and Wrekin (STW) footprint.

Working alongside an experienced multidisciplinary team of consultants, specialist nurses and family support staff, the post holder will contribute to the delivery of high-quality symptom management, advance care planning and holistic family-centred care across hospital and community settings.

This is a 5 PA locum consultant post offering a unique opportunity for an established paediatrician with an interest in palliative care to further develop specialist knowledge and skills within an accredited training centre. Depending on experience, there may be opportunities to work towards paediatric palliative medicine SPIN competencies under consultant supervision.

Applicants must hold full GMC registration with a licence to practise and demonstrate the skills and experience required to work at consultant level within paediatrics.

The successful candidate will provide specialist paediatric palliative care for babies, children and young people with life-limiting conditions across Birmingham Women's and Children's NHS Foundation Trust and the wider West Midlands. Working alongside the existing consultant and specialist nursing team, the post holder will support children with malignant and non-malignant conditions across both hospital and community settings.

The role includes delivering expert symptom management, advance care planning and end-of-life care, whilst working closely with multidisciplinary teams, community services, hospices and other partner organisations. The post holder will also contribute to service development, education and the ongoing delivery of high-quality specialist paediatric palliative care across the region.

More information included within the JD.

Birmingham Women's and Children's NHS Foundation Trust is the first of its type in the UK. Our Trust was formed in February 2017 to drive forward our commitment to provide the highest quality, world-class physical and mental health care for our women, children and families. Uniting our hospitals means more seamless care; more investment to make greater advances in our specialist treatment and world-leading neo-natal and fetal work. Importantly, it also gives us a greater voice in shaping the future of family-centred care.

Birmingham Children's Hospital is a UK leading specialist paediatric centre with an international reputation in several areas.

Birmingham Women's Hospital is one of two dedicated women's hospitals in the UK, with the busiest single site maternity unit, delivering more than 8,200 babies a year offering a full range of gynaecological, maternity and neonatal care.

Our Trust is committed to creating the best place to work. We believe in promoting and enhancing inclusion, diversity and equality and encourage applications from all areas of the community, who meet the criteria for the role, regardless of age, gender identity, disability, race, religion or sexual orientation.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for a colleague to join our Practice Team, making a difference to patients in Letchworth.

  • You will be registered with GMC and engaged in regular clinical work.
  • Be an experienced doctor with GP accreditation
  • Hold MRCGP examination or equivalent experience
  • Have a sound knowledge of the principles and values that support good medical practice
  • We operate a Total Triage model of working, so experience in this would be an advantage.
  • Have good organisational skills
  • Have excellent interpersonal skills and be committed to working as part of a team
  • Have a clear commitment to delivering quality and patient focused service
  • Have a record of continuous professional development
  • You will provide clinical care to patients, this will include consultation sessions, telephone triage, econsults, correspondence, results, medication reviews and prescription signing and other clinical administration, medicals, reports, home visits, surgery meetings and on-call (excluding out of hours).
  • Adhere to the highest personal and professional standards as set out by the GMC and to put individual patient care as your priority.
  • Provide support, on a rota basis, as the Triage Clinician for total triage way of working
  • Work with the Directors and Practice Manager to support the development, delivery and review of the agreed surgery action plan may include list growth, patient satisfaction levels, QOF, enhanced services, safeguarding of patients, KPI targets, CQC, PNC DES activities, resources and profile and cost management.
  • Provide colleague clinical support to your peer GPs, nurses, HCAs, trainees and other healthcare colleagues.
  • Work closely with the Practice primary health care team in delivering clinical care.
  • Actively participate in regular clinical Practice meetings.
  • Ensure on going CPD to keep abreast of new clinical developments.
  • Document and report significant events and matters relating to clinical governance to the Practice Manager.
  • The Birchwood and Sollershott Surgery is one practice based over two sites. We are an accredited education practice, which supports ST2/ST3s.
  • With a patient list of approx 18,500 and growing, we are a busy and lively practice.
  • We operate a Total Triage model of working, with a clinical triage team supporting the triage for patient enquiries.

  • Our multi-disciplinary clinical team is made up of GPs, Paramedic, ANPs, prescribing nurses, Practice Nurses and Health Care Assistants.
  • We operate in a supportive PCN area, with support from Clinical Pharmacists, Pharmacy Technicians, First Contact Physio, Midwifery, Phlebotomy, Mental Health Nurse, Social Prescribers and Enhanced Access Service.

title: Consultant Clinical Oncologist
descriptionHtml:
The Worcestershire Oncology Centre, located at the heart of the Worcestershire Royal Hospital, is a premier facility dedicated to providing exceptional cancer care to approximately 600000 people of Worcestershire and surrounding areas. Since its opening in 2014, our centre has been at the forefront of delivering comprehensive oncology services, combining advanced medical technology with a compassionate, patient-centred approach. Our mission is to offer the highest standard of care to our patients through innovative treatments, cutting-edge research, and a commitment to continuous improvement. We strive to deliver personalized care that meets the unique needs of each patient, ensuring the best possible outcomes and enhancing quality of life.

Please note that we are currently still pending Royal Collage approval for this JD.

We have a face to face AAC booked for the 15th December 2026 with a required 5 minute presentation title of "What are the biggest challenges facing modern radiotherapy today and the future vision for the radiotherapy service"

We currently have financial approval for 2 WTE positions are are currently seeking approval for a 3rd post at 0.8WTE

This Consultant Clinical Oncologist position is pivotal in supporting and expanding our oncology services, particularly in the fields of outpatient care and chemotherapy. As part of our dynamic team, you will be based primarily at the Worcestershire Oncology Centre in Worcester, with the opportunity to engage in visiting sessions at either the Kidderminster Treatment Centre or the Alexandra Hospital in Redditch, once a week. This role involves working alongside a dedicated team of 17 consultant oncologists (comprising 12 clinical and 5medical oncologists), with plans for further expansion over the next few years.

8.0 PAs on average per week (includes clinical activity, clinically related activity, predictable & unpredictable emergency work). Within 8 PAs for DCC, 1.5-2PA for radiotherapy planning and peer review will be included (proportionate to workload and split between radiotherapy and SACT activity). Cross-site travel and clinical administration time is included in each session of DCC.

Supporting Professional Activities (SPA):

2.0 SPAs per week to support your personal CPD and revalidation related activities.

Worcestershire Acute Hospitals NHS Trust is a large acute and specialised hospital trust that provides a range of local acute services to the residents of Worcestershire and more specialised services to a larger population in Herefordshire and beyond.

The Trust operates hospital-based services from three sites in Kidderminster, Redditch and Worcester

Our workforce is more than 7,000 strong, and our caring staff are recognised as providing good and outstanding patient-centred care. You could be one of them.

We are committed to recruiting the best people to work with us. Our values, which we ask all staff to demonstrate, underpin our everyday work and remain firmly at the heart of all we do.

Being open and honest

Ensuring people feel cared for

Showing respect to everyone

We are committed to developing a culture of continuous improvement by embedding the principles of our Improvement System.

We are proud to have achieved Timewise accreditation - this means we are committed to embedding flexible working within our organisation as a flex positive employer.

DBS Checks and Costs

Any applicants who are offered posts requiring a DBS check as part of their employment check will have the cost of this check (at the current rate) deducted from their salary. Please see link in Supporting Information section for more details on DBS checks and costs.

employer: Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Gynaecologist with interest in Early Pregnancy/Acute Gynae
descriptionHtml:
Applications are invited to apply for the above post in the Gynaecology Department at the Oxford University Hospitals NHS Trust. The department is seeking a capable and motivated doctor who enjoys working in a tertiary referral service and wishes to effect change and improve care for patients within this service

The postholder will join an existing team of 18 NHS gynaecologists who together provide both a local gynaecology service to the population of Oxford and a highly specialist tertiary service in urogynaecology, reproductive medicine, endometriosis and Gynae-oncology. This post is a Trust wide position and may involve clinical sessions at the Horton Hospital in Banbury and the John Radcliffe Hospital sites, as well as the community based Early Pregnancy Assessment Unit (EPAU) in Rosehill, Oxford.

The aim of this post is to better align capacity with demand in general gynaecology and to provide additional consultant capacity in the urgent care service as well as high quality gynaecological ultrasound. The post also offers general and specialist clinics, and regular operating lists. Applications from candidates willing to participate in the termination service will be particularly welcome.

Oxford University Hospitals NHS Trust provides gynaecology services across three sites (John Radcliffe Hospital Oxford, Horton Hospital Banbury and the Churchill Hospital, Oxford). The successful applicant will work across all sites. The post holder will be expected to undertake a combination of general gynaecology and specialist clinics. It is anticipated that the specialist clinics will be undertaken in Rosehill Early Pregnancy Assessment Unit

The post-holder will be expected to undertake theatre lists (the majority of the surgery undertaken is minimal access) at the John Radcliffe hospital.

The post holder will manage in-patients at the John Radcliffe Hospital and undertake gynaecology on-call duties of no more frequent than 1:10 paid at a Band A supplement. Competency should be maintained in diagnostic laparoscopy, management of miscarriage and ectopic for out of hours work.

Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is one of the largest NHS teaching trusts in the country. It provides a wide range of general and specialist clinical services and is a base for medical education, training and research. The Trust comprises four hospitals - the John Radcliffe Hospital, Churchill Hospital and Nuffield Orthopaedic Centre in Headington and the Horton General Hospital in Banbury.

title: Consultant Foot & Ankle Orthopaedic Surgeon (Sheffield)
descriptionHtml:
One Health is looking for a fellowship-trained Orthopaedic Consultant with a sub-specialty in Foot & Ankle to support and grow the One Health Groups Orthopaedic Team.

The successful candidate will have experience working within a similar role in a private or NHS setting. You should have a professional outlook, empathetic telephone manner and understand the importance of patient confidentiality.

  • You should currently be in a substantive NHS post OR in a long-term locum post (more than 12 months)
  • If not in current NHS post, should have been a substantive NHS consultant for at least 3 years before leaving the NHS
  • On GMC register and have no hearings or restrictions

This role will involve assessing and operating on NHS patients referred to One Health, via the NHS e-Referral System. Appointments will be held across a number of outreach clinic sites, including West Yorkshire, South Yorkshire and Leicestershire. One Health was established in Sheffield in 2004 and has successfully grown to become a significant healthcare provider in the region. Our services are available to NHS and private patients, with clinics located at over 30 locations across Yorkshire, Derbyshire, Nottinghamshire and Lincolnshire. Our Head Office is based in Sheffield but will require the successful candidate to work from various locations remotely.

We have a dedicated Patient Liaison Team offering high-quality administration support, coupled with advanced technology which allows for us to offer a modern, paperless and secure service. One Health brings healthcare closer to where people live by offering outpatient facilities over a wide geographical area. We are committed to clinical excellence and our mission to provide innovative, high quality medical and clinical services for NHS patients, optimising outcomes so they can quickly continue healthy lives.

Benefits of working with OHG are:

  • Flexible working options
  • Use of latest technology

  • NHSLA for all NHS work undertaken for the Group

title: Consultant Haematologist
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking a dedicated and enthusiastic Consultant Haematologist to join our dynamic team. This is a full-time position although applicants interested in part-time work are also encouraged to apply. The successful candidate will contribute to the provision of clinical and laboratory haematology services for the Worcestershire population, which numbers approximately 550,000.

The Trust encompasses three principal hospital sites throughout the county: Worcestershire Royal Hospital in Worcester, Alexandra Hospital in Redditch, and Kidderminster Treatment Centre. The Consultant will be primarily based at Worcestershire Royal Hospital with responsibilities that include delivering clinical and laboratory haematology services at this location and conducting outreach clinics at one of our peripheral sites.

The Haematology Department is actively engaged in clinical research and is recognised as a major recruiting centre for Haematological NCRI Trials.

There is significant scope for the successful applicant to develop a specialist interest should they wish, supported by research links with the University of Birmingham and the University of Worcester.

As part of the Consultant Advisory Appointment Committee, shortlisted candidates will be asked to provide a 5 minute presentation on the topic: The current challenges facing a Haematology DGH and the way forward

Interview Date: Tuesday 15th December 2026

Please contact Dr Nick Pemberton for further information npemberton@nhs.net

Our Haematology Consultants collaborate closely to provide a BCSH Level 2b/3 inpatient Clinical Haematology service to both Worcestershire and Herefordshire patients. Services are delivered from a busy, 18-bed ward at Worcestershire Royal Hospital, which also offers shared care for autologous stem cell transplantation in partnership with University Hospitals Birmingham.

We are actively involved in the West Midlands Specialist Registrar Training Scheme and participate in weekly joint multidisciplinary team (MDT) meetings, which serve patients from both Worcestershire and Herefordshire. These meetings are regularly attended by specialist Haematopathologists, Radiologists, and Oncologists, ensuring comprehensive patient care.

The Worcestershire Oncology Centre, a Cancer Centre operational for the past five years, is staffed by a full complement of Clinical and Medical Oncologists.

Worcestershire Acute Hospitals NHS Trust is a large acute and specialised hospital trust that provides a range of local acute services to the residents of Worcestershire and more specialised services to a larger population in Herefordshire and beyond.

The Trust operates hospital-based services from three sites in Kidderminster, Redditch and Worcester

Our workforce is more than 7,000 strong, and our caring staff are recognised as providing good and outstanding patient-centred care. You could be one of them.

We are committed to recruiting the best people to work with us. Our values, which we ask all staff to demonstrate, underpin our everyday work and remain firmly at the heart of all we do.

Being open and honest

Showing respect to everyone

title: Salaried GP, 6 sessions, 12 month fixed term
descriptionHtml:
The Ridgeway Surgery in Harrow is seeking a salaried GP for six sessions per week on a 12-month fixed-term contract.

The sessions are required on a Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

Join a multidisciplinary team where you can contribute to patient care and help shape how we deliver our services. We are a training practice, rated Good in all areas by the CQC, with a strong focus on collaborative working, digital transformation and improving access for patients.

You will work alongside GP partners, salaried GPs, advanced clinical practitioners, pharmacists, nurses and our wider care team. This is an opportunity to bring your experience and ideas to a practice actively developing its services.

The appointment is fixed term while we review our longer-term clinical staffing needs in light of anticipated neighbourhood service developments, premises plans and our financial position. This review will inform whether future provision involves salaried GP role or a different level of clinical capacity. Extension or a permanent salaried appointment cannot be guaranteed.

We welcome applications from GPs who enjoy working collaboratively and want to contribute to the next stage of our practices development.

You will provide high-quality general medical care across six sessions per week, working on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays. These working days are required to meet the practices clinical cover needs.

Your work will include face-to-face, telephone and online consultations, managing acute presentations and ongoing conditions, alongside prevention and health promotion.

You will undertake the clinical administration associated with patient care, including reviewing results and correspondence, prescribing and making referrals, supported by our multidisciplinary team.

You will work collaboratively with colleagues to ensure safe, coordinated care, contributing to clinical discussions, safeguarding and quality improvement. We welcome your ideas for improving services and making effective use of digital tools.

The role will include home visits where clinically appropriate and opportunities to contribute to teaching and supervision, according to your experience and interests.

The Ridgeway Surgery is a GP training practice in Harrow, providing care from our main surgery and our branch at Alexandra Avenue Health and Social Care Centre. We were rated Good in all areas by the CQC in 2026.

Our multidisciplinary team includes GP partners, salaried GPs, advanced clinical practitioners, clinical pharmacists, nurses, healthcare assistants and care navigators, supported by our administrative and management teams.

We value collaborative working, clear communication and a practical approach to solving problems. Colleagues bring different skills and perspectives, helping us provide coordinated care and respond to the needs of our patients.

We are actively developing our services, with a focus on access, long-term condition management and effective use of digital tools. As a training practice, we also support learning and the development of future healthcare professionals.

Joining us offers the opportunity to contribute your ideas, work alongside an experienced team and help shape the practices next stage of development.

title: Senior Locally Employed Doctor in Ophthalmology - Glaucoma
descriptionHtml:
Applications are invited for three twelve months fellowship posts in Glaucoma in one of the largest ophthalmic units in the UK. There are three posts, to commence from 1st week of August 2027.

Candidates that are non-GMC registered at the point of application will be considered for this position, under the Trusts International Fellowship Scheme (please note, there is a £750 admin charge for this scheme). More information re this scheme can be found on our website - link in job description.

Manchester Royal Eye Hospital (MREH) is a major tertiary referral centre with complex glaucoma cases being received from across the North West, from North Wales and beyond. It is also one of only a handful of centres in the UK offering a dedicated paediatric glaucoma service. MREH glaucoma unit has a National and International reputation for leading the way in adopting new glaucoma surgical techniques including MIGS and has an active clinical research portfolio in the diagnosis and management of glaucoma. We have led the way in the development of new and innovative Glaucoma Service Delivery Models, including first Glaucoma Referral Refinement Scheme in the UK, an in-house optometric led glaucoma assessment clinic, virtual clinics and Nurse-led Patient Education Clinic and the first Home-day phasing Service.

The Glaucoma Unit consists of 5 full time consultants: Mr L Au, Mr J Yu, Mr K Yau, Miss F Tacea and Miss F Mason.

These fellowship posts offer wide clinical experience in the management of glaucoma including both complex adult and paediatric cases. The fellows will also gain insight into the service delivery of glaucoma through our innovative optometric schemes and virtual clinics. Laser and Surgical training include SLT, YAG, Argon and diode (external and endoscopic) laser therapies, enhanced trabeculectomy, angle surgery, minimally invasive glaucoma surgery and glaucoma drainage devices on both adult and paediatric cases.

The Fellow will participate in outpatient clinics undertaking diagnosis, management and follow up of patients under the care of the Consultants. He or she will undertake surgery both under supervision and, where appropriate, unsupervised. The Fellow attends outpatient clinic sessions and dedicated operating sessions under the direction of the Consultant trainers. In addition, they will perform a laser session per week. They will provide urgent glaucoma opinions for tertiary and internal referrals with the support of the supervising consultants.

Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust (MFT) is a leading centre of clinical excellence, renowned for pioneering patient care, advanced medical research, and a collaborative multi-speciality environment. We are the largest provider of specialist services, and our Oxford Road Campus in Manchester is the largest health academic campus in Europe - a great place to progress your career.

With over 30,000 employees, a turnover exceeding £3 billion, and 10 hospital and community services, join our team to help us deliver outstanding healthcare to our diverse communities.We offer an engaging and supportive environment, with access to state-of-the-art facilities and cutting-edge technology. Research and Innovation are at the heart of our work, offering opportunities to lead research that shapes the future of medicine, working alongside experts, advancing clinical practice, and improving patient outcomes.At MFT, we foster a culture where every colleague is valued and empowered to thrive. Your expertise is recognised, your ambitions are supported, and your impact is felt at every level. Whether you want to develop your clinical skills, pursue research interests, or seek leadership opportunities, MFT provides the ideal environment to achieve your medical or professional aspirations.If you are dedicated to driving clinical innovation and delivering compassionate patient care, join us to shape tomorrow's healthcare; where clinical excellence, innovation, and your career will thrive.

title: Integrated Care Team GP
descriptionHtml:
