employer: Practice Plus Group - Health in Justice
title: General Practitioner
descriptionHtml:
UNLOCK YOUR BEST WORK LIFE

+ MAKE A DIFFERENCE TO EVERY LIFE

We have an exciting opportunity for a General Practitioner to join our Primary Care team.HMP Brixton has recently transitioned from Cat C training prison to Category B Remand Prison. The site is based close to Brixton underground station with good access via public transport. Within this role you will work closely with the multidisciplinary team, gaining insight to Mental Health and Substance Misuse. As part of your role you'll attend the weekly MDT meetings, complete patients reviews and support individuals undergoing detoxification.

Hours

Wednesday: 08:00 - 12:00

This position is part time working 4 hours per week per week.

Salary

You'll receive an annual salary up to £129,500 FTE - depending on experience.

How will we support you?

  • Bespoke induction, including our Introducing Health in Justice training course
  • Competency framework
  • Regional and national career development opportunities
  • Our bespoke Learning Management System to address your learning needs
  • Support from the wider team

Candidates are required to have a Legal right to work in the UK and due to the nature of the role, offers of employment will be subject to additional vetting and security checks.

Our General Practitioners are extremely valued and are well respected members of the Prison Healthcare community, as a General Practitioner, your responsibilities will vary. You will

  • Deliver first class healthcare to a diverse group of patients, and therefore as a General Practitioner at Practice Plus Group you get the opportunity to further develop your knowledge in areas you wouldn't usually experience within a practice, or even A&E environment.
  • Provide clinical assessment and diagnosis to patients requirements and make timely decisions regarding future management.
  • Provide a highly specialist resource to other members of the healthcare team at site, as well as the patients you work with having active
  • involvement in clinical governance and effectiveness activities.
If you are interested in career development, we have a wide range of opportunities for you to develop your skills and experience, which include both internal and external options for development and learning.

It doesn't stop there we also offer:

  • Discounts on shopping and leisure activities
  • Support to grow in your role and continue your professional development
  • 24/7 employee assistance helpline and financial assistance when you need it

The Health in Justice team at Practice Plus Group makes a real difference across over 53 prisons, young offenders and immigration removal centres. Were the UKs leading independent provider of NHS services to over 40,000 patients in secure environments, always putting their needs first, regardless of their background.

Practice Plus Groups purpose is to Unlock your best work life and we stand by our core values:

  • We treat patients and each other as they would like to be treated
  • We act with integrity
  • We embrace diversity
  • We strive to do things better together
We are looking for caring, compassionate but also driven professionals who can help us drive our vision for a fair and inclusive healthcare access to all.

Requirements

  • MBChB or MBBS
  • Inclusion on the GMC Register and GP Performers List
  • Evidence of engagement with annual appraisal
  • Experience working as a General Practitioner in community general practice
  • Evidence of continuing professional development
  • Ability to work with patients with a history of substance misuse
  • RCGP Certificate in Substance Misuse 1 and 2, or prepared to undertake these qualifications
Secure environments are one of the most challenging, yet rewarding places for healthcare professionals to work. If you're looking for a role where you can develop your existing healthcare skills and learn something new every day in an environment that never stands still, then this could be the right opportunity for you.

title: Trust Doctor (eqv to ST3+) In Cardiology
descriptionHtml:
This is an exciting opportunity to join Barts Health NHS Trust and work within a modern Community Diagnostic Centre that delivers high-quality cardiovascular diagnostics and outpatient services closer to patients' homes. The role is focused on echocardiography and community cardiology, providing extensive exposure to the assessment and management of patients with suspected or established cardiovascular disease.

The post holder will be based predominantly within the Community Diagnostic Centre (CDC) at Mile End Hospital, providing high-quality echocardiography and specialist cardiology services to support the diagnosis, assessment and management of patients with suspected or established cardiovascular disease.

Clinical Responsibilities

o Perform and report transthoracic echocardiograms (TTE) to a high standard, undertaking comprehensive assessment of cardiac structure and function in accordance with departmental and national guidelines.o Assess patients referred to community cardiology services with symptoms of undifferentiated breathlessness, integrating clinical findings with echocardiographic and other diagnostic investigations to support diagnosis and management planning.o Participate in community-based murmur clinics, evaluating patients with suspected valvular heart disease and contributing to appropriate investigation, diagnosis and follow-up pathways.o Support valve disease assessment services, including the surveillance and longitudinal follow-up of patients with known valvular heart disease, ensuring timely referral for specialist review where indicated.

Barts Health is one of the largest NHS trusts in the country, and one of Britain's leading healthcare providers.

Our vision is to be a high-performing group of NHS hospitals, renowned for excellence and innovation, and providing safe and compassionate care to our patients in east London and beyond. That means being a provider of excellent patient safety, known for delivering consistently high standards of harm-free care and always caring for patients in the right place at the right time. It also means being an outstanding place to work, in which our WeCare values and behaviours are visible to all and guide us in how we work together.

We strive to live by our WeCare values and are committed to promoting inclusion, where every staff member has a sense of belonging. We value our differences and fully advocate, cultivate and support an inclusive working environment.

title: Specialty Doctor in Palliative Medicine
descriptionHtml:

Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust (MFT) is a leading centre of clinical excellence, renowned for pioneering patient care, advanced medical research, and a collaborative multi-speciality environment. With over 30,000 employees, a turnover exceeding £3 billion, and 10 hospital and community services, join our team to help us deliver outstanding healthcare to our diverse communities.We offer an engaging and supportive environment, with access to state-of-the-art facilities and cutting-edge technology. Research and Innovation are at the heart of our work, offering opportunities to lead research that shapes the future of medicine, working alongside experts, advancing clinical practice, and improving patient outcomes.

At MFT, we foster a culture where every colleague is valued and empowered to thrive. Your expertise is recognised, your ambitions are supported, and your impact is felt at every level. If you are dedicated to driving clinical innovation and delivering compassionate patient care, join us to shape tomorrow's healthcare; where clinical excellence, innovation, and your career will thrive.

title: Consultant in Nuclear Medicine & Clinical Radiology
descriptionHtml:
Applications are invited for a full time Consultant Radiologist post specialising in NM, PETCT and general radiology, which has arisen from the increasing activity and outstanding unfilled sessions within the department. The post will be based at the Charing Cross, Hammersmith and St Mary's campuses, depending on the needs of the department. The post will include two sessions for SPA.

The mainstay of the post will be reporting activity covering all FDG and non-FDG tracers in use, as well as nuclear medicine studies. The post-holder will be expected to contribute to the Knee MRC MDT, and experience in joint prosthesis work is essential. It is essential the candidate is also able to support the running of the NM department generally, such as taking clinical NM queries from staff, trainees and referrers. The post will include general radiology sessions (up to two sessions), and the successful candidate is expected to support and participate in departmental objectives which includes ultrasound scanning, duty/urgent radiology reporting, weekday evening and weekend support for trainees (including trauma), and may include the provision of extended-day consultant lead reporting and general on-call in the future.

The post will be based at the Charing Cross, Hammersmith and St Mary's campuses, but may change in view of the Trust site and clinical strategy reviews which are on-going. The post holder will also be expected to play an active role in trainee supervision - as a clinical or educational supervisor - and teaching as well as close liaison with clinical staff, and have ambitions to take on various management roles in the department. Rapid access and scan turnaround times, as well as efficient and safe inpatient and emergency workload, are key priorities for the department as a whole.

At Imperial College Healthcare you can achieve extraordinary things with extraordinary people, working with leading clinicians pushing boundaries in patient care.

employer: Hull University Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust
title: Senior Clinical Fellow ST7+
descriptionHtml:
The successful candidate will assume a direct clinical role within the department, based at Hull University Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust (HUTH) sharing all facilities equally with the existing trainees. This is a 12 months fellowship program. The successful candidate will work full time 40 hours per week, (Flexible working may be considered). It is expected that the successful applicant will play an active role in the 1:11 first on call rota covering Hull University Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust (HUTH).

Oculoplastic surgery training covers a wide range of procedures dealing with the orbit, eyelids, lacrimal system, and the face. Surgical training in a fellowship typically includes:

  • Eyelid surgery -- ptosis repair, entropion/ectropion correction, eyelid reconstruction following tumour excision, and malposition correction
  • Lacrimal surgery -- external DCR (dacryocystorhinostomy) and endonasal (endoscopic) DCR.
  • Orbital surgery -- orbital biopsies, orbital decompression, and management of anterior orbital tumours.
  • MDTs -- Oculoplastics MDTs, skin cancer MDTs, and joint lists.

The Humber Health Partnership is one of the largest acute and community Partnership arrangements in the NHS, seeing well over one million patients every year and managing a budget of over £1.3 billion.

Made up of two Trusts - Northern Lincolnshire and Goole NHS Foundation Trust (NLAG) and Hull University Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust (HUTH) - our Partnership has significant ambitions and is committed to delivering world-class hospital and community services for the 1.65 million people we serve.

Together we employ nearly 20,000 staff. Our five main hospital sites are Diana, Princess of Wales Hospital, Scunthorpe General Hospital and Goole and District Hospital, for NLAG and Hull Royal Infirmary and Castle Hill Hospital for HUTH.

As Teaching Hospitals working with the Hull York Medical School, we both lead and contribute to research in many areas - biomedical research, primary care, palliative medicine, cardiovascular and respiratory medicine, vascular surgery, cancer surgery and oncology.

We believe that by developing a diverse, inclusive, innovative, skilled and caring workforce, we can deliver excellent care to our patients and a great future for our employees, our Partnership and our community.

descriptionHtml:
Applications are invited for the post of Clinical Fellow Higher (ST3-5) in Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery (0.4WTE) at Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust. This role functions at the Specialist Registrar (StR) level and is based within our busy regional department.

Applications from job seekers who require skilled worker sponsorship to work in the UK are welcome and will be considered alongside all other applications. For further information please visit the UK Visas and Immigration website.

It is a requirement for skilled worker applicants, applying for entry clearance into the UK, to present a criminal record certificate from each country they have resided continuously or cumulatively for 12 months or more in the past 10 years. descriptionHtml:
We welcome rehabilitation medicine specialists/consultants to join our team for an 8 PA post.

This post is one of four new Consultant Trauma & Orthopaedic posts, alongside Orthopaedic Spine, Shoulder & Elbow (with an interest in Upper Limb Trauma) and Children's Orthopaedics.

MKUH is a University Teaching Hospital in partnership with the University of Buckingham, with undergraduate teaching delivered through the Buckingham and Oxford medical schools.

title: Salaried GP (3 to 6 sessions) at Hilary Cottage Surgery in Fairford
descriptionHtml:
If youre an enthusiastic GP looking for a rewarding new role in a progressive, friendly practice, we'd love you to join us at Hilary Cottage Surgery in Fairford, near Cirencester, Gloucestershire.

Hilary Cottage Surgery is a thriving, semi-rural training and dispensing practice situated in the Cotswolds, offering primary care to around 7600 patients.

We are seeking a salaried GP who values patient-centred care, teamwork, and the opportunity to contribute to excellent clinical care.

We have three GP Partners and four Salaried GPs working collaboratively within a close-knit, supportive, clinical team, and we are now recruiting for up to 8 extra sessions for one or two GPs.

This is a rare opportunity to take on a GP role at Hilary Cottage. Situated in a beautiful, semi-rural location, this could be your rewarding next step whatever the stage you are at in your GP career.

We can offer the right candidate(s) up to 6 clinical sessions, and we are interested in meeting you if you see yourself working any number of sessions from 3 up to 6 (possibly more) per week.

Please contact the team for an informal chat or send us your CV and a covering letter. We look forward to hearing from you

Hilary Cottage Surgery runs a Total Triage service with Accurx, and we use SystmOne clinical system. We are a training practice with 7 GPs, including 2 GP trainers, plus 1-2 trainees.

We are part of the South Cotswolds PCN and are based in Fairford. There are three GP Partners and four Salaried GPs combining to create a cohesive, encouraging and friendly team.

Most importantly, Hilary Cottage Surgery is a nice place to work, with a great team of GPs, nurses, pharmacist, paramedic/ANPs, phlebotomists, managers, receptionists, pharmacy technicians, HCAs, administrators and dispensers. There's about 40 of us, most of whom work part time, and we have carefully fostered and grown a working environment that cares for the team and is a nice (and even fun) place to work.

Situated in a town within a wider rural setting, this opportunity could be your rewarding next step whatever the stage you are at in your GP career.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:

We welcome newly qualified GPs and experienced clinicians equally, what matters more than years of experience is the right values and appetite for the role.

As well as routine and on-the-day clinical work, the role includes duty and triage sessions, long-term condition management, and participation in journal clubs, clinical meetings, and GSF. Home visits are shared equitably and supported by our in-hours visiting service. Administrative workload is fully supported.

About Dolphin House Surgery

employer: The Hillingdon Hospital NHS Foundation Trust
title: Dermatologist Consultant (8PAs)
descriptionHtml:
The post-holder will play a key role in realising our ambition to continue to build a high quality clinical Dermatology and Allergy service. The successful applicant will be a committed clinician with specialist training in Dermatology and a commitment to excellent clinical service delivery, service improvement, teaching, training and other qualities as identified in the person specification. It is a requirement of the post that every doctor takes part in annual job planning and annual appraisal as part of the revalidation of cycle. Job planning is outlined in point 4 as is a draft proposed job plan.

The post-holder will be responsible to the Divisional Director of planned care at The Hillingdon Hospital and job plan negotiated annually. It is a 8 PA post -6.5 direct clinical care (DCC), 1.5 supporting professional activities (SPA), the latter includes clinical and educational supervision, audit and personal CPD. Personal CPD must be included as part of annual appraisal which is mandatory and required for the revalidation process.

The post holder will, together with his or her consultant colleagues and other health care professionals in the Directorate, provide an effective and comprehensive service for patients and support continuing service developments.

The post holder will be encouraged to develop any areas of expertise of special interest that he or she may have in accordance with the service needs of the department.

The Hillingdon Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is the only acute Hospital in the London Borough of Hillingdon and offers a wide range of services including accident and emergency, inpatient care, day surgery, outpatient clinics and maternity services. The Trust's services at Mount Vernon Hospital include routine day surgery, delivered at a modern treatment centre, a minor injuries unit and outpatient clinics.

The safety and well-being of our patients and of our staff is paramount and we are making urgent improvements to address this - particularly in infection prevention and control. We are making progress and going forward by working in partnership with local GPs, charities,community services, academic partners, our local authority, neighbouring hospitals and the wider North West London Integrated care system, and ensuring that we listen and work in partnership with our local population. We are absolutely focused on ensuring that our hospitalsprovide high quality, safe and compassionate care, while drive forward the building of the new Hillingdon Hospital.

We have over 3,500 members of staff that are proud to care for nearly half a million people, with a vision to be an outstanding provider of healthcare through leading health and academic partnerships, transforming services, to provide the best care where needed.

title: Locum Consultant Ophthalmologist- Spec interest in Glaucoma
descriptionHtml:

In this role, you will contribute to delivering exceptional Ophthalmology services across Imperial college healthcare NHS trust.

title: Senior Trust Grade in Anaesthesia
descriptionHtml:
Join us for a career and portfolio boosting opportunity

The benefit of the department's strong training, University, Trent Simulation Centre and

employer: Great Ormond Street Hospital for Children NHS Foundation Trust
title: Trust Doctor in Paediatric Cardiology
descriptionHtml:
Trust Doctor SHO in Paediatric Cardiology

Great Ormond Street Hospital invites applicants of ST 2-3 level equivalent for 6-month post in paediatric cardiology. The post would be well-suited - but not limited - to junior doctors-in-training wanting to have a period of out-of-programme experience. It may be possible to count this placement towards your training, dependent on the completion of Level 1 curriculum competencies.

Your main role would be to cover a busy general cardiology ward and cardiology day ward. During your time, you would also be encouraged to attend all areas of the unit, including cardiac theatres, the catheter laboratory and echo department. There is a formal teaching programme specifically for SHOs, as well as registrar teaching within the department. There are also several courses available, which may be prioritised and subsidised for GOS staff (including the echo and morphology courses). It is possible for a dedicated trainee to learn the basics of clinical echo during these placements. The position would undoubtedly be useful in preparation for an application to paediatric cardiology training at ST4.

Applicants must be registered with the GMC or eligible for registration.

We would encourage any junior doctor considering a career in paediatric Cardiology, or becoming a general paediatrician with an interest in Cardiology to contact Dr Craig Laurence craig.laurence@gosh.nhs.uk

Scope of the role

The main role would be to cover a busy general cardiology ward and cardiology day ward. title: Consultant Neurologist Locum interest in Movement Disorder/Epilepsy
descriptionHtml:

employer: South Tyneside and Sunderland NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Haematologist
descriptionHtml:
This new Consultant Haematologist post will work across the North East Central Alliance, a new, formal strategic partnership between County Durham and Darlington NHS Foundation Trust (CDDFT) and South Tyneside and Sunderland NHS Foundation Trust (STSFT).

The STSFT haematology service already provide the haematology service at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital Gateshead. The appointment will contribute to the delivery and development of clinical and laboratory haematology services across the three trusts, serving a combined population of 1.3 million.

This is an exciting opportunity to join a dynamic team as the services come together to undertake a programme of sustained team expansion and service re-development. The detailed job description and job plan will be agreed with the successful candidate, taking account of their preferences, experience and subspecialty interests alongside the needs of the service. The post offers scope to develop a specialist interest and contribute to shared pathways, teaching, research and service improvement

The clinical haematology service is based at Sunderland Royal Hospital (SRH), with sessions at South Tyneside Hospital, Queen Elizabeth II Hospital Gateshead and University Hospital of North Durham (UHND). An agreed job plan will complement the post holders sub-specialty interests and include some clinical sessions at UHND.

The role comprises:

  • A 1-in-10 attending week, providing Level 3 inpatient haematology care at SRH, managing two-week-wait referrals, liaison work and laboratory reporting.
  • A 1-in-10 non-resident overnight on-call commitment, providing advice across STSFT, QE and CDDFT.
  • Two adult haematology clinics per week during non-attending weeks across sites, covering haemato-oncology, haemostasis and thrombosis, and general haematology.
  • Reviewing day-unit patients across sites.
  • Prescribing inpatient and outpatient chemotherapy.
  • Providing advice and guidance to GPs.
  • Reporting bone marrow biopsies.
  • Attending the weekly Consultant Grand Round at SRH and weekly MDT, with rotating involvement in the bone marrow morphology MDT.

Although full time, applications from candidates wishing to work less than full time are encouraged.

Applicants must hold MRCP and FRCPath, be on the GMC Specialist Register with a licence to practise and, if UK-trained, hold a Certificate of Completion of Training (CCT). Further details are provided in the job description.

Please add your telephone number to your application form so we can contact you quickly if required.

One Team One Trust - There are many reasons to work at our Trust. From our commitment to putting people first to our accessible services and award winning teams. We have a passion for research, innovation and tackling inequalities. We welcome all applications irrespective of peoples race, disability, gender, sexual orientation, religion/belief, age, gender identity, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy/maternity and in particular those from under- represented groups. Flexible working is supported via our Flexible Working Policy.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
An exciting opportunity has arisen for a motivated, compassionate and patient focused GP to join our dynamic team for four to six sessions per week.

We are looking for a GP who shares our commitment to providing high quality, holistic and patient centred care and who will enjoy working as part of our supportive multi disciplinary team.

The successful candidate will provide the full range of general practice care, including acute consultations, management of long term conditions, review and actioning of results, occasional home visits and participation in our planned care home ward rounds, providing proactive and coordinated clinical care to residents.

The successful candidate will be joining an established multi disciplinary team and will have opportunities to contribute to clinical governance, quality improvement, shared learning and the ongoing development of our services.

Our vision is to be an approachable, compassionate team delivering high standards of holistic, patient centred care in a respectful and inclusive way. We are looking for someone whose approach to both patients and colleagues reflects these principles.

The successful candidate will provide high quality, safe and effective clinical care to our patients, including consultations, examinations, diagnosis, treatment, follow up and appropriate referral.

They will manage acute presentations and long term conditions, developing personalised care plans and supporting patients to make informed decisions about their health.

The role will include occasional home visits, alongside participation in a regular care home ward round, working collaboratively with the wider multidisciplinary team to provide proactive, person centred care to residents. This will include clinical review, management of acute and long term conditions, medication review where appropriate, advance care planning and coordination with care home staff and other health and care professionals.

The postholder will review and action investigations, correspondence and results in a timely manner, undertake appropriate prescribing and medicines management, and maintain accurate and contemporaneous clinical records.

As a member of the clinical team, the postholder will participate in practice meetings, clinical governance, audit, significant- event learning and quality improvement activity.

They will maintain appropriate continuing professional development and participate fully in appraisal, revalidation and other professional requirements.

Huntcliff Surgery is a well-established, patient-focused GP practice at the heart of the Saltburn-by-the-sea community, caring for 10,000 patients.

Our vision is to be an approachable, compassionate team delivering high standards of holistic, patient centred care in a respectful and inclusive way.

Our values underpin how we care for our patients, how we work with one another and how we develop our services:

  • Compassion - treating patients and colleagues with kindness, understanding and empathy.
  • Person Centred Care - recognising each patient as an individual and involving them in decisions about their care.
  • High Standards - taking pride in providing safe, effective and consistently high-quality care.
  • Respectful - treating everyone fairly, professionally and with dignity.
  • Approachable & Welcoming - creating an environment in which patients and colleagues feel comfortable, listened to and supported.
Our clinical team currently includes 3 GP Partners, salaried GPs, Nurse Practitioners, a GP Assistant, Senior Health Care Assistant and Phlebotomist, supported by a pharmacist, pharmacy technician and dedicated prescribing and administration teams.

We also benefit from a strong wider workforce, including ARRS colleagues such as First Contact MSK Practitioner, Mental Health Practitioners and Social Prescriber, alongside our management and administrative teams.

We welcome applications from GPs who share our values and would like to contribute to the continuing development of Huntcliff Surgery.

title: Head of School for Radiology - Wsx
descriptionHtml:

The Head of School will focus upon improvement of learner supervision, assessment and experience, engagement of faculty and ensuring effective educational outcomes, both now and in the future. The role is evolving and will also focus on whole workforce transformation and developing multi-professional links mas well as innovative ways of curriculum delivery and workforce well-being strategies.

The Head of School will be expected to meet the challenges of leading the School and Education Providers to deliver the changing curricular in an evolving service landscape.

To support the Postgraduate Dean, Heads of School work across the spectrum of health and where relevant, social care, within the context of a team, so that the provision of education reflects changing service models. This will deliver an integrated workforce comprising individuals from a spectrum of professional and other backgrounds.

NHS England has a wide range of statutory functions, responsibilities and regulatory powers. These are focused on supporting the wider NHS to deliver high quality care, as well as doing those things that are best done once for the whole NHS.

Our staff bring expertise across clinical, operational, commissioning, technology, data science, cyber security, software engineering, education, and commercial specialisms -- enabling us to design and deliver high-quality NHS services.

In March 2025, the Government announced that NHS England and the Department of Health and Social Care will increasingly merge functions, ultimately leading to NHS England being fully integrated into the department.

If you currently work within the NHS and if successful at interview, we will initiate an Inter Authority Transfer (IAT) via the Electronic Staff Record (ESR).This retrieves key data from your current or previous NHS employer to support onboarding, including competency status, Continuous Service Dates (CSD), and annual leave entitlement. You may opt out at any stage of the process.

Colleagues with a contractual office base are expected to spend, on average, at least 40% of their time working in our offices.

We cannot offer visa sponsorship for any vacancies.

title: Consultant Psychiatrist - Deal Community
descriptionHtml:
Are you passionate about making a real impact on the lives of people with mental health needs?

As a Consultant Psychiatrist at Kent and Medway Mental Health NHS Trust, you'll lead a collaborative team and provide high-quality care to the vibrant communities of Deal and its surrounding villages.

This is a community-based post where you will work flexibly and collaboratively with two other consultants in the South Kent Coast Community Mental Health Teams. Please note, we also have vacancies based in Dover and Folkestone. Please apply for each vacancy you are interested in.

Successful applicants will ideally have MRCPsych or equivalent and be on, or within six months of inclusion on, the Specialist Register. You will be fully registered with the GMC, and have Approved Clinician status and S12 approval under the Mental Health Act (or achieve this within 3 months of appointment).

  • To provide clinical leadership within the South Kent Coastal Community Mental Health Team alongside two other Consultant colleagues.
  • The provide medical input as required to patients under care of the Community Mental Health Team
  • To be actively involved in strengthening relationships with external agencies including the local CCG.
  • To take an active leadership role in screening of referrals as well as assessment of new referrals jointly with other team members

We are Kent and Medway Mental Health NHS Trust. We care for the mental health and wellbeing of people across Kent and Medway and are rated 'Good' by the Care Quality Commission (CQC).

Our teams support children, young people and adults with a wide range of mental health needs. We also provide specialist services, including all-age eating disorder services and neurodevelopmental assessments for children and young people, such as autism and ADHD.

Because we work across the whole county and across hospital and community settings, we can make care more joined up and easier to access for the people we serve.

Our vision is simple: we are here to help communities not just live with mental illness, but live well. It's why we're passionate about working with communities to make mental health care better for everyone. Everything we do is guided by our values: caring, inclusive, curious and confident.

Join us if you share our passion for better mental health care and want to be part of a team that's working well together.

title: Consultant Anaesthetist: NHS Elective Surgery Hub
descriptionHtml:
One Health is seeking a highly motivated and experienced Consultant Anaesthetist to join our surgical team at the One Health Elective Surgery Hub, North Lincolnshire.

This is an exciting opportunity to become part of an established and expanding independent healthcare provider delivering high-quality elective surgical services for NHS patients. The successful candidate will play a key role in providing expert anaesthetic care, supporting service development, and ensuring the delivery of outstanding patient outcomes within a dedicated elective surgery environment.

This is a full-time employed position, working Monday to Friday, based primarily at:

One Health Elective Surgery Hub North Lincolnshire

Warren Road

SCUNTHORPE

DN15 6XH

Salary will be in line with the NHS Consultant pay scale, depending on experience.

Applicants should be experienced substantive NHS Consultants, be included on the GMC Specialist Register, and hold unrestricted GMC registration and licence to practise.

The role will involve providing comprehensive anaesthetic services for NHS patients referred to One Health.

Key responsibilities include:

Providing high-quality anaesthetic care for elective surgical patients.

Undertaking pre-operative assessment, optimisation and perioperative management.

Supporting post-operative recovery and pain management.

Working collaboratively with surgeons and multidisciplinary teams to deliver safe, effective patient care.

Maintaining accurate clinical records and complying with clinical governance and regulatory requirements.

The One Health Elective Surgery Hub North Lincolnshire is One Health's first dedicated elective surgery hub, developed to provide high-quality surgical care within a state-of-the-art facility, supporting timely access to treatment and excellent patient experiences.

title: Consultant Neurophysiologist

title: Locum Paediatric Consultant Anaesthetist
descriptionHtml:
We are looking to welcome a consultant anaesthetist to primarily work within our Southwest Peninsular Children's Surgical Unit and be on the paediatric on call rota, but be willing and able to flex to cover work within our adult theatre complex. The job plan will incorporate, on average, one session in adult theatres per week to maintain skill, subject to mutual agreement.

We are the largest hospital in the Southwest Peninsula, and offer a secondary care service to approximately 500 000 patients, and a tertiary care service to a further 1.5 million. We are a major trauma centre. Almost all adult surgical specialties are catered for, including cardiac, neurosurgery, thoracics and paediatrics. A successful applicant will be joining a welcoming and friendly department that has held ACSA Accreditation since 2015 and is proud of its collegiate spirit. We have a strong track record in clinical excellence & translational research, and receive very positive feedback from our rotating trainees. We understand the need to accommodate a healthy work life balance and aim to support flexible working. We have a lively social programme and a dedicated anaesthetic coffee room, known as the 'Back Bar'.

We are located on the Devon/Cornwall border with access to all the amenities of a metropolitan city, yet moments away from the moors and sea. We are proud that Plymouth was voted the top city to live in England in 2023!

This post is for a substantive Consultant Anaesthetist capable of delivering high-quality anaesthesia across all major paediatric surgical specialties. In addition to clinical duties, responsibilities will include teaching, continuing medical education, and participation in quality improvement activities.

The post holder will be expected to participate in the paediatric on-call rota. There are separate on-call rotas for adult general surgery/neurosurgery and obstetrics, as well as adult ICU and cardiac services.

As a busy and expanding Trust, the role will also involve some weekend elective, emergency, and trauma anaesthetic cover. An appropriate allocation of programmed activities will be agreed to reflect these duties. We are committed to flexibility and strongly support a healthy work-life balance, welcoming applications from candidates seeking less than full-time work.

The enclosed job plan is indicative and may be subject to change following ongoing service developments, with the aim of meeting both the needs of the service and the professional interests of the post holder.

We are a people business - where every member of staff matters and can make a difference. Patients are at the heart of everything we do. Joining University Hospitals Plymouth NHS Trust means becoming part of a team of dedicated staff, who are committed to leading the way through innovation, clinical excellence and great customer care. The Trust has great opportunities for career development in a highly progressive working environment. We offer all of this in a vibrant, modern city with a historic reputation for adventure. title: Consultant Psychiatrist - Salisbury Community CAMHS
descriptionHtml:
We are recruiting for a full-time Consultant Psychiatrist to join Salisbury Community CAMHS and work with a well-established multi-disciplinary team at Salisbury District hospital.

You'll provide psychiatric clinical input and leadership within a recently redesigned service delivering targeted mental health care to children and young people with severe and enduring mental health needs through our Getting More Helppathway.

You'll work in partnership within the multidisciplinary team for the clinical management of patients. This will include risk assessment, the assessment of the needs of carers, and the development of services to meet the needs of patients and families for whom the team is responsible.

You'll work 10 programmed activities with a job plan typically comprising 75% direct clinical care and 25% supporting professional activities, in line with Royal College of Psychiatrists' guidance. Opportunities are available to develop interests in service development, quality improvement, and teaching and training within a well-established, supportive multidisciplinary team and consultant peer group.

Join us in shaping brighter futures for children and young people at one of the UK's leading mental health Trusts; we would be delighted to hear from you.

  • Provide clinical leadership and medical input to the team
  • Responsibility for those patients you see yourself, together with those patients seen by medical staff directly supervised by you
  • With other consultants in the team, have responsibility for the clinical governance of the team as clinical leads for the team
  • The team will assess all emergencies referred to it within a day of referral. When necessary, this will include responsibility for Mental Health Act assessment of patients. The Consultant is not expected to make initial assessments, except in certain circumstances. The Consultant psychiatrists will work in partnership within the multidisciplinary team for the clinical management of patients in relation to the Trust Key working model. This will include risk assessment, the assessment of the needs of carers, and the development of services to meet the needs of patients and families for whom the team is responsible.
  • Be a clinical leaders in your team and ensure excellent systems of clinical governance so that their team provides high quality, safe care to patients. Consultants are expected to encourage a Restorative Just and Learning Culture of Learning, participate in safety huddles and investigations and participate in identifying improvements in practice where appropriate.

Oxford Health provides physical, mental health and social care for people of all ages across Oxfordshire, Buckinghamshire, Swindon, Wiltshire, Bath and Northeast Somerset. Our services are delivered at community bases, hospitals, clinics and people's homes, delivering care as close to home as possible.

Our vision is that 'our teams support every person to achieve their best quality of life through compassionate and evidence-based care informed by research'.

Our values are to be caring, safe and excellent.

title: Consultant Radiologist
descriptionHtml:
The successful candidate will join a dynamic and forward-thinking radiology department, providing specialist oncological imaging and reporting services to support patients across medical oncology, radiation oncology, haemato-oncology and palliative care. The role offers opportunities to contribute to the reporting and governance of PET/CT and nuclear medicine studies, alongside broader diagnostic radiology practice.

The radiology department at CCC provides a comprehensive oncological imaging service. CCC-Liverpool is equipped with CT, MRI, PET/CT, Ultrasound, Plain Film and Interventional Radiology facilities. The CCC-Wirral site offers general radiology, CT, MRI, Ultrasound, Nuclear Medicine and PET/CT services.

CCC also operates the Paddington Community Diagnostic Centre, providing opportunities to undertake general radiology reporting alongside specialist oncology imaging. Out-of-hours reporting is supported through an independent teleradiology service.

Applicants should hold an ARSAC licence, or demonstrate a commitment to obtaining one, and will be supported in developing their expertise in molecular imaging and oncological PET/CT reporting as part of this role.

The successful candidate will play a key role within the Radiology Department, providing high-quality diagnostic imaging services to support The Clatterbridge Cancer Centre's specialist cancer pathways. Core responsibilities will include reporting cross-sectional imaging examinations, including CT, MRI and PET/CT studies (subject to training and accreditation), participation in multidisciplinary team meetings, protocol development, image vetting, and providing expert radiological advice to clinical colleagues across oncology, haematology and palliative care services.

The post holder will be expected to contribute to service development, quality improvement initiatives, audit, teaching and clinical governance activities, supporting the continued growth and innovation of imaging services across the Trust. There will be opportunities to develop subspecialty interests aligned to departmental and organisational priorities.

The Radiology Department operates across the CCC-Liverpool, CCC-Wirral and Paddington Community Diagnostic Centre sites, providing comprehensive oncological and diagnostic imaging services.

The post is offered on a 10 Programmed Activity job plan (8 DCC, 2 SPA). Direct Clinical Care activities will primarily comprise reporting sessions for oncological and general diagnostic imaging, participation in multidisciplinary team meetings, and associated clinical support activities.

The Clatterbridge Cancer Centre NHS Foundation Trust is one of the UK's leading cancer centres providing highly specialist cancer care to a population of 2.4m people across Cheshire and Merseyside, and the surrounding areas, including North Wales and the Isle of Man.

Our vision is to not only maintain this level of commitment to excellence but to work with our academic and healthcare partners across the region to ensure care, treatment and patient outcomes continuously improve in the future. We are very proud of all our expert and loyal staff and we welcome people who share the collective aim of delivering excellence in everything that we do.

Our values represent who we are and what we believe in. They define how we act to deliver the best possible care for our patients and shape The Clatterbridge Cancer Centre as a great place to work.

We are -

  • Kind
  • Empowered
  • Responsible
  • Inclusive

title: General Practitioner with Special Interest in Gynaecology
descriptionHtml:
General Practitioner with Special Interest in Gynaecology for Primary Care Services (GPwSI)

Available Shifts In Person 4 hours per session:

North Bucks- Winslow Health Centre MK18 3DW

South Bucks- Wye Valley HP11 2TT, The Simpson Centre HP9 1TX

Salary: £73.23 per hour

We are seeking a motivated and passionate General Practitioner with a strong interest in Women's Health to join our dynamic and supportive Community Gynaecology Team.

What We Offer

  • Experienced GPwSI and/or Consultant-Led Support: Benefit from direct training and advice from the start and continuing throughout.
  • Comprehensive Training Portfolio: Dedicated pathways to train you up to competency in advanced procedures such as pessary fittings and cervical polypectomies, as well as removal of lost coils and insertion of difficult coils.
  • Skill Maintenance & Growth: A structured environment designed to help you maintain your existing skills while safely acquiring new clinical knowledge.
  • Collaborative Culture: Join a warm, welcoming, and multidisciplinary team dedicated to transforming women's healthcare delivery.

This is an exciting opportunity for a GP who is looking to develop and expand their expertise in women's health while working alongside experienced GPs with Special Interests (GPwSI) and Consultant Gynaecologists. You will provide high-quality, patient-centred gynaecological care within a community setting, helping to improve access to specialist services and deliver outstanding patient outcomes.

Whether you are already experienced in women's health or are looking to further develop your specialist skills, we offer a structured and supportive environment for professional growth.

Essential Requirements

Candidates must possess the following qualifications and core clinical skills upon appointment:

  • Qualifications: Fully registered General Practitioner with the GMC (or relevant national body) and on the GP Register.
  • Cervical Smear Taker: Certified and up to date with national cervical screening program guidelines.
  • LARC Procedures: Competent and confident in intrauterine system/device (IUCD/IUS) insertion and removal (Coil Fitter & Remover).
  • Clinical Interest: A strong commitment to womens health and a desire to progress within this specialty.
  • Communication: Exceptional interpersonal skills with the ability to provide empathetic, patient-centered care.

About FedBucks

FedBucks is a not-for-profit GP federation of 45 GP practices covering a population of over 550,000 patients across Buckinghamshire. We began in 2016 and now employ around 300 members of staff at our head office site, and across our planned and unplanned care services.

As a GP Federation and Social Enterprise, we are proud to represent our member practices and to champion primary care by working with local general practice and system partners in the provision of community-based healthcare services. We are dedicated to providing safe and compassionate care to our patients across our range of planned and unplanned healthcare services in Buckinghamshire and believe in continuous commitment to quality service delivery and positive patient outcomes.

Patients are at the heart of everything we do, and we pride ourselves in our purpose when enabling excellent patient care and supporting general practice.

The successful applicant will be required to undergo an enhanced background check (e.g., DBS) prior to appointment, and regular safeguarding training will be provided and required.
